ole container.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An application that contains a linked or embedded OLE object from another application. For example, if an OLE object in an Access database contains a Microsoft Excel worksheet, Access is the OLE container.

association.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In PerformancePoint Planning Business Modeler, the relationship between a source model and a destination model for the purpose of manipulating the arrangement of interpretive data and aggregating the corresponding numerical measurements.

quick access toolbar.translation: Thanh công cụ truy nhập nhanh
quick access toolbar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A customizable toolbar that provides one-click access to commands.

local partitioned view.translation: dạng xem phân chia cục bộ
local partitioned view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view that joins horizontally partitioned data from a set of member tables across a single server, making the data appear as if from one table.

drop-down list box.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control on a menu, toolbar, dialog box, or data access page that displays a list of options when you click the small arrow next to the list box.

hardware interface.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A card, plug, or other device that connects pieces of hardware with the computer so that information can be moved from place to place. For example, standardized interfaces such as RS-232-C standard and SCSI enable communications between computers and printers or disks.

model database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu mô hình
model database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database that is installed with Microsoft SQL Server and that provides the template for new user databases. SQL Server creates a database by copying in the contents of the model database and then expanding the new database to the size requested.

reconciliation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An adjustment made to two versions of the same fixed or calculated number when they are not the same.

overtype mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A setting in which existing characters are replaced with newly typed characters.

help.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A capability of many programs and operating systems to display advice or instructions for using their features when so requested by the user, as by a screen button or menu item or a function key.

online help.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A capability of many programs and operating systems to display advice or instructions for using their features when so requested by the user, as by a screen button or menu item or a function key.

data viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical tool that displays data as it moves between two data flow components at run time.

configuration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In reference to a single microcomputer, the sum of a system's internal and external components, including memory, disk drives, keyboard, video, and generally less critical add-on hardware, such as a mouse, modem, or printer. Software (the operating system and various device drivers), the user's choices established through configuration files such as the AUTOEXEC.BAT and CONFIG.SYS files on IBM PCs and compatibles, and sometimes hardware (switches and jumpers) are needed to "configure the configuration" to work correctly. Although system configuration can be changed, as by adding more memory or disk capacity, the basic structure of the system--its architecture--remains the same.

scan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An image-bearing surface such as a single page or multi-page of text or picture that is passed through a scanner and has become a computer file.

memory usage delta.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Task Manager, the change in memory, in kilobytes, used since the last update.

emoticon.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A string of text characters that, when viewed sideways, form a face expressing a particular emotion.

cost line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of a cost template that specifies one or more categories that form the basis of a cost estimate.

fact dimension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard dimension that is constructed based on data from a fact table.

degenerate dimension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard dimension that is constructed based on data from a fact table.

report model.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A metadata description of business data used for creating ad hoc reports.

track.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component of the timeline where editing elements such as videos, images, audio, stickers, text blocks, etc. are placed and arranged to create a video.

audio track.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual song or other discrete piece of audio content.

taskbar button.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A button that represents an item or program that is open and running on your computer. For example, if you open Microsoft Word, and then minimize it, it will be displayed as a taskbar button, which you can then click when you want to maximize it.

mail contact.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mail-enabled Active Directory contact that contains information about people or organizations that exist outside an Exchange Server organization. Each mail contact has an external email address.

pass-through statement.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SELECT statement that is passed directly to the source database without modification or delay.

smallint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data type of 2 bytes (16 bits) that stores whole numbers in the range of -2^15 (-32,768) through 2^15 - 1 (32,767).

debug.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To detect, locate, and correct logical or syntactical errors in a program or malfunctions in hardware. In hardware contexts, the term troubleshoot is the term more often used, especially when the problem is a major one.

soft shadowing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shadowing effect that uses gradation as opposed to a hard outline.

fuzz testing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A testing process that supplies structured but invalid input to software application programming interfaces (APIs) and network interfaces to maximize the likelihood of detecting errors that might lead to software vulnerabilities.

fuzzing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A testing process that supplies structured but invalid input to software application programming interfaces (APIs) and network interfaces to maximize the likelihood of detecting errors that might lead to software vulnerabilities.

software bundler.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that installs other potentially unwanted software, such as adware or spyware. The license agreement of the bundling program may require these other components in order to function.

report project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A template in the report authoring environment.

application role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SQL Server role created to support the security needs of an application.

differential base.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The most recent full backup of all the data in a database or in a subset of the files or filegroups of a database.

authorization store.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file containing user and group information used by the Authorization Manager.

multibase differential.translation: khác biệt từ nhiều cơ sở
multibase differential.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A differential backup that includes files that were last backed up in distinct base backups.

content conversion.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of transforming email messages from one format to another for the purpose of mail flow or storage, such as MAPI to MIME, or uuencode to Base64 encoded, or for appropriate rendering that is specific to an email client, such as HTML to RTF to plain text.

broadband.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A transmission medium designed for high-speed data transfers over long distances. Cable modem services and Digital Subscriber Line (DSL) are examples of broadband networks.

cube role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of users and groups with the same access to a cube. A cube role is created when you assign a database role to a cube, and it applies only to that cube.

windows error reporting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Windows technology that collects data when the system crashes or stops responding and sends it to Microsoft.

wer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Windows technology that collects data when the system crashes or stops responding and sends it to Microsoft.

project task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the tasks that comprise the tasks in a business project.

isometric.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the presets for 3D rotation effects. When selected, specifies that the object will be rotated isometrically.

custom rule.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a role, a specification that limits the dimension members or cube cells that users in the role are permitted to access.

dirty read.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A read that contains uncommitted data.

cached data.translation: dữ liệu đã lưu vào bộ đệm ẩn
cached data.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data stored in a cache.

midpoint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A handle that appears in the middle of a selected line, arc, or other one-dimensional (1-D) shape.

select.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To add a check to a check box to specify a desired feature or option.

toolbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A bundle of software, services, marketing materials, etc., bundled together and meant to be used together.

bid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The maximum amount that an advertiser is willing to pay for a keyword or placement.

shuffle all.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The menu item that allows the play back all of the items in a playlist once, in random order. Playback ends when all of the items in the list have been played one time.

shuffle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To present items within a set in no established order, as opposed to ordering items by name, by date taken, by size, etc., and typically used with audio and visual media, such as album song order or photo slide shows.

scanner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature in Microsoft Purview Information Protection that can automatically label files that have previously been auto-classified with the appropriate classification and sensitivity label.

basic columns.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A grouping of column headings on a report.

lan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network of computers, printers, and other devices located within a relatively limited area (for example, a building). A LAN enables any connected device to interact with any other on the network.

local area network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network of computers, printers, and other devices located within a relatively limited area (for example, a building). A LAN enables any connected device to interact with any other on the network.

company network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network of computers, printers, and other devices located within a relatively limited area (for example, a building). A LAN enables any connected device to interact with any other on the network.

data convergence.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data at the Publisher and the Subscriber that matches.

encrypted trigger.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A trigger that is created with an optional encryption parameter that encrypts the definition text and cannot be decrypted.

integrity rule.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the rules that you set to establish and preserve relationships between tables when you add, change, or delete records.

search.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The UI element that initiates the process of seeking a particular file or specific data. A search is carried out by a program through comparison or calculation to determine whether a match to some pattern exists or whether some other criteria have been met.

network gateway.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that connects networks using different communications protocols so that information can be passed from one to the other. A gateway both transfers information and converts it to a form compatible with the protocols used by the receiving network.

gateway.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Software that facilitates access to data that resides on a private, on-premises network, for subsequent use in a cloud service.

form files.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of files that are used to implement a form. File types can include .html, .xml, .xsd, .xslt, script, and other file types that are necessary to support the functionality of the form.

press and hold.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A gesture represented by placing a finger on the screen and holding it there for a part of a second or more

trust center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A website that describes the compliance, security, and privacy features of Microsoft Office 365.

discount.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A reduction in the selling price of products or services usually offered by the seller when the buyer agrees to meet specific conditions.

breakout room.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shared space where smaller groups of attendees can meet separately.

room.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A physical space where patients receive healthcare treatment.

full-text search.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A search for one or more documents, records, or strings based on all of the actual text data rather than on an index containing a limited set of keywords.

hover.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To move the pointer over a UI element for a specified duration with the intent of interacting with that element.

elapsed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Completed or passed. The measured duration of an event.

hot standby server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standby server that can support rapid failover without a loss of data from committed transactions.

hot standby.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standby server that can support rapid failover without a loss of data from committed transactions.

template part.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A customized set of controls that can be saved for reuse in multiple form templates. Template parts are saved as custom controls in the Controls task pane.

microsoft® office groove® server 2007 da.translation: Microsoft® Office Groove® Server 2007 Data Bridge
microsoft® office groove® server 2007 da.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component of Microsoft Office Groove Server 2007 that enables data integration between Microsoft Office Groove 2007 client-side workspaces and enterprise databases and applications.

sql server profiler.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical user interface for monitoring an instance of the SQL Server Database Engine or an instance of Analysis Services.

microsoft® office professional plus 2007.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A suite of Microsoft productivity software that supports common business tasks, including word processing, email, presentations, and data management and analysis.

mobile phone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A button in the Options dialog box, on the Phones tab, that the user clicks to enter his or her mobile phone number.

nudge.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To send a reminder to a Viva Goals user to make an update.

online archive.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A repository that is separate from the user’s mailbox and that allows items to be archived on the server.

microsoft® office access® 2007.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An edition of a Microsoft relational database management system designed for ease of use.

content source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of options that you can use to specify what type of content is crawled, what URLs to crawl, and how deep and when to crawl.

cgi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server-side interface for initiating software services. For example, a set of interfaces that describe how a Web server communicates with software on the same computer. Any software can be a CGI program if it handles input and output according to the CGI standard.

common gateway interface.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server-side interface for initiating software services. For example, a set of interfaces that describe how a Web server communicates with software on the same computer. Any software can be a CGI program if it handles input and output according to the CGI standard.

application server role.translation: Vai trò Máy chủ Ứng dụng
application server role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A role that consists of the services that provide users access to data and content. To run Microsoft Dynamics CRM, you must have at least one computer that is running the Application Server role.

audio codec.translation: Đối tượng Quản lý Phân tích
audio codec.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The digital encoding used to represent audio data.

row field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field that's assigned a row orientation in a PivotTable report. Items associated with a row field are displayed as row labels.

user-level security.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: When using user-level security in an Access database, a database administrator or an object's owner can grant individual users or groups of users specific permissions to tables, queries, forms, reports, and macros.

criteria pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The area of the window that displays the criteria used to limit the records included in the result set of your query.

action argument.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Additional information required by some macro actions - for example, the object affected by the action or special conditions under which the action is carried out.

plaintext.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data in its unencrypted or decrypted form.

cleartext.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data in its unencrypted or decrypted form.

unbound control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that is not connected to a field in an underlying table, query, or SQL statement. An unbound control is often used to display informational text or decorative pictures.

back payment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A payment made by a customer for a past due obligation.

access mechanism.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In programming, the means by which an application can read from or write to a resource.

access method.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In programming, the means by which an application can read from or write to a resource.

roam.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To move between different environments and have the same user experience in both environments.

hypertext transfer protocol over secure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message transfer protocol used by the World Wide Web to service page requests, and which adds a security layer using Secure Socket Layer (SSL) technology.

https.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message transfer protocol used by the World Wide Web to service page requests, and which adds a security layer using Secure Socket Layer (SSL) technology.

hypertext transfer protocol secure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message transfer protocol used by the World Wide Web to service page requests, and which adds a security layer using Secure Socket Layer (SSL) technology.

subtotal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Math and trigonometry Excel function that returns a subtotal in a list or database.

logical record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A merge replication feature that allows you to define a relationship between related rows in different tables so that the rows are processed as a unit.

page down key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A keyboard key (often labeled "PgDn") that is often used to move the cursor down to the top of the next page or a specific number of lines. Its function may vary in different programs.

answer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To accept an incoming telephone call.

resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity in the Microsoft Graph that can be related to other entities.

workgroup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A privacy relationship setting that allows a large amount of information to be viewed, usually assigned to people on your team.

peer-to-peer network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A distributed network that has no dedicated servers and whose connection is established between different devices where each device can be a client or a server.

3-d walls and floor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The areas surrounding many 3-D chart types that give dimension and boundaries to the chart. Two walls and one floor are displayed within the plot area.

snap-in.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of tool that you can add to a console supported by Microsoft Management Console (MMC). A stand-alone snap-in can be added by itself; an extension snap-in can be added only to extend the function of another snap-in.

declarative referential integrity.translation: tính toàn vẹn tham chiếu khai báo
declarative referential integrity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: FOREIGN KEY constraints defined as part of a table definition that enforce proper relationships between tables.

incoming mail.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message that has been sent across one or more messaging systems. It may have been sent only to you or to many other recipients. Incoming messages are placed in a receive folder designated to hold messages of a particular class. You can set up a different receive folder for each message class that you handle or use one folder for all of the classes.

incoming message.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message that has been sent across one or more messaging systems. It may have been sent only to you or to many other recipients. Incoming messages are placed in a receive folder designated to hold messages of a particular class. You can set up a different receive folder for each message class that you handle or use one folder for all of the classes.

system administrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person responsible for setting up and managing local computers, stand-alone servers, member servers, or domain controllers. An administrator performs such duties as assigning user accounts and passwords, establishing security access levels, watching for unauthorized access, allocating storage space, and helping users with networking problems.

administrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person in charge of managing a computer. The administrator is responsible for installing software, assigning passwords, and managing files.

sysadmin.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person responsible for setting up and managing local computers, stand-alone servers, member servers, or domain controllers. An administrator performs such duties as assigning user accounts and passwords, establishing security access levels, watching for unauthorized access, allocating storage space, and helping users with networking problems.

primary business contact.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The main business contact linked to an Account.

initialize.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To set a variable to an initial value.

apostrophe.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ' character (user-typed text).

right single quotation mark.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ’ character (publishing character).

client region.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The portion of a window where an application displays output such as text or graphics.

proc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The computational and control unit of a computer. The CPU is the device that interprets and executes instructions.

central processing unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The computational and control unit of a computer. The CPU is the device that interprets and executes instructions.

cpu.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The computational and control unit of a computer. The CPU is the device that interprets and executes instructions.

processor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes personal data on behalf of the controller.

company.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The privacy relationship setting that allows a medium amount of information to be viewed, typically for people in your company and for people outside your company who work with you.

subject tree.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The hierarchical list of categories used to correlate and organize information.

grouping pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The area of the grouping window in which most user interaction takes place.

postal code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An alphanumeric code assigned to all addresses in order to facilitate mail delivery.

digital id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A combination of a digital certificate and a public and private encryption key set.

imaging.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The processes involved in the capture, storage, display, and printing of graphical images.

atomic.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to an operation where all the transaction data modifications must be performed; either all of the transaction data modifications are performed or none are performed.

white space.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any characters that can be found between words - this includes space (" "), newline (carriage return in combination with line feed), and the tab character.

white-space character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any characters that can be found between words - this includes space (" "), newline (carriage return in combination with line feed), and the tab character.

tarpitting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The practice of artificially delaying server responses for specific SMTP communication patterns that indicate high volumes of spam or other unwelcome email messages. The intent is to slow down the communication process for such email traffic so that the cost of sending spam increases for the person or organization who is sending the email.

varchar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The variable-length data type with a maximum of 8,000 ANSI characters.

share database.translation: Chia sẻ Cơ sở dữ liệu
share database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An option, found on the Business Contact Manager menu, in the Database Tools selection, that enables the user to share all information in a database.

newline character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control character that represents the end of a line of text and the beginning of a new line.

new line character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control character that represents the end of a line of text and the beginning of a new line.

chargeable transaction.translation: giao dịch có thể tính phí được
chargeable transaction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A transaction that can be included on an invoice and charged to a customer.

case study.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A detailed description of the processes specific customers engage in when selecting product solutions and technologies for deployment in response to business or technological challenges.

personal note.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A text note provided by a user that is displayed along with his or her presence status.

command prompt window.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window that mimics an old MS-DOS display for typing command-line instructions.

calculation formula.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Multidimensional Expressions (MDX) expression used to supply a value for cells in a calculation subcube, subject to the application of a calculation condition.

denial of service attack.translation: tấn công từ chối dịch vụ
denial of service attack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An attempt by a malicious (or unwitting) user, process, or system to prevent legitimate users from accessing a resource (usually a network service) by exploiting a weakness or design limitation in an information system.

dos.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An operating system that is loaded from disk devices when the system is started or rebooted.

denial-of-service attack.translation: tấn công từ chối dịch vụ
denial-of-service attack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An attempt by a malicious (or unwitting) user, process, or system to prevent legitimate users from accessing a resource (usually a network service) by exploiting a weakness or design limitation in an information system.

source data.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The list or table that's used to create a PivotTable or PivotChart report. Source data can be taken from an Excel list or range, an external database or cube, or another PivotTable report.

digitally sign.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To add a digital signature to a macro or file.

input device.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A peripheral device whose purpose is to allow the user to provide input to a computer system. Examples of input devices are keyboards, mice, joysticks, and styluses.

resolution strategy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of criteria that the repository engine evaluates sequentially when selecting an object, where multiple versions exist and version information is unspecified in the calling program.

superscript.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One character (or more) that is slightly higher than other text on a line, such as a footnote reference mark.

message transfer system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The X.400 term for a messaging system, which is a product that enables electronic communication over a network.

mts.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The X.400 term for a messaging system, which is a product that enables electronic communication over a network.

network location.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network type that a computer is connected to that automatically sets the appropriate firewall settings for the location.

mitigation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The act of reducing the probability and/or impact of a risk to an acceptable level.

risk mitigation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The act of reducing the probability and/or impact of a risk to an acceptable level.

pre-order.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To order an item that is currently not available.

home service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The status message displayed for the current network when a user changes the network selection to something other than the network of the main provider.

distribution share.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A folder that contains the source files for Windows products that you install. It may also contain additional device drivers and application files.

mail-enabled universal distribution grou.translation: nhóm phân phối thống nhất hỗ trợ thư
mail-enabled universal distribution grou.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group of recipients that are created to expedite the mass emailing of messages and other information. When email is sent to a mail-enabled universal distribution group, all members of that list receive a copy of the message. Mail-enabled universal distribution groups cannot be used to assign permissions.

data selector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A wizard that lets users select, configure, and import data from a data source into a Visio diagram.

data selector wizard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A wizard that lets users select, configure, and import data from a data source into a Visio diagram.

system protection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows technology that protects OS resources (files, folders registry keys) and prevents applications and administrators from making changes to a computer's resources in an arbitrary way.

identifying field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field or group of fields that identify an entity as a unique object.

pivotchart report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A chart that provides interactive analysis of data, like a PivotTable report. You can change views of data, see different levels of detail, or reorganize the chart layout by dragging fields and by showing or hiding items in fields.

database owner.translation: chủ sở hữu cơ sở dữ liệu
database owner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person who created the database, and has full control, including granting access permissions or deleting records. When a database has been restored, then the person who restored it becomes the owner.

mirror database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu phản chiếu
mirror database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database that functions as a backup of a primary database, receiving copies of every change to the primary database, and that can take over traffic if the primary database becomes unavailable.

mb.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A memory measurement unit that is equal to 1 million bytes.

megabyte.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A memory measurement unit that is equal to 1 million bytes.

highlight.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item or activity shared on Skype through the Highlights feature.

digital.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In computing, a characteristic of data that is represented as binary digits (zeros and ones).

data flow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An exchange of information between processes that represent discrete packets of data that flow into and out of processes.

spoof.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To make a transmission appear to come from a user other than the user who performed the action.

security role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A defined set of application access privileges. The security role assigned to a user determines which tasks the user can perform and which parts of the user interface the user can view. All users must be assigned at least one security role in order to access the system.

3-d effect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A diagramming capability that shows charts in three dimensions.

data adapter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object used to submit data to and retrieve data from databases, Web services, and Extensible Markup Language (XML) files.

full-text enabling.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of allowing full-text querying to occur on the current database.

justify.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To adjust horizontal spacing so that text is aligned evenly along both the left and right margins. Justifying text creates a smooth edge on both sides.

target server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server that receives jobs from a master server.

brand colors.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The colors that are specific to a particular company or product.

durability.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In the ACID model, the property of a transaction to persist, even during system failure.

account information.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The required information provided in order to authorize access to the enterprise application.

public key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The nonsecret half of a cryptographic key pair that is used with a public key algorithm. brochure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A three or four-panel publication style typically used to present information about products, services or special offers.

active window.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The window in which a user is currently working or directing input. An active window is typically at the top of the Z order and is distinguished by the color of its title bar.

task scheduler.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The tool which enables users to automatically perform routine tasks on a chosen computer by monitoring whatever criteria the users choose to initiate the tasks (referred to as triggers) and then executing the tasks when the criteria is met.

hosting environment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web or desktop application, such as a Windows Forms application, into which an InfoPath form is embedded.

design set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of publications that share a consistent color scheme, font scheme, and design.

control-break report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report that summarizes data in user-defined groups or breaks. A new group is triggered when different data is encountered.

text.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In word processing and desktop publishing, the main portion of a document, as opposed to headlines, tables, figures, footnotes, and other elements.

product and service items.translation: Các mục Sản phẩm và Dịch vụ
product and service items.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A dialog box that allows a user to add a new product to an Opportunity or the Product and Service Items list.

ics.translation: hệ thống kiểm soát công nghiệp
ics.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A combination of processes, control systems, and instrumentation used in production environments to achieve consistency, economy and safety levels above human control.

internet connection sharing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Windows technology that provides home and small-office computer users who have networked computers with the ability to share a single connection to the Internet.

internet sharing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Windows technology that provides home and small-office computer users who have networked computers with the ability to share a single connection to the Internet.

decision tree.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A treelike model of data produced by certain data mining methods. Decision trees can be used for prediction.

pt.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unit of measure referring to the height of a printed character. A point equals 1/72 of an inch, or approximately 1/28 of a centimeter.

point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An acknowledgment given to a player when they meet the conditions of a KPI in a game. Points add up to the player's score.

ribbon.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A band that is used to represent data in a ribbon chart.

real.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The official currency of Brazil.

batch processing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The execution of a batch file.

outdent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To move a task to a higher outline level.

negative indent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An indent where the text is displaced into the left margin if text direction is set to left-to-right, or toward the right margin if text direction is set to right-to-left.

memory-resident.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Permanently located in a computer's memory, rather than swapped in and out of memory as needed.

ram resident.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Permanently located in a computer's memory, rather than swapped in and out of memory as needed.

memo.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of column that contains long strings, typically more than 255 characters.

reading pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window in an email program where you can preview an item without opening it.

landscape orientation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An orientation where the long dimension of a rectangular area (for example, screen, photo, or paper) is horizontal.

landscape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An orientation where the long dimension of a rectangular area (for example, screen, photo, or paper) is horizontal.

twain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cross-platform interface for acquiring electronic images that have been captured by scanners, digital cameras, and still-frame video capture boards.

serial number.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number assigned to a specific inventory item to identify it and differentiate it from similar items with the same item number.

session.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A logical connection created between two hosts to exchange data.

software compatibility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In reference to software, harmony on a task-oriented level among computers and computer programs.

choose.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Lookup and reference Excel function that chooses a value from a list of values.

retention period.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The duration of time for which the data should be available.

retention range.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The duration of time for which the data should be available.

process color.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the four transparent inks (cyan, magenta, yellow, and black) that are used in commercial printing to produce color photographic images and a wide range of solid colors.

twip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unit of measure used in typesetting and desktop publishing, equal to one-twentieth of a printer's point, or 1/1440th of an inch.

marquee component.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control or component on a page that displays moving text.

scrolling text control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control or component on a page that displays moving text.

autodiscover.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature available in Outlook 2007 and some mobile devices that automatically configures the clients for access to Exchange Server 2007. The client sends the user name and password information to the Exchange 2007 server. The Autodiscover Web service that is running on the Exchange Client Access server returns an XML file that contains configuration information, which is interpreted by the client. If the user is moved to a different server later, the client will automatically query the Autodiscover Web service again to update the client configuration.

term.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Either a single number or variable, or numbers and variables multiplied together. For example, the expression 4x - 7 + y = 5 contains four terms: 4x, 7, y, and 5.

offline address book generation.translation: khởi tạo sổ địa chỉ ngoại tuyến
offline address book generation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process by which Exchange Server creates and updates the OAB. Administrators can define when the OAB generation process will run.

oab generation.translation: khởi tạo sổ địa chỉ ngoại tuyến
oab generation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process by which Exchange Server creates and updates the OAB. Administrators can define when the OAB generation process will run.

side-fold card.translation: Bưu thiếp gập bốn ngang dọc
side-fold card.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the page size options available in Publisher for printing a folded card. This option prints four pages per sheet of paper, with fold on left.

accepted domain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An SMTP namespace for which Microsoft an Exchange Server organization sends and receives email.

property definition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The characteristics or properties that define how a property is used and interpreted. The group of properties that forms a property definition is stored in a dictionary.

countersign.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To sign a document already signed by the other party.

horizontal line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web page editor command that inserts a horizontal line onto a Web page.

eyedropper.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool that enables a user to sample the color of any pixel on a screen and apply that color to an object.

ruler origin.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The beginning or zero point of a horizontal or vertical ruler.

allocate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To assign resources to an account.

trap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To create small overlaps where two differently colored objects abut on a printed page.

windows api.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The API that developers can use for creating applications that run on Windows 95 or later.

master page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A page that defines the layout and common elements for a set of web pages. It is merged at run time with content pages that define page-specific content.

handoff.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A process where a person ending their shift gives worker from the incoming shift pertinent information.

placeholder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A symbolic value used in place of a real value that is unknown or unavailable at the current time, or that is not displayed for security reasons.

packet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unit of information transmitted from one computer or device to another on a network.

hold down.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To continue to press a keyboard key or mouse button.

open xml formats.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The international open standard for word-processing documents, presentations, and spreadsheets that can be freely implemented across multiple applications and platforms.

webmail.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Electronic mail that can be accessed through a Web site.

web-based e-mail.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Electronic mail that can be accessed through a Web site.

web-based mail.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Electronic mail that can be accessed through a Web site.

scalar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A factor, coefficient, or variable consisting of a single value (as opposed to a record, an array, or some other complex data structure).

service-level agreement.translation: thỏa thuận cấp độ dịch vụ
service-level agreement.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An agreement between two or more parties describing the deliverables, support, and communication that each party will provide to the other.

sla.translation: thỏa thuận cấp độ dịch vụ
sla.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An agreement between two or more parties describing the deliverables, support, and communication that each party will provide to the other.

intercompany.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Relating to interactions between two or more internal companies.

e-mail router configuration wizard.translation: Trình hướng dẫn Cấu hình Bộ định tuyến Email
e-mail router configuration wizard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A wizard that guides users in creating an incoming email configuration, an outgoing email configuration, and a link to an existing Microsoft Dynamics CRM deployment. After they install and configure these components using this wizard, the Microsoft Dynamics CRM E-mail Router will transport incoming and outgoing Microsoft Dynamics CRM email.

administrative time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: All of a resource's time not devoted to a formal "project" (includes Working and Non-Working Time).

exchange activesync.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A protocol that makes it possible for users to sync their email, calendar, contact, and task data from Exchange Server to supporting devices.

open.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To create an account so that a product, service, or app is available for use.

transport event.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An occurrence of a particular message transport activity or phase through the SMTP and NNTP services.

distribution database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu phân phối
distribution database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database that stores replication status data, metadata about the publication, and, in some cases, acts as a queue for data moving from publisher to subscribers.

auto-recover.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The cross-Office feature that automatically recovers content if the user's program or computer malfunctions.

autorecover.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The cross-Office feature that automatically recovers content if the user's program or computer malfunctions.

autorecovery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The cross-Office feature that automatically recovers content if the user's program or computer malfunctions.

recording.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A stored record of the audio and video components of a meeting or session.

failover.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a failover cluster or server cluster, the process of taking a clustered service or application offline on one node and bringing it back online on another node.

issue tracking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A solution provided as a template with Microsoft Office Developer that makes it possible for users to enter issues into a database and track them through resolution. The Issue Tracking solution can be used as is or as the baseline for new solutions.

crop mark.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mark that shows where a publication page will be trimmed.

gadget.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A lightweight and task-specific add-in program that integrates with applications to expose data at a glance.

disk space.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of storage space available for storing and processing on a disc.

source object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The single object to which all objects in a particular collection are connected by way of relationships that are all of the same relationship type.

great-looking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Impressive or compelling in appearance.

active directory federation services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component that provides Web single-sign-on (SSO) technologies. AD FS provides SSO by securely sharing digital identity and entitlement rights across security and enterprise boundaries. AD FS supports the WS-Federation Passive Requestor Profile (WS-F PRP).

active directory federation services (ad.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component that provides Web single-sign-on (SSO) technologies. AD FS provides SSO by securely sharing digital identity and entitlement rights across security and enterprise boundaries. AD FS supports the WS-Federation Passive Requestor Profile (WS-F PRP).

ad fs.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component that provides Web single-sign-on (SSO) technologies. browser-compatible form template.translation: mẫu biểu mẫu tương thích với trình duyệt

extensible markup language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A markup language for describing and exchanging structured data in a format that is independent of operating systems and applications. XML is a World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) specification and is a subset of Standard Generalized Markup Language (SGML).

xml.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A markup language for describing and exchanging structured data in a format that is independent of operating systems and applications. XML is a World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) specification and is a subset of Standard Generalized Markup Language (SGML).

account lockout.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows security feature that locks a user account if a number of failed logon attempts occur within a specified amount of time, based on security policy lockout settings. Locked accounts cannot log on.

collect data through e-mail.translation: Thu thập Dữ liệu Qua Email
collect data through e-mail.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows an end-user to collect data via E-mail using Access, Outlook, and InfoPath.

relationship role.translation: vai trò của mối quan hệ
relationship role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of text labels describing the role accounts and contacts play with opportunities as well as other accounts and contacts.

leader line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A line or row of characters used to lead the eye from a data label to a data point, or from a callout to the appropriate part of an illustration.

profit chart.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A diagram that displays the theoretical increase in profit that is associated with using various data models.

lookup field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field in a table that draws data from another table.

inflation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The overall price movement (generally upward) of goods and services in an economy.

selector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a cascading style sheet style definition (or style rule), the HTML element linked to a particular set of style properties and values.

mapped data field.translation: trường dữ liệu được ánh xạ
mapped data field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field that represents commonly used information, such as "First Name." If a data source contains a "First Name" field or variation, such as "FName," the data source field automatically maps to the corresponding mapped data field.

trend analysis chart.translation: biểu đồ phân tích xu hướng
trend analysis chart.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A chart that shows the projected trend for a KPI based on analysis of previous data.

dynamic distribution group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A distribution group that uses recipient filters and conditions to derive its membership at the time the message is sent.

edge transport server role.translation: vai trò máy chủ Edge Transport
edge transport server role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Exchange Server 2007 and 2010 server role that provides anti-spam and antivirus protection and applies messaging security policies to messages in transport between organizations by using a series of agents that act on messages as they are processed by the message transport components. This server role is deployed in the perimeter network outside the Active Directory directory service forest. Computers that have the Edge Transport server role installed handle all Internet-facing mail flow and provide Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) relay and smart host services for the Exchange organization.

callback function.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A function provided by (IIS) that allows an Internet Server API (ISAPI) extension or filter to access IIS services.

server subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription to a merge publication with an assigned priority value used for conflict detection and resolution.

global subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription to a merge publication with an assigned priority value used for conflict detection and resolution.

raw ip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of Internet protocol that does not contain any link-layer header before it.

low-level ip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of Internet protocol that does not contain any link-layer header before it.

bleed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The extent to which a picture runs off the printed page.

action row.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A row in the upper part of the Macro window in which you enter macro names, actions, conditions, and comments associated with a particular macro or macro group.

a1.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An alphanumeric convention for referencing the location of cells in a worksheet. The column is represented by a letter (A through IV, for a total of 256 columns) and the row is represented by a number (1 through 65536).

a1 notation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An alphanumeric convention for referencing the location of cells in a worksheet. The column is represented by a letter (A through IV, for a total of 256 columns) and the row is represented by a number (1 through 65536).

a1 reference style.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An alphanumeric convention for referencing the location of cells in a worksheet. The column is represented by a letter (A through IV, for a total of 256 columns) and the row is represented by a number (1 through 65536).

reports.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A folder in the workspace browser where available report views are listed.

exchange management console.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Exchange 2007 graphical user interface (GUI) from which administrators can perform tasks to configure and manage Exchange servers. The Exchange Management Console is based on Windows Microsoft Management Console (MMC) 3.0.

touch training.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that helps improve the recognition of a user's touch flicks by a process in which the user's touch flicks are analyzed.

uniform resource locator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An address that uniquely identifies a location on the Internet. A URL is usually preceded by http://, as in http://www.microsoft.com. A URL can contain more detail, such as the name of a page of hypertext, often with the file name extension .html or .htm.

url.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An address that uniquely identifies a location on the Internet. A URL is usually preceded by http://, as in http://www.microsoft.com. A URL can contain more detail, such as the name of a page of hypertext, often with the file name extension .html or .htm.

web address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An address that uniquely identifies a location on the Internet. A URL is usually preceded by http://, as in http://www.microsoft.com. A URL can contain more detail, such as the name of a page of hypertext, often with the file name extension .html or .htm.

ole object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object that supports the OLE protocol for object linking and embedding.

event trigger.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The mechanism by which a system or application event triggers either an instant or an animated change in one or more properties.

ip allow list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A filtering list that is used by the Connection Filter agent in Exchange Server 2007. IP addresses on the IP Allow list are considered "safe" and are exempted from processing by other anti-spam agents.

ip/voip gateway.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A third-party hardware device or product that connects a legacy PBX to a LAN. An IP/VoIP gateway translates or converts TDM or telephony circuit-switched protocols to packet switched protocols that can be used on a VoIP-based network.

error bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In statistical or scientific data, a bar that shows the potential error or degree of uncertainty relative to each data marker in a series.

master design set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A design set that includes a broad collection of common business publications.

trim points.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The points where playback of a file or clip begins and ends. There are two trim points: start trim point and end trim point.

join column.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A column referenced in a join condition.

accounting system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The accounting program.

mailbox database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu hộp thư
mailbox database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database for storing mailboxes in Exchange Server. The mailbox database manages the data in mailboxes, tracks deleted messages and mailbox sizes, and assists in message transfers. A mailbox database is stored as an Exchange database (.edb) file.

in-app subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An agreement in which a customer prepays for periodic or regular services.

conversation handle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An handle which uniquely defines a conversation.

permission policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An approach to restricting permission for a given document, workbook, presentation, or message. The policy defines which Office features are available, which information can be accessed, and what level of editing is allowed.

business phone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The field where the telephone number for a business can be entered.

getting started.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that serves as a launching point for several optional Windows tasks and OEM-defined tasks.

write-in product.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A product that is manually added to quotes, orders, and invoices rather than selected from the Microsoft Dynamics CRM product catalog.

application service provider.translation: nhà cung cấp dịch vụ ứng dụng
application service provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An organization that delivers a contractual service to deploy, host, manage, and provide access to an application from a facility other than the customer's site.

asp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web-oriented technology developed by Microsoft that is designed to enable server-side scripting.

modify report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A button, found on the Report toolbar, that enables the user to customize a report.

normalization rule.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A design rule that minimizes data redundancy and results in a database in which the Database Engine and application software can easily enforce integrity.

offline address book.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A snapshot of information from an address book that has been downloaded so that an Outlook user can access it while disconnected from the server. It contains the properties of a user, such as email addresses, that Outlook requires to send an email message and display information about the sender.

oab.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A snapshot of information from an address book that has been downloaded so that an Outlook user can access it while disconnected from the server. It contains the properties of a user, such as email addresses, that Outlook requires to send an email message and display information about the sender.

web query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query that retrieves data stored on your intranet or the Internet.

abort.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To terminate abruptly, often used in reference to a program or procedure in progress.

file restore.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An operation that restores one or more files of a database.

automatic recovery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Recovery that occurs every time SQL Server is restarted.

offline address book distribution.translation: phân phối sổ địa chỉ ngoại tuyến
offline address book distribution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The method by which the offline address book (OAB) can be accessed by users when they are working remotely or over a dial-up connection. To distribute the OAB, administrators can use Web-based distribution, public folder distribution, or both. Public folder distribution is required for Outlook 2003 or earlier clients.

oab distribution.translation: phân phối sổ địa chỉ ngoại tuyến
oab distribution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The method by which the offline address book (OAB) can be accessed by users when they are working remotely or over a dial-up connection. To distribute the OAB, administrators can use Web-based distribution, public folder distribution, or both. Public folder distribution is required for Outlook 2003 or earlier clients.

routing group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A logical grouping of well-connected Exchange servers between which no connector is required for message transfer.

autoshape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A predefined or free-form figure — such as a line, oval, cube, flowchart symbol, banner, or free-form scribble — that the user can insert into a document and then customize.

forest root domain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The first domain created in a new forest. The forest-wide administrative groups, Enterprise Admins and Schema Admins, are located in this domain. As a best practice, new domains are created as children of the forest root domain.

x-coordinate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The position of a point with reference to the x-axis, defined in conjunction with the y- and z-coordinates.

panning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A multi-touch gesture that consists of one or two fingers moving in the same direction, parallel to each other.

checkpoint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a server cluster node`s registry, a snapshot of the Cluster subkey or of an application subkey. The checkpoint is written to the quorum disk when certain events take place, such as a node failure.

storage group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of mailbox stores and public folder stores that share a set of transaction log files. Exchange manages each storage group with a separate server process.

principal database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In database mirroring, a read-write database whose transaction log is continuously sent to the mirror server, which restores the log to the mirror database.

constant.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A numeric or string value that is not calculated and, therefore, does not change.

maximize.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To enlarge an app on a dual-screen device so that it goes across both screens.

administrator role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of rights that allows a user to modify all web site content and manage site settings and accounts.

controller.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data; where the purposes and means of such processing are determined by Union or Member State law, the controller or the specific criteria for its nomination may be provided for by Union or Member State law

game controller.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device used to control a video game. For example, a joystick, mouse, or gamepad.

n-ary.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to an operator that can hold an arbitrary number of arguments, or to a function that can hold an arbitrary number of operators.

nary.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to an operator that can hold an arbitrary number of arguments, or to a function that can hold an arbitrary number of operators.

ro.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to the status of an ad that has been opened for review within the last 30 minutes.

read-only.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Capable of being retrieved (read), printed or copied but not changed (written) or saved.

mta.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An apartment that consists of one or more threads.

multithreaded apartment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An apartment that consists of one or more threads.

excel cube functions.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Functions used to extract and display OLAP data (sets and values).

network drive.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: On a local area network (LAN), a drive that other computers on the network can connect to. A network drive allows people to access shared files and folders.

user-defined field.translation: trường do người dùng xác định
user-defined field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field that you can define to track information specific to your business.

what you see is what you get.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to a program or interface that allows creation and editing of web pages, text, or graphical user interfaces such that users can see what the end results will look like while the documents are being created.

wysiwyg.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to a program or interface that allows creation and editing of web pages, text, or graphical user interfaces such that users can see what the end results will look like while the documents are being created.

enumerated data type.translation: loại dữ liệu được liệt kê

enum type.translation: loại dữ liệu được liệt kê
enum type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data type consisting of a sequence of named values given in a particular order.

cluster continuous replication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A replication that combines the asynchronous log shipping and replay features built into Exchange 2007 with the failover and management features provided by a failover cluster that is created with the Microsoft Windows Cluster service.

ccr.translation: hồ sơ chăm sóc sức khỏe liên tục
ccr.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard format used to transfer patient health information between systems.

alert box.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An on-screen box, in a graphical user interface, that is used to deliver a message or warning.

time off.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A period of time where a worker is not working.

remote host.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web server on a separate server computer. A remote host is connected to other servers by a network connection.

rights-managed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Stored on a server or client computer that is configured to control access to content by using information rights management (IRM) technology.

presence awareness.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that enables the user to see when people are working in a workspace, online, or offline

cross-validation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A method for evaluating the accuracy of a data mining model.

prediction calculator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A new report that is based on logistic regression analysis and that presents each contributing factor together with a score calculated by the algorithm. The report is presented both as a worksheet that helps you enter data and make calculations of the probable outcomes, and as a printed report that does the same thing.

caption.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Descriptive text that represents the audio content of a television or video program as text on the screen.

caption text.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Descriptive text that is associated with a piece of content, such as an image.

shopping basket analysis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard data mining algorithm that analyzes a list of transactions to make predictions about which items are most frequently purchased together.

market basket analysis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard data mining algorithm that analyzes a list of transactions to make predictions about which items are most frequently purchased together.

holdout store.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The data mining structure that is used to cache the holdout data. It contains references to the holdout data.

autocommit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default transaction management mode for the Database Engine. The Database Engine automatically starts a transaction for each individual Transact-SQL statement. When the statement completes, the transaction is committed or rolled back based on the success or failure of the statement.

auto commit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default transaction management mode for the Database Engine. The Database Engine automatically starts a transaction for each individual Transact-SQL statement. When the statement completes, the transaction is committed or rolled back based on the success or failure of the statement.

autocommit mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default transaction management mode for the Database Engine. The Database Engine automatically starts a transaction for each individual Transact-SQL statement. When the statement completes, the transaction is committed or rolled back based on the success or failure of the statement.

gather-write operation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A performance optimization where the Database Engine collects multiple modified data pages into a single write operation.

box and whisker chart.translation: biểu đồ hộp và dải dữ liệu trung bình
box and whisker chart.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A statistical type of chart that uses boxes to indicate statistical distribution and easily identify outlier points. There are five values: upper quartile, lower quartile, High Box, Low Box, and Median.

box plot chart.translation: biểu đồ hộp và dải dữ liệu trung bình
box plot chart.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A statistical type of chart that uses boxes to indicate statistical distribution and easily identify outlier points. There are five values: upper quartile, lower quartile, High Box, Low Box, and Median.

boxplot.translation: biểu đồ hộp và dải dữ liệu trung bình
boxplot.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A statistical type of chart that uses boxes to indicate statistical distribution and easily identify outlier points. There are five values: upper quartile, lower quartile, High Box, Low Box, and Median.

database reference.translation: tham chiếu cơ sở dữ liệu
database reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A path, expression or filename that resolves to a database.

target queue.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Service Broker, the queue associated with the service to which messages are sent.

provider object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object that's part of a data provider such as Oracle Provider for SQL Server.

save process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of writing data to disk.

report signature.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A string used to identify the version of a report.

hierarchy tree.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A structure in which elements are related to each other hierarchically.

table reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A name, expression or string that resolves to a table.

delete clause.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A part of a DML Statement that contains the DELETE keyword and associated parameters.

diamond-shape relationship.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A chain of attribute relationships that splits and rejoins but that contains no redundant relationships. For example, Day->Month->Year and Day->Quarter->Year have the same start and end points, but do not have any common relationships.

workload group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Resource Governor, a container for session requests that are similar according to the classification rules that are applied to each request. A workload group allows the aggregate monitoring of resource consumption and a uniform policy that is applied to all the requests in a group.

version history.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that tracks and stores a record of a shared document when it is first created, and each time it is edited.

declarative management framework facet.translation: Thuộc tính Khung Quản lý Khai báo
declarative management framework facet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of logical pre-defined properties that model the behavior or characteristics for certain types of managed targets (such as a database, table, login, view,etc) in policy-based management.

facet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A piece of data about a resource that contains complex values, generally indicating behaviors or capabilities of an item.

declarative management framework.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A policy based system of SQL Server management.

data flow component.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component of SQL Server 2005 Integration Services that manipulates data.

transformation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The replacement of the variables in an algebraic expression by their values in terms of another set of variables.

destination.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The location (drive, folder, or directory) to which a file is copied or moved.

raw file source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An SSIS source that reads raw data from a file.

raw file destination.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An SSIS destination that writes raw data to a file.

filter criteria.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Conditions that users specify to limit which records are included in the result set of a query.

foreign connector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Exchange Server 2007 connector that uses a Drop directory on a Hub Transport server to send messages to a local messaging server that doesn't use the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) as its primary transport mechanism.

full import.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An import of all data from a file, or a scoped view, of a connected data source to the connector space. Data from the connected data source is compared with data in the connector space. If there are no attribute changes, the object is not changed in the connector space.

constructor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special initialization function that is called automatically whenever an instance of a class is declared. This function prevents errors that result from the use of uninitialized objects. The constructor must have the same name as the class itself and must not return a value.

ip allow list provider.translation: Bộ cung cấp Danh sách Cho phép IP
ip allow list provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Exchange Server 2007, the feature that the Exchange administrator configures to enable functionality provided by IP Allow List Provider services that compile lists of IP addresses that are known not to have sent spam in the past. The Connection Filter agent queries the service to determine if a given IP address is "safe."

ip allow list provider configuration.translation: Cấu hình bộ cung cấp Danh sách Cho phép IP
ip allow list provider configuration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Configuration that is used by the Connection Filter agent to query an IP Allow List provider.

ip allow list provider service.translation: Dịch vụ bộ cung cấp Danh sách Cho phép IP
ip allow list provider service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A business that compiles and distributes lists of IP addresses that are known not to have sent spam in the past.

ip block list provider.translation: Bộ cung cấp Danh sách Chặn IP
