ip block list provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Exchange Server 2007, the feature that the Exchange administrator configures to enable functionality provided by IP Block List Provider services that compile lists of IP addresses from which spam has originated in the past.

ip block list provider configuration.translation: Cấu hình bộ cung cấp Danh sách Chặn IP
ip block list provider configuration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The configuration that is used by the Connection Filter agent to query an IP Block List provider.

ip block list provider service.translation: Dịch vụ bộ cung cấp Danh sách Chặn IP
ip block list provider service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The business that compiles and distributes lists of IP addresses from which spam has originated in the past.

real-time block list service.translation: Dịch vụ bộ cung cấp Danh sách Chặn IP
real-time block list service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The business that compiles and distributes lists of IP addresses from which spam has originated in the past.

rbl service.translation: Dịch vụ bộ cung cấp Danh sách Chặn IP
rbl service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The business that compiles and distributes lists of IP addresses from which spam has originated in the past.

journaling mailbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mailbox used only for collecting journal reports in an Exchange Server organization.

junk e-mail folder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The folder where junk email is delivered.

organization configuration node.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Exchange Server 2007, a node in the Console pane of the Exchange Management Console that administrators use to configure administrative access roles for users or groups.

quota message.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An email message that is automatically sent by Microsoft Exchange to the owners of a mailbox or a public folder when a size limit, which is called a storage quota, for the mailbox or public folder has been exceeded or is at risk of being exceeded.

recipient block list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An administrator-defined list of recipients for which mail coming in from the Internet should never be accepted.

rtaudio.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An advanced speech codec that is designed for real-time two-way Voice over IP (VoIP) applications such as gaming, audio conferencing, and wireless applications over IP. RTAudio is the preferred Microsoft audio codec and is the default codec for Microsoft Unified Communications platforms.

server configuration node.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Exchange Server 2007, a node in the Console pane of the Exchange Management Console that enables administrators to view a list of all the servers in their Exchange organization and perform server role-specific tasks. The Server Configuration node contains the following sub-nodes: Mailbox, Client Access, Hub Transport, and Unified Messaging.

spam confidence level threshold.translation: ngưỡng mức tin cậy là thư rác
spam confidence level threshold.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The level at which the content filter feature in Exchange Server takes a specific action on a specific message, such as rejecting a message or deleting a message.

test environment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An environment that corresponds as closely as possible to the production environment and within which system and user acceptance tests can be carried out.

tls authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Authentication by using the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol.

tts engine.translation: công cụ chuyển văn bản sang tiếng nói
tts engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The component of Speech Engine Services that processes text input and produces speech output by synthesizing words and phrases.

text-to-speech engine.translation: công cụ chuyển văn bản sang tiếng nói
text-to-speech engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The component of Speech Engine Services that processes text input and produces speech output by synthesizing words and phrases.

unified messaging language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the languages in which Microsoft Exchange Server 2007 Unified Messaging (UM) functionality is supported by the availability of UM language packs.

usage type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Exchange Server 2007, the type of connector that is determined by the intended use of the connector. The usage type determines the default settings for the connector. This includes the SIDs that are authenticated, the permissions that are assigned to those SIDs, and the authentication mechanism.

work pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Exchange 2007, the bottom middle pane of the Exchange Management Console. The work pane provides detailed information about the specified Exchange server.

drawing interchange format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer-aided design file format originally developed by Autodesk; for use with the AutoCAD program to facilitate transfer of graphics files between different applications.

drawing exchange format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer-aided design file format originally developed by Autodesk; for use with the AutoCAD program to facilitate transfer of graphics files between different applications.

dxf.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer-aided design file format originally developed by Autodesk; for use with the AutoCAD program to facilitate transfer of graphics files between different applications.

dynamic connector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A one-dimensional (1-D) connector shape that changes its path to avoid crossing through two-dimensional (2-D) placeable shapes that lie between the two shapes the connector connects.

routable connector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A one-dimensional (1-D) connector shape that changes its path to avoid crossing through two-dimensional (2-D) placeable shapes that lie between the two shapes the connector connects.

estimate at completion.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The expected total cost of a task or project, based on performance as of the status date. EAC is calculated as follows: EAC = ACWP + (BAC-BCWP)/CPI.

eac.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The web-based management tool for Microsoft Exchange administrators and enterprise email users.

internet locator service server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that lists the names and email addresses of people who are running NetMeeting and who are logged on to the server. This information is used to connect to their computers.

ils server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that lists the names and email addresses of people who are running NetMeeting and who are logged on to the server. This information is used to connect to their computers.

directory server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that lists the names and email addresses of people who are running NetMeeting and who are logged on to the server. This information is used to connect to their computers.

design.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of Copilot prompts that let users leverage the Microsoft Design features related to image skills and document themes from within Word, PowerPoint, OneNote, and others.

dgn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A format used by the Bentley MicroStation CAD program to store drawing files.

consolidated project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A project containing one or more inserted projects. These can retain links to their source projects and may be linked to one another.

master project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A project containing one or more inserted projects. These can retain links to their source projects and may be linked to one another.

communicates relationship.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a use case diagram, a relationship that defines how an actor participates in a use case. You can add an arrow to the relationship to indicate the direction the information flows.

actuals.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of work that has been performed on a task or assignment.

actual work.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of work that has been performed on a task or assignment.

actual cost of work performed.translation: chi phí thực tế cho công việc đã thực hiện
actual cost of work performed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The actual costs incurred for work already performed by a resource on a task, up to the project status date or today's date.

acwp.translation: chi phí thực tế cho công việc đã thực hiện
acwp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The actual costs incurred for work already performed by a resource on a task, up to the project status date or today's date.

baseline cost.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The original project, resource, and assignment cost as shown in the baseline plan. The baseline cost is a snapshot of the cost at the time when the baseline plan was saved.

budget at completion.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The original project, resource, and assignment cost as shown in the baseline plan. The baseline cost is a snapshot of the cost at the time when the baseline plan was saved.

bac.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The original project, resource, and assignment cost as shown in the baseline plan. The baseline cost is a snapshot of the cost at the time when the baseline plan was saved.

font manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software program that helps you increase or decrease the sets of available fonts.

type manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software program that helps you increase or decrease the sets of available fonts.

active accessibility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technology that improves the way programs and the operating system work with accessibility aids, such as screen readers.

msaa.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technology that improves the way programs and the operating system work with accessibility aids, such as screen readers.

microsoft active accessibility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technology that improves the way programs and the operating system work with accessibility aids, such as screen readers.

microsoft project exchange.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A record-based ASCII text format that is used to import data into Project.

mpx.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A record-based ASCII text format that is used to import data into Project.

microsoft project database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A record-based Access-compliant file format that you can use for saving an entire project.

mpd.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A record-based Access-compliant file format that you can use for saving an entire project.

end name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A name that appears as a text string near the end of a binary association. It indicates the role played by the class attached to the association end, so each end can have its own end name.

role name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A name that appears as a text string near the end of a binary association. It indicates the role played by the class attached to the association end, so each end can have its own end name.

local formula.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A formula that is stored in a cell of a shape instead of being inherited from a master or a style. A local formula overrides changes to the corresponding cell in the master of which the shape is an instance.

local override.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A formula that is stored in a cell of a shape instead of being inherited from a master or a style. A local formula overrides changes to the corresponding cell in the master of which the shape is an instance.

tap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To touch an item once with the tablet pen and then lift the pen quickly.

connection filter agent.translation: Tác nhân Bộ lọc Kết nối
connection filter agent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An anti-spam agent that is enabled on computers that have the Microsoft Exchange Server 2007 Edge Transport server role installed.

resource breakdown structure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The structure that describes an organization's hierarchy. The RBS code defines the hierarchical position that a resource holds in the organization.

rbs.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The structure that describes an organization's hierarchy. The RBS code defines the hierarchical position that a resource holds in the organization.

user breakdown structure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The structure that describes an organization's hierarchy. The RBS code defines the hierarchical position that a resource holds in the organization.

pert analysis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A process by which you evaluate a probable outcome based on three scenarios: best-case, expected-case, and worst-case.

program, evaluation and review technique.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A process by which you evaluate a probable outcome based on three scenarios: best-case, expected-case, and worst-case.

bcwp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The earned value field that indicates how much of the task's budget should have been spent, given the actual duration of the task.

budgeted cost of work performed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The earned value field that indicates how much of the task's budget should have been spent, given the actual duration of the task.

cross-reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A reference in a document to other material.

budgeted cost of work scheduled.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The earned value field that shows how much of the budget should have been spent, in view of the baseline cost of the task, assignment, or resource. BCWS is calculated as the cumulative time-phased baseline costs up to the status date or today's date.

bcws.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The earned value field that shows how much of the budget should have been spent, in view of the baseline cost of the task, assignment, or resource. BCWS is calculated as the cumulative time-phased baseline costs up to the status date or today's date.

coefficient of determination.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number from 0 to 1 that reveals how closely the estimated values for the trendline correspond to your actual data. A trendline is most reliable when its R-squared value is at or near 1.

r-squared value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number from 0 to 1 that reveals how closely the estimated values for the trendline correspond to your actual data. A trendline is most reliable when its R-squared value is at or near 1.

business logic.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of an application program that performs the required data processing of the business. It refers to the routines that perform the data entry, update, query and report processing, and more specifically to the processing that takes place behind the scenes rather than the presentation logic required to display the data on the screen.

schedule variance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The difference between the budgeted cost of work performed [BCWP] and the budgeted cost of work scheduled [BCWS]. This is calculated as follows: SV = Budgeted Cost of Work Performed - Budgeted Cost of Work Scheduled.

sv.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The difference between the budgeted cost of work performed [BCWP] and the budgeted cost of work scheduled [BCWS]. This is calculated as follows: SV = Budgeted Cost of Work Performed - Budgeted Cost of Work Scheduled.

to complete performance index.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ratio of the work remaining to be done to funds remaining to be spent, as of the status date [BAC - BCWP]/[BAC - ACWP]. A TCPI value greater than one indicates a need for increased performance; less than one indicates performance can decrease.

tcpi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ratio of the work remaining to be done to funds remaining to be spent, as of the status date [BAC - BCWP]/[BAC - ACWP]. A TCPI value greater than one indicates a need for increased performance; less than one indicates performance can decrease.

tick mark label.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A label that identifies the categories, values, or series in a chart.

tick-mark label.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A label that identifies the categories, values, or series in a chart.

tick mark.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small line of measurement, similar to a division on a ruler, that intersects an axis.

trusted publisher.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The developer of a macro that is trusted by you on your computer. The trusted publisher is identified by the certificate that they used to digitally sign the macro.

trusted source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The developer of a macro that is trusted by you on your computer. The trusted publisher is identified by the certificate that they used to digitally sign the macro.

variance at completion.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The earned value field that shows the difference between the budget at completion [BAC] and the estimate at completion [EAC]. In Project, the EAC is the Total Cost field, and the BAC is the Baseline Cost field.

vac.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The earned value field that shows the difference between the budget at completion [BAC] and the estimate at completion [EAC]. In Project, the EAC is the Total Cost field, and the BAC is the Baseline Cost field.

us unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unit used in the United States' measurement system, such as inches, feet, yards, and miles.

u.s. unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unit used in the United States' measurement system, such as inches, feet, yards, and miles.

chronicle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A table that stores state information for a single application. An example is an event chronicle, which can store event data for use with scheduled subscriptions.

mediation server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server running Lync Server or Office Communications Server that mediates signaling and voice between the Enterprise Voice IP network and the public switched telephone network.

active data object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The data access interface that communicates with OLE DB-compliant data sources to connect to, retrieve, manipulate, and update data.

activex data objects.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The data access interface that communicates with OLE DB-compliant data sources to connect to, retrieve, manipulate, and update data.

ado.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The data access interface that communicates with OLE DB-compliant data sources to connect to, retrieve, manipulate, and update data.

field data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A property of a field that defines the kinds of data the field can store.

data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A property of a field that defines the kinds of data the field can store.

cd-rom.translation: bộ nhớ chỉ đọc trên đĩa compact
cd-rom.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A form of storage characterized by high capacity (roughly 650 MB) and the use of laser optics instead of magnetic means for reading data.

compact disc read-only memory.translation: bộ nhớ chỉ đọc trên đĩa compact
compact disc read-only memory.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A form of storage characterized by high capacity (roughly 650 MB) and the use of laser optics instead of magnetic means for reading data.

anonymous access.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An authentication mechanism that does not require user accounts and passwords.

anonymous authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An authentication mechanism that does not require user accounts and passwords.

1-d shape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shape that only has length, thus existing only in one dimension.

2-d shape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shape that has four selection handles that you can use to resize the shape proportionally.

2-element constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A constraint that applies to two elements, such as two classes or two associations. The constraint is shown as a dashed arrow from one element to the other, labeled by the constraint string in braces ({ }).

action state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an activity diagram, a type of state that has an internal action and at least one outgoing transition that involves the explicit events of completing the internal action.

active page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The page that is currently available for editing in a document.

activity diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special case of a statechart diagram in which all of the states are action states and the transitions are triggered by the completion of actions in the source state.

activity plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A schedule for planning the activities that often follow the completion of a project.

actor class.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The basic component of a ROOM structure diagram. The space inside the actor can contain actor references, behavior end ports, reference ports, bindings, and layer connections. The border can contain class relay ports and class end ports.

actor reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The actors that define components of your structure diagram. Actor references can appear only inside an actor class. An actor reference can have reference ports on its outside border.

actual duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time a task has been in progress.

ade file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Access project (.adp) file with all modules compiled and all editable source code removed.

administrative closure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of documenting and archiving a project in a timely manner, as well as formally accepting the project's product and lessons learned.

alignment box.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The rectangle that appears around shapes and objects from other applications as you move them.

angle of rotation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The angle of the orientation of a shape's local coordinate system with respect to its parent coordinate system. The angle of rotation is specified in the Angle cell of the Shape Transform section in a ShapeSheet spreadsheet.

data definition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The attributes, properties, and objects in a database.

angular unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The unit in which angles are expressed in ShapeSheet cells.

assignment delay.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time between the scheduled start of a task and the time that the assigned resource is to start working on the task.

assignment owner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An enterprise resource who is responsible for entering progress information in Project Web Access. This person can be different than the person initially assigned to the task.

assignment view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view that shows the resources assigned to each task as well as the total and time-phased work and cost information for each assignment. The two assignment views are the Task Usage and Resource Usage views.

association end.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The end of a binary or other association where it connects to a class. By associating properties with an association end, you can indicate the role or direction.

associationrole.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of collaboration role that describes the relationship between two ClassifierRoles. It is represented by a path between two class role elements and can include the underlined name of the corresponding association.

bound element.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a static structure diagram, a use of a parameterized class, or template, in which the parameters from the parameterized class are bound to actual values.

bow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The distance from the midpoint of a circular arc to the midpoint of the arc's chord.

breakdown shape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shape in a PivotDiagram, positioned along the connector between a parent PivotDiagram node and the children of that node.

breakdown.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shape in a PivotDiagram, positioned along the connector between a parent PivotDiagram node and the children of that node.

showplan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report showing the execution plan for an SQL statement.

budget resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A resource that captures the maximum capacity for a project to consume money, work, or material units for a project. Budgets can only be applied at the project level by assigning a budget resource to the project summary task.

built-in menu.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A menu that is available by default in an application; it is not created by the user.

built-in style.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The formatting attributes that are available by default in an application's style list.

calendar view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Project view that displays a project's tasks in a calendar format.

callevent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, an indication that an object has received a call for an operation. A CallEvent is defined using the following format: event-name (comma-separated-parameter-list)

card verification value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The code that credit card companies use to authorize credit card charges. For example, American Express uses a four-digit number on the front of the credit card, and Visa, MasterCard, and Discover use a three-digit number on the back.

cvv.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The code that credit card companies use to authorize credit card charges. For example, American Express uses a four-digit number on the front of the credit card, and Visa, MasterCard, and Discover use a three-digit number on the back.

mastercard securecode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The code that credit card companies use to authorize credit card charges. For example, American Express uses a four-digit number on the front of the credit card, and Visa, MasterCard, and Discover use a three-digit number on the back.

verified by visa.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The code that credit card companies use to authorize credit card charges. For example, American Express uses a four-digit number on the front of the credit card, and Visa, MasterCard, and Discover use a three-digit number on the back.

card validation code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The code that credit card companies use to authorize credit card charges. For example, American Express uses a four-digit number on the front of the credit card, and Visa, MasterCard, and Discover use a three-digit number on the back.

category axis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A chart axis that represents the category for each data point. It displays arbitrary text values like Qtr1, Qtr2, and Qtr3; it cannot display scaled numerical values.

category field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field that is displayed in the category area of PivotChart view. Items in a category field appear as labels on the category axis.

center of rotation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The point around which a shape or text block rotates.

centerline trap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The small overlap created where two differently colored objects that are close in luminance abut on a printed page.

constraint violation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A violation that occurs when the restriction criteria are not satisfied.

certificate revocation checking.translation: kiểm tra thu hồi chứng chỉ
certificate revocation checking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A way to see if a certificate used to sign a message is valid. Outlook can check the status of the certificate from the issuing certification authority's database.

changeevent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, an event in which a designated condition becomes true. A ChangeEvent is indicated by the keyword when followed by a Boolean expression in parentheses, for example: when (balance < 0)

check clause.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Code that enforces constraints on a table or column.

check constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A constraint that allows for business rules that span multiple tables. For example, the Order table could have a CHECK constraint that would prevent orders for a customer from exceeding a credit limit defined for the customer in the Customer table.

choice group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that is used to present a set of mutually exclusive choices. By default, a choice group contains two choice sections, one of which appears to the user as the default choice in the form.

choicepoint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The point at which transitions split into multiple, mutually exclusive branches, each terminating at a different destination state. One of the branches must be a default branch.

choke.translation: phần chồng lấp giảm màu đậm
choke.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small overlap that decreases the knockout of the lower of two differently colored, abutting objects.

classifier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An algorithm trained through machine learning to determine the class of an input.

classifierrole.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of collaboration role that is a slot for an object in a collaboration. It is represented by the class rectangle symbol with only the name compartment showing.

code mask.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The format that you define for a work breakdown structure [WBS] code or a custom outline code. The mask specifies the sequence and number of letters or numbers required for each level and the symbol separating the levels.

code pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Visual Basic for Applications, the window that is used to display, edit, and write module-level and procedure code.

collaboration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The act of working together in groups by sharing information and processes through the use of cloud computing.

collaboration diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An interaction diagram that shows, for one system event described by one use case, how a group of objects collaborate with one another.

color category.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A keyword or phrase with an associated color that helps you keep track of items, such as messages, contacts, and appointments. You can use color categories to easily find, sort, filter, or group items.

column area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of PivotTable view that contains column fields.

component object model add-in.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A supplemental program with the filename extension .dll or .exe that extends the capabilities of a program by adding custom commands and specialized features.

com add-in.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A supplemental program with the filename extension .dll or .exe that extends the capabilities of a program by adding custom commands and specialized features.

combination view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view containing two views. The bottom pane view shows detailed information about the tasks or resources in the top pane view. For example, the Gantt Chart view could be in the top pane and the Task Form view in the bottom pane.

committed resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A resource that is formally allocated to any task assignments they have within a project.

complex transition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, a relationship between multiple source and/or target states or action states.

visualization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical representation of data.

visual.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object that enables user interaction or input, often to initiate an action, display information, or set values.

component diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An implementation diagram that shows the structure of the code itself.

composite object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A high-level object made of tightly bound parts. A composite object is an instance of a composite class, which implies the composition aggregation between the class and its parts.

composite state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart diagram, a state that has been decomposed into concurrent (representing and relationships) or mutually exclusive (representing or relationships) substates.

conditional format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A format, such as cell shading or font color, that Excel automatically applies to cells if a specified condition is true.

connection type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The type of Web Part connection. For example, the Provide Row To connection type passes a row of data from one Web Part to another Web Part.

contact form.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view of an individual contact that contains all the information stored in the contact.

contact index.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of buttons used to move through contact items displayed in Address Cards or Detailed Address Cards view. The Contact index moves the focus to the first contact whose name begins with the selected character.

content database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu nội dung
content database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft SQL Server or WMSDE database that contains the content for one or more SharePoint sites.

continued notice.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A note at the beginning or end of a text box indicating that the text is continued from or continues on a different page.

contour.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The shape of how scheduled work for an assignment is distributed across time. Use a contour to control how Project schedules the work of a resource.

contract closeout.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The completion of the contract [such as fixed price or lump sum, cost reimbursable, unit price contracts]. Closeout includes resolving all outstanding issues and items, such as inspections or invoices.

cost rate table.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of information about a resource's rates, including the standard rate, overtime rate, any per-use cost, and the date when the pay rate takes effect. You can establish up to five different cost rate tables for each resource.

cost resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A resource that doesn't depend on the amount of work on a task or the duration of a task, such as airfare or lodging.

critical task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A task that must be completed on schedule for the project to finish on time. If a critical task is delayed, the project completion date might also be delayed. A series of critical tasks makes up a project's critical path.

crosstab report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Printed information about tasks and resources over a specified time period. There are five predefined crosstab reports in Project: Cash Flow, Crosstab, Resource Usage, Task Usage, and Who Does What When.

crow's foot.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specification language for describing data structures. You can use the Crow's Foot entity and relationship shapes to diagram the structure of databases.

custom color.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A color in the Visio application that is stored with a shape as an RGB or HSL value rather than as an index to the document's color palette. A custom color is saved only with the shape to which it is applied.

message number.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number that identifies a SQL Server error message.

custom form.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A form that you customize to better fit your needs.

custom task pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An .html file whose content is displayed in a window next to a form. Custom task panes can provide form-specific commands and Help content.

cyan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A color that is essential to the CMY color model and the CMYK color-mixing method.

dao.translation: Đối tượng Truy nhập Dữ liệu
dao.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A programming interface to access and manipulate database objects.

data access objects.translation: Đối tượng Truy nhập Dữ liệu
data access objects.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A programming interface to access and manipulate database objects.

data pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The area of the window that displays the result set of your query.

data point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual value plotted in a chart and represented together with other data points by bars, columns, lines, pie or doughnut slices, dots, and various other shapes called data markers. Data markers of the same color constitute a data series.

database replication.translation: sao chép cơ sở dữ liệu
database replication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of creating two or more special copies (replicas) of an Access database. Replicas can be synchronized, changes made to data in one replica, or design changes made in the Design Master, are sent to other replicas.

dataflow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data preparation artifact that ingests, transforms, integrates, and enriches big data by defining data source connections, ETL logic, refresh schedules, and more. In other words, a dataflow is a process that defines how the data should flow.

dataflow diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool for functional analysis that shows the general flow of information through a system or program.

data flow diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool for functional analysis that shows the general flow of information through a system or program.

date separator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A character that is used to separate the day, month, and year when date values are formatted. The characters are determined by system settings or by the Format function.

decision.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an activity diagram, a guard condition that indicates different possible transitions from an action state. If one of these transitions leads to another decision, that decision is represented with the traditional diamond shape.

default control style.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default property setting of a control type. You customize a control type before you create two or more similar controls to avoid customizing each control individually.

default font.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The font that a program uses by default to display text.

default property.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A property that you can set for a control so that each time a new control of that type is created, this property will have the same value.

default role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A setting associated with a particular user role. Users who are not assigned to an existing role are automatically assigned to the role that is specified as the default.

default unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The unit of measure used to display a value if no units of measure are explicitly specified.

deferred event.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, an event that must be postponed for later use while another activity is under way. You can show a deferred event for a state by including the event among the state's internal transitions.

delay.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time between the scheduled start of a task and the time when work should actually begin on the task.

sbcs.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A character encoding in which each character is represented by 1 byte. Single byte character sets are mathematically limited to 256 characters.

single-byte character set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A character encoding in which each character is represented by 1 byte. Single byte character sets are mathematically limited to 256 characters.

derived element.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An element, such as an attribute or association, that can be calculated or derived from other information. For example, an age attribute for the class Person can be derived if you know the Person's date of birth.

design grid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The grid that you use to design a query or filter in query Design view or in the Advanced Filter/Sort window. For queries, this grid was formerly known as the QBE grid.

destruction marker.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a collaboration diagram, a marker used to indicate object roles and association roles, or links, that are destroyed during the operation.

detail area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of PivotTable view that contains detail and total fields.

discriminator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A text label on a generalization path that indicates the name of a partition of the general class that the more specific class is in. The default discriminator is an empty string.

discussion board.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web site component that enables users to participate in topics of discussion by posting and replying to comments.

discussion comment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A remark or topic of discussion that is associated with a Web page or Microsoft Office file and is stored on a discussion server.

dithered.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Produced with the use of dithering.

double-precision.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Characteristic of a number stored in twice the amount (two words; typically 8 bytes) of computer memory that is required for storing a less precise (single-precision) number. Commonly handled by a computer in floating-point form.

drawing file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Visio file with a .vsd extension that contains a drawing.

aggregation wrapper.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A wrapper that encapsulates a COM object within another COM object.

drawing scale.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ratio of distance on the printed page to distances in the real world. For example, a drawing scale of 1 cm = 1 m means that 1 centimeter on the printed page represents 1 meter in the real world.

drawing type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Visio file (template) with a .vst extension that opens with the stencils, styles, and settings you need to create a particular type of drawing.

driving resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The resource whose assignment to a task determines the finish date of the task.

duration field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of field whose content is expressed as a duration of time. Examples include the Work, Duration, and Delay fields. A duration field includes the duration unit, such as hour, day, or week.

dwg.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard format used by CAD programs (such as Autodesk AutoCAD) to store drawing files.

early finish date.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The earliest date that a task could possibly be completed, based on early finish dates of predecessor and successor tasks, other constraints, and any leveling delay.

earned value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A measure of the cost of work performed up to the status date or current date. Earned value uses your original cost estimates saved with a baseline and your actual work to date to show whether the actual costs incurred are on budget.

echo.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of Access updating or repainting the screen while a macro is running.

effort-driven scheduling.translation: lên lịch biểu dựa trên nhân công
effort-driven scheduling.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default method of scheduling in Project; the duration of a task shortens or lengthens as resources are added or removed from a task, while the amount of effort necessary to complete a task remains unchanged.

elapsed duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time that a task will take to finish, based on a 24-hour day and a 7-day week, including holidays and other nonworking days. For example: emin = elapsed minute, ehr = elapsed hour, eday = elapsed day, ewk = elapsed week.

dynamic recovery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process that detects and/or attempts to correct software failure or loss of data integrity within a relational database management system (RDBMS).

snooze.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To delay an item, such as a reminder, an alarm, or a recommendation, by a specified time.

long parsing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In the SQL system there are two typical types of threads: - short thread: it is a process that use the resources for a short time and - long thread: it is a process that use the resources for a long time. long parsing: is the analysis of the threads that lived for a long time Note: the definition of short/long is based on the system calculation/statistic for each process.

strategic merger or acquisition evaluati.translation: Đánh giá Hợp nhất hoặc Sáp nhập Chiến lược
strategic merger or acquisition evaluati.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A template that addresses, from a Strategic Business Development perspective, the general activities that a company goes through to determine their business growth strategy. The roadmap includes understanding market position, evaluating trade-offs between mergers/acquisitions and internal development, evaluating M&A candidates and placing valuation on target companies.

candidate key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A column or set of columns that have a unique value for each row in a table.

lift chart.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A chart that represents the improvement that a mining model provides when compared against a random guess, and measures the change in terms of a lift score.

unary operator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An operator that takes only one operand, for example, the increment (++) operator.

responder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that reacts or responds to requests or events.

device independent bitmap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file format designed to ensure that bitmap graphics created using one application can be loaded and displayed in another application exactly the way they appeared in the originating application.

dib.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file format designed to ensure that bitmap graphics created using one application can be loaded and displayed in another application exactly the way they appeared in the originating application.

html viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: UI element consisting of a report toolbar and other navigation elements used to work with a report.

unbound object frame.translation: khung đối tượng không bị chặn
unbound object frame.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control you place on a form or report to contain an unbound object.

code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of Copilot prompts that helps users write code.

event viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component you can use to view and manage event logs, gather information about hardware and software problems, and monitor security events. Event Viewer maintains logs about program, security, and system events.

publication access list.translation: danh sách truy cập ấn bản
publication access list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The primary mechanism for securing the Publisher. It contains a list of logins, accounts, and groups that are granted access to the publication.

pal.translation: danh sách truy cập ấn bản
pal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The primary mechanism for securing the Publisher. It contains a list of logins, accounts, and groups that are granted access to the publication.

hyperlink base.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A path containing a document with hyperlinks that is used as the root of the hyperlinks in the document.

series data point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual value plotted in a chart and represented together with other data points by bars, columns, lines, pie or doughnut slices, dots, and various other shapes called data markers. Data markers of the same color constitute a data series.

series point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual value plotted in a chart and represented together with other data points by bars, columns, lines, pie or doughnut slices, dots, and various other shapes called data markers. Data markers of the same color constitute a data series.

storage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The interface that enables users to see what is consuming the storage space on their phone, displaying the space used by apps, games, media, settings, and more. It also allows moving content from phone to SD card.

toggle key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A keyboard key that alternates between turning a particular operation, function, or mode on or off.

outlook web app.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Office Web application that provides secure access to email, personal calendar, group scheduling, and collaboration applications on Microsoft Exchange Server with only a Web browser.

microsoft outlook web app.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Office Web application that provides secure access to email, personal calendar, group scheduling, and collaboration applications on Microsoft Exchange Server with only a Web browser.

localized version.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A version of a program that has been localized for other markets and/or translated into other languages.

parallel device.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that uses a parallel connection.

lpt device.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that uses a parallel connection.

validation rule.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A property that defines valid input values for a field or record in a table, or a control on a form.

r/w.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Able to be both read from and written to.

read/write.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Able to be both read from and written to.

dc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an Active Directory forest, a server that contains a writable copy of the Active Directory database, participates in Active Directory replication, and controls access to network resources.

domain controller.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an Active Directory forest, a server that contains a writable copy of the Active Directory database, participates in Active Directory replication, and controls access to network resources.

elevation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The vertical distance of a point or an object above or below a reference surface or datum. Generally, the reference surface is mean sea level.

elevation of privilege.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process by which a user obtains a higher level of privilege than that for which he has been authorized. A malicious user may use elevation of privilege as a means to compromise or destroy a system, or to access unauthorized information.

e-mail marketing service.translation: Dịch vụ Tiếp thị qua Email
e-mail marketing service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An online service for your Marketing Campaign that allows you to acquire and manage email lists, and to track the results.

embedded image.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A picture that is stored within a document rather than being linked to a source file outside of the document.

embedded picture.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A picture that is stored within a document rather than being linked to a source file outside of the document.

enterprise project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A project that is stored in Project Server to ensure information integrity. To make changes to an enterprise project, users with access permissions are required to check it in and out from Project Server.

enterprise resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A resource that is part of an organization's entire list of resources. Enterprise resources can be shared across projects.

enumerated field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of field whose content is selected from a list of predefined choices. For example, in the Accrue At field you can select the way resource costs are accrued from a list that includes Start, Prorated, and End.

error number.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A whole number in the range 0 - 65,535 that corresponds to the Number property setting of the Err object. When combined with the Description property setting of the Err object, this number represents a particular error message.

estimated duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A duration for which you have only enough information to determine a tentative value. So that its status is clearly visible, an estimated duration is clearly marked by a question mark immediately following the duration unit.

event address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An address similar to a URL that provides network access to an event, such as a live broadcast. Attendees go to this address to view the event from their computers.

expected duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The total span of active working time expected for a task, that is, the amount of time from the expected start to the expected finish of a task.

identifier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A text string that unambiguously refers to a hardware or software component under a certain context and can be used to access the data in that component.

extension point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A location within a use case at which an action sequence from another use case may be inserted. Within a use case, each extension point name must be unique. Extension points appear in a compartment at the bottom of the Use Case shape.

external data.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data that is stored outside of the application that is currently in use.

external data range.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A range of data that is brought into a worksheet but that originates outside of Excel, such as in a database or text file.

external dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A relationship in which the start or finish date of a task depends on a task in another project.

cross-project link.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A relationship in which the start or finish date of a task depends on a task in another project.

external predecessor.translation: tác vụ tiếp trước bên ngoài
external predecessor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A predecessor to a task in the current project that resides in another project, represented by a task that appears dimmed in the task list.

external successor.translation: tác vụ tiếp sau bên ngoài
external successor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A successor to a task in the current project that resides in another project, represented by a task that appears dimmed in the task list.

external task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A line item in a timesheet that does not correspond to a project task in Project Server.

favorite folders.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pane located on top of the Navigation Pane that has copies of your Inbox, Sent Items, and so on. You can add, remove, and arrange folders in this pane. Collapse or expand the pane by clicking the arrow in the Favorite Folders header.

field button.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A button that identifies a field in a PivotTable or PivotChart report. You can drag the field buttons to change the layout of the report, or click the arrows next to the buttons to change the level of detail displayed in the report.

attachment control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that allows users to attach files to their form when they fill it out.

file attachment control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that allows users to attach files to their form when they fill it out.

filter area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of PivotTable or PivotChart view that contains filter fields.

filter field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field in the filter area that you can use to filter data displayed in PivotTable or PivotChart view. Filter fields perform the same functions as page fields in Microsoft Excel PivotTable reports.

filter icon.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The icon that appears next to filtered data in a form.

final state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, a representation of the completion of activity in the enclosing state or action state. The final state is indicated by a bull's eye.

finish date.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The date that a project or task is scheduled to be completed. This date is based on the task's start date, duration, calendars, predecessor dates, task dependencies, and constraints.

fixed date.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A date to which a task is tied either because the date was entered in the Actual Start or Actual Finish field or because the task is constrained by an inflexible constraint.

fixed grid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Grid lines on the drawing page that stay the same distance apart when you zoom in or zoom out of a drawing.

fixed material consumption.translation: mức sử dụng vật tư cố định
fixed material consumption.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Absolute quantity of a material resource to be used to complete an assignment. A fixed consumption rate indicates that the amount of material used will be constant, regardless of changes to task duration or assignment length.

fixed-duration task.translation: tác vụ có lượng thời gian cố định
fixed-duration task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A task in which the duration is a fixed value and any changes to the work or the assigned units [that is, resources] don't affect the task's duration. This is calculated as follows: Duration x Units = Work.

flexible constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A constraint that does not tie a task to a single date. Flexible constraints are As Soon As Possible, As Late As Possible, Finish No Earlier Than, Finish No Later Than, Start No Earlier Than, and Start No Later Than.

floating.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Able to move freely as its own window. A floating window is always on top. Toolbars, menu bars, the toolbox, and palettes can float.

folder home page.translation: trang chủ liên kết với thư mục
folder home page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Internet Web page or intranet page that is associated with an Outlook folder. If a page has been associated with the folder and the option is set, the Web page appears in the Outlook window whenever you select the folder.

form area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The area of the InfoPath workspace that displays the form you are working with.

forms cache.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A location on a computer's hard drive to store a local copy of a form to improve performance when opening a form subsequent times.

free slack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time that a task can slip before it delays another task.

functional band.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shape that represents a functional unit, such as a department, in which process steps occur. You use either horizontal or vertical functional band shapes depending on the orientation you want for your diagram.

gantt bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical element on the chart portion of the Gantt Chart view representing the duration of a task.

generic resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A placeholder resource that is used to specify the skills required for a specific task.

gesture recognition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of the Pencil tool. As you begin to move the mouse, Visio quickly calculates the path the mouse pointer travels. If the path of the mouse is straight, the Pencil tool draws a straight line segment.

global file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Project file [Global.mpt] that contains information you can use for different projects. Information in a global file can include views, calendars, forms, reports, tables, filters, toolbars, menu bars, macros, and options settings.

goal seek.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A method to find a specific value for a cell by adjusting the value of one other cell. When goal seeking, Excel varies the value in a cell that you specify until a formula that's dependent on that cell returns the result you want.

grade.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A classification that allows users to identify attribute profiles as A, B, or C for the prediction being generated and enables users to efficiently plan targeted follow-ups.

factorial.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Expressed as n! (n factorial), the result of multiplying the successive integers from 1 through n; n! equals n x (n - 1) x (n - 2) x ... x 1.

grid lines.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The faint vertical and horizontal lines that appear in the drawing window when the grid is turned on. You can use grid lines to help position shapes precisely.

grid origin.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The point that defines the layout of grid lines on the drawing page. A vertical grid line and a horizontal grid line pass through the grid origin, and all other grid lines are drawn at specified intervals from these reference lines.

group transition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An outgoing transition segment with an outgoing arrow that begins on the state context and has no chained incoming transition.

guard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, a condition that specifies when an event can take place. Whenever its event fires, a guard is evaluated only once.

highlighting filter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A filter that displays all information and highlights the data that match the filter criteria.

html code fragment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: HTML code that you add to your Web page to create features such as a script, a counter, or a scrolling marquee.

html extension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature or setting that is an extension to the formal HTML specification. Extensions may not be supported by all Web browsers, but they may be used widely by Web authors. An example of an extension is marquee scrolling text.

hyperlink data type.translation: Loại dữ liệu siêu kết nối
hyperlink data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data type for an Access database field that stores hyperlink addresses. An address can have up to four parts and is written using the following format: A data type for an Access database field that stores hyperlink addresses. An address can have up to four parts and is written using the following format: displaytext#address#subaddress#.

idef1x.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specification language for describing data structures. Visio includes an IDEF1X template. You can use the IDEF1X entity and relationship shapes to diagram the structure of databases.

implementation class.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a static structure diagram, a class that defines the physical data structures and procedures of an object as implemented in a traditional programming language, such as C++. An object may have only one implementation class.

inflexible constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A constraint that ties a task to a date. The inflexible constraints are Must Finish On and Must Start On.

initial state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, a representation of the starting point of an object before any events included in the diagram have acted upon it. An initial state is indicated by a solid filled circle.

initiator role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A particular user role of your choice that is automatically assigned to users who open your forms for the first time, overriding any other role assignments.

ink entry mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The environment in which you can fill out a form by writing in ink.

ink guide.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shaded area that increases in size as you write in a form field with a tablet pen.

installable isam.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A driver you can specify that allows access to external database formats such as dBASE, Excel, and Paradox. The Microsoft Access database engine installs (loads) these ISAM drivers when referenced by your application.

installation folder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The location where a software is installed.

integer field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of field whose content is a whole number. Examples include the ID and Unique ID fields.

interaction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A representation of an event or activity of relevance to a business.

interim plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of task start and finish dates that you can save at certain stages of your project. You can compare an interim plan with the baseline plan or current plan to monitor project progress or slippage. You can save up to 10 interim plans.

internal self-transition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A transition segment that begins and ends on the same state context, and that has neither a chained incoming transaction nor a chained outgoing transaction. This transition is a combination of the group and history transitions.

international format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A phone number format for dialing any call from any location or with a calling card.

inter-project dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A way to show that your project, or a specific task in your project, requires a deliverable in another project. Your project and task dates are not affected by changes to the dates in the project you are dependent upon.

join line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A line that connects fields between two tables and shows how the data is related. The type of join indicates which records are selected for the query's result set.

junction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Process Engineering, the shape used to connect pipelines when one pipeline is split by another pipeline. The default junction shape is Junction. However, you can specify any shape on the document stencil as a junction.

kashidas.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The special characters used to extend the joiner between two Arabic characters. Used to improve the appearance of justified text by visually lengthening words rather than increasing the spacing between words. Can also function like a hyphen.

late finish date.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The latest date that a task can finish without delaying the finish of the project. It is based on the task's late start date, as well as the late start and late finish dates of predecessor and successor tasks, and other constraints.

lessons learned.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A review of best practices, project insights, and client information. As the project team disbands and new projects begin, reviewing the lessons learned lets you record information gathered and generated through the project.

leveling.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Resolving resource conflicts or overallocations by delaying or splitting certain tasks. When Project levels a resource, its selected assignments are distributed and rescheduled.

leveling delay.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time that an assignment or task is to be delayed from the original scheduled start date as a result of resource leveling or of manually entering a leveling delay.

link line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: On the Gantt Chart and Network Diagram, the line that appears between two tasks to indicate a task dependency.

link type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The type of task dependency. The four dependency types are Finish-to-start [FS], Finish-to-finish [FF], Start-to-start [SS], and Start-to-finish [SF].

linked style sheet.translation: biểu định kiểu được nối kết
linked style sheet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of cascading style sheet that exists in a separate file and is referenced throughout one or more Web pages.

linked picture.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A picture that links to a high-resolution image file that is stored outside of the publication file. If the linked picture is changed in an image-editing program, you can update the linked picture in the publication file.

linked project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A project that contains task dependencies to and from tasks in other project files. A link to a task in another project is represented with a placeholder or ghost task.

linking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows users to easily add links to content within other content (e.g. pages, sections, section groups) and provides quick navigation through these links. The feature operates in the same manner that links work in wikis.

list-separator character.translation: ký tự ngăn cách danh sách
list-separator character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A character, usually a comma or semicolon, that separates elements in a list.

local administrators group.translation: nhóm quản trị viên cục bộ
local administrators group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The group of users who have permission to perform administration tasks on the local server computer. The permissions for this group are set by using the administration tools for the operating system.

local formatting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Individual formatting attributes such as line width, fill color, or font size, that you apply to a selected shape by using a command on the Format menu, such as Line, Fill, or Text.

lunar calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A calendar that is based on cycles of the moon phase.

mandatory constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A constraint that requires every instance of an object type's population to play that role. With a disjunctive mandatory role constraint, each member of the object type's population must play at least one of the roles indicated.

mandatory property.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A property that requires a value when it exists as an object in the Directory Navigator and in the diagram. Mandatory properties that are defined for a class cannot be deleted.

mapped range.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A range in an XML list that has been linked to an element in an XML map.

master shape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shape on a stencil that you use repeatedly to create drawings. When you drag a shape from a stencil onto the drawing page, the shape becomes an instance of that master.

material label.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The unit of measure for a material resource, such as tons, cubic yards, or board feet.

material resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A supply or other consumable item that is used to complete tasks in a project.

maximum units.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The maximum percentage or number of units that a resource is available to be scheduled for any tasks. The maximum units value indicates the highest capacity at which the resource is available for work; the default value is 100 percent.

menu bar macro.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A macro containing AddMenu actions that you can use to create a custom menu bar or shortcut menu.

deployment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of distributing and installing a software program throughout an entire organization.

software deployment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of distributing and installing a software program throughout an entire organization.

message label.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An arrow label that indicates the message sent, its arguments and return values, and the sequencing of the message within the larger interaction (including call nesting, iteration, branching, concurrency, and synchronization).

message rule.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of criteria for updating a project file with the information in Project Server workgroup messages. For example, project managers can specify that updates from all workgroup members be automatically accepted.

metaclass.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a static structure diagram, a class whose instances are classes. It is shown in UML notation as a class with the stereotype metaclass.

microsoft script editor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An editor that is used to add text, edit HTML tags, and edit any Microsoft Visual Basic Scripting Edition (VBScript) code in a data access page. You can also view your page in the Script Editor as it would appear in a Web browser.

midtone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tone in a picture that is in the middle of the tonal range, between the lightest and darkest tones

mirror file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file separate from your database model diagram in which you can save the code from your model.

move mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The mode in which you can move columns in Datasheet view by using the left and right arrow keys.

multi-object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a collaboration diagram, a set of object roles on the ''many'' end of an association role. Using a multi-object shows that an operation addresses an entire set rather than a single object within the set.

multiple critical paths.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A series of tasks that must be completed on schedule for a project to finish on schedule. Identify and track multiple critical paths to be more effective in managing conditions that could affect your project's finish date.

multiple projects.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Several project plans that may or may not be linked or consolidated. If you are working on several projects at one time, you can compare information about critical paths, resource sharing, or priorities among all of the projects.

site collection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of Web sites that have the same owner and share administration settings. Each site collection contains a top-level site, can contain one or more subsites, and may have a shared navigation structure.

entered field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field in which you may type or edit information.

enterprise global template.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of default settings, such as views, tables, and fields, that are used by all projects across the organization. These settings exist within a special project in Project Server.

clickstream analysis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Clickstream data are information that users generate as they move from page to page and click on items within a Web site, usually stored in log files. Web site designers can use clickstream data to improve users' experiences with a site.

missed conversation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An incoming conversation that was not acknowledged by the user. Missed conversation notifications are saved and reported to the user.

accented character.translation: ký tự được đánh dấu trọng âm
accented character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A character that has a diacritic attached to it—such as “ñ.”

desktop.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The work area on a computer screen that simulates the top of an actual desk. The desktop contains the Recycle Bin and other icons (shortcuts to programs, files, folders, and various types of documents such as letters, reports, or pictures) that you can arrange on the electronic desktop just as you would arrange real objects on top of a desk.

desktop computer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that fits conveniently on a desk or table, and is not designed to be portable.

frame format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The way in which a network type, such as Ethernet, formats data to be sent over a network. When multiple frame types are allowed for a particular network type, the packets are structured differently and are, therefore, incompatible. All computers on a network must use the same frame type to communicate.

frame type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The way in which a network type, such as Ethernet, formats data to be sent over a network. When multiple frame types are allowed for a particular network type, the packets are structured differently and are, therefore, incompatible. All computers on a network must use the same frame type to communicate.

communications link.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The connection between computers that enables data transfer.

name autocorrect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that automatically corrects common side effects that occur when you rename forms, reports, tables, queries, fields, or controls on forms and reports. However, Name AutoCorrect cannot repair all references to renamed objects.

n-ary association.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a static structure diagram, an association among three or more classes (a single class may appear more than once). Each instance of the association is an ordered set of values from the respective classes.

navigation button.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A button that is used to move through records or through the pages of a document.

navigation mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The mode in Microsoft Access in which an entire field is selected and the insertion point is not visible. In Navigation mode, you can move between fields by using the arrow keys.
