neutral character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A character that does not have strong right-to-left or left-to-right language attributes.

non-enterprise project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A project that has not been published to Project Server, either because it is being saved by someone who is not a project manager on the project, or because there is not a valid connection to the server.

object data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A fundamental data type representing any object that can be recognized by Visual Basic. Although you can declare any object variable as type Object, it is best to declare object variables according to their specific types.

object flow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an activity diagram, a dashed arrow that indicates that an object is input or output by an action. An object flow arrow connects an object flow state either to a control flow arrow or to an action state.

object flow state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an activity diagram, a state that defines an object flow between actions. An object flow state signifies the availability of an instance of a classifier in a given state, usually as the result of an operation.

object in state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an activity diagram, an object that is manipulated by a number of successive activities. Each appearance of the object indicates a different phase in its life.

object lifeline.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a sequence diagram, a representation of the existence of an object at a particular time. If the object is created or destroyed during the time period the diagram represents, then the lifeline stops or starts at the appropriate point.

odbc database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database for which an Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) driver that you can use for importing, linking to, or exporting data is supplied.

offline cube file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file you create on your hard disk or a network share to store OLAP source data for a PivotTable or PivotChart report. Offline cube files allow you to keep working when you are not connected to the OLAP server.

off-page reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A 2-D shape that you can use in large flowchart diagrams to link to another page in the drawing.

ole container control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Visual Basic control that is used to link and embed objects from other applications in a Visual Basic application.

ole object data type.translation: Loại dữ liệu đối tượng OLE
ole object data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field data type that you use for objects created in other applications that can be linked or embedded (inserted) in an Access database.

online spotlight.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A section of the Business Contact Manager Home page where links to Help topics and other information are provided. The links are included in the Online Spotlight section to call the user's attention to the information.

open shape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shape such as a line, arc, or zigzag. You can format an open shape with line patterns and ends, such as by changing a solid line to a dashed line and adding an arrow to one end.

optimistic duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The best-case possibility for the total span of active working time expected for a task, that is, the amount of time from the optimistic start to optimistic finish of a task.

or constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An indicator of a situation in which any instance of a class can participate in only one association at one time. The constraint is shown as a dashed line connecting two or more associations, which must have a class in common.

outline code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A custom tag that users define for tasks or resources to allow them to show a hierarchy of the tasks in their project that is different from WBS codes or outline numbers. You can create up to 10 sets of custom outline codes in your project.

interoperability.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ability for two or more software applications to work together with little effort from the user.

outline number.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number that indicates the exact position of a task in an outline. For example, a task with an outline number of 7.2 indicates that it's the second subtask under the seventh top-level summary task.

overallocation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The result of assigning more tasks to a resource than the resource can accomplish in the working time available.

page pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of pane that displays the page that is selected in the thumbnail pane in a larger size, and enables portions of the page to be selected and copied.

page sheet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A ShapeSheet that represents a page.

page unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The size or distance on the printed page.

measurement unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The size or distance in the real world.

paper space.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a CAD drawing, a two-dimensional workspace analogous to a sheet of paper in which a drafter can arrange different views of a 3-D drawing.

parameterized class.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a static structure diagram, a template that describes a class with one or more unbound formal parameters. It defines a family of classes, each of which is specified by binding the parameters to actual values.

paste area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The target destination for data that has been cut or copied by using a clipboard.

patterns.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Principles that guide developers as they assign responsibilities to software classes and design system behavior. They are most useful when creating collaboration diagrams where messages imply responsibility.

peak units.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The highest level at which a resource is scheduled for all assigned tasks during a given period of time. Peak units are expressed as a percentage, number of units, or consumption rate.

percent complete.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field that you use to enter or display how much of a task has been completed. This value is expressed as the percentage of the task duration that has been completed.

percent work complete.translation: phần trăm công việc hoàn thành
percent work complete.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A percentage value that indicates the current status of a task, resource, or assignment, expressed as the percentage of work that has been completed.

periodic spline.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A closed spline with no defined endpoints.

personal view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view of a list, SharePoint document library, or Web Part Page that is available only to a particular user.

personalized web part.translation: Phần Web được cá nhân hóa
personalized web part.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shared Web Part that has been modified by a user in personal view. The changes made to a Web Part personalized in this way are visible only to the user who made those changes.

per-use cost.translation: chi phí mỗi lần sử dụng
per-use cost.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set fee for the use of a resource that can be in place of, or in addition to, a variable. For work resources, a per-use cost accrues each time that the resource is used. For material resources, a per-use cost is accrued only once.

pessimistic locking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of locking in which the page containing one or more records, including the record being edited, is unavailable to other users when you use the Edit method, and remains unavailable until you use the Update method.

pessimistic duration.translation: lượng thời gian không kỳ vọng
pessimistic duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The worst-case possibility for the total span of active working time expected for a task, that is, the amount of time from the pessimistic start to pessimistic finish of a task.

physical percent complete.translation: phần trăm hoàn thành thực tế
physical percent complete.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An alternative value to Percent [%] Complete or Percent [%] Work Complete that you enter per task. This may be useful when analyzing project performance through such means as variance analysis or earned value analysis.

pivottable form.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An interactive table that summarizes large amounts of data by using format and calculation methods that you choose. You can rotate its row and column headings to view the data in different ways, similar to an Excel PivotTable report.

placeable shape.translation: hình dạng có thể định vị
placeable shape.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A 2-D shape that is set to work with routable connectors and automatic layout. If a shape is set as placeable, a routable connector can detect and avoid crossing through it.

plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of information that describes the details of a subscription.

planned cost.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The latest cost of tasks, resources, assignments, and the entire project, which Project displays in the Cost field as cost or total cost.

point-to-point connection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A method of connecting shapes such that the actual point of connection stays the same no matter how you move the connected shapes.

portfolio.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of projects within an organization that may share common management of scope, budget, or resources.

positioning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Placing elements, such as text and graphics, on a page to let the page author control the exact location and layer order of a page element.

predefined bookmark.translation: thẻ đánh dấu tài liệu được xác định trước
predefined bookmark.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A bookmark that Microsoft Word automatically sets in each document.

procedure-level variable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A variable that is declared within a procedure. Procedure-level variables are always private to the procedure in which they are declared.

procure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To obtain the work and material resources required to complete a project.

progress line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A visual representation of the progress of your project, displayed in the Gantt Chart view. Progress lines connect in-progress tasks, creating a graph on the Gantt Chart indicating work that is behind and peaks indicating work that is ahead.

project assumption.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A factor that, for planning purposes, is considered to be true, real, or certain. Assumptions generally involve a degree of risk.

project calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The base calendar used by a project.

project constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A factor that will limit the project management team's options. For example, a predefined budget is a constraint that may limit the team's scope, staffing, and schedule options.

project summary task.translation: nhiệm vụ tổng kết dự án
project summary task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A task that summarizes the duration, work, and costs of all tasks in a project. The project summary task appears at the top of the project, its ID number is 0, and it presents the project's timeline from start to finish.

project triangle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The interrelationship of time, money, and scope. If you adjust any one of these elements, the other two are affected. For example, if you adjust the project plan to shorten the schedule, you might increase costs and decrease scope.

proposed resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A resource with a pending resource allocation to a task assignment that has not yet been authorized. This resource assignment does not detract from the availability of the resource to work on other projects.

pseudo index.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A dynamic cross-reference of one or more table data fields (columns) that permits an ODBC table (server table) without a unique index to be edited.

publish assignments.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To notify resources of new and changed assignments to tasks.

quality.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The degree of excellence, or the desired standards, in a product, process, or project.

quick click category.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A default color category that is assigned to an item when you click the Categories column for the item in your Inbox or other table view. You set this color category from the Categorize menu.

recurring task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A task that occurs repeatedly during the course of a project. For example, you might define the weekly status meeting as a recurring task.

recursive section.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that contains other controls, can be inserted within itself, and is bound to nested reference fields.

redlining.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of reviewing and marking up or adding comments to a drawing, document or other file.

reference mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A word, number, or abbreviation used to identify a unique instance of an entity object type.

reference port.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A port that defines the internal and external ports of an actor reference. Reference ports can be placed only on the outer border of an actor reference shape. They can be used as anchors for bindings.

resolve.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To record the outcome of a case and remove it from the queue of active cases.

referenced database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu tham chiếu
referenced database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The database to which the user has established a reference from the current database. The user can create a reference to a database and then call procedures within standard modules in that database.

refinement dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A kind of dependency that indicates a historical or derivation relationship between two elements with a mapping between them. A description of the mapping may be attached to the dependency in a note.

relay port.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of class port that defines the internal and external ports of an actor class. Can appear only on the border of an actor class. Relay ports relay incoming messages to a contained actor or outgoing messages from a contained actor.

remaining cost.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The estimated cost that is yet to be incurred for a task, resource, or assignment.

remaining duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time left to work on a task before the task is completed. This is calculated as follows: Remaining Duration = Duration - Actual Duration.

remaining work.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of work, in terms of a time unit such as hours or days, that is left to be completed on a task. This is calculated as follows: Remaining Work = Work - Actual Work.

repaint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To redraw the screen. The Repaint method completes any pending screen updates for a specified form.

report period.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The span of time during which you track and update a task that the workgroup manager has assigned to you. You can change the unit of time to days, weeks, or a single unit of time for the whole task.

report template.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Excel template (.xlt file) that includes one or more queries or PivotTable reports that are based on external data. When you save a report template, Excel saves the query definition but doesn't store the queried data in the template.

report type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of reports that all contain similar information.

resource calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A calendar that specifies working and nonworking time for an individual resource. A resource calendar differs from a base calendar, which specifies working and nonworking time for more than one resource.

resource information.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The categories of information shown in the Resource Sheet view that specify details about a resource, such as name, type, group, maximum units, and standard rate.

resource list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The resources that are available for assignments to tasks. The resource list may be stored in a single project file or shared with a resource pool.

resource pool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of resources that is available for assignment to project tasks. A resource pool can be used exclusively by one project or can be shared by several projects.

resource report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Printed information about a project's resources, which usually includes information about costs and the allocation of resources.

resource usage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An account of how many hours a resource is scheduled to work within a given time period, and thus an indicator of resources allocation within that time period.

revoked certificate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A certificate that has been cancelled by a certificate authority (CA) and is no longer valid.

rich black.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A more saturated black color created by using 100% process black and some percentage of one or more of cyan, magenta, or yellow.

risk management plan.translation: kế hoạch quản lý rủi ro
risk management plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A document defining how risk will be managed throughout the project. It can include identified risks, probabilities, contingency plans and methods for implementing them, and a strategy for allocating resources if a risk event occurs.

trace dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A kind of dependency that indicates a historical relationship between two elements that represent the same concept at different semantic levels or from different points of view.

usage dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A kind of dependency that indicates that one element requires the presence of another element for its correct implementation or functioning.

backward pass.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Calculation of late finish and late start dates for project activities, determined by working backward from the project's finish date.

base calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A template that can be used as a project and task calendar to specify default working and nonworking time for a set of resources.

baseline plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The original project plans [up to 11 per project] used to track progress on a project. The baseline plan is a snapshot of your schedule at the time that you save the baseline and includes information about tasks, resources, and assignments.

begin point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The selection handle at the beginning of a one-dimensional (1-D) shape. The begin point is marked by an X.

binary association.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a static structure diagram, a relationship between exactly two classes. You can add name and stereotype properties to a binary association. The point where a binary association connects to a class is an association end or role.

quick click flag.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A default flag that is assigned to an item when you click the Flag Status column in your Inbox or other table view. You set the default time, date, or other criteria for the flag from the Follow Up menu.

record selector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Excel pane that gives details on objects that match a string in a selected cell when multiple objects match, allowing the user to select the desired object.

workspace.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Loop element that lets the user see, group, organize, and stay up-to-date with all the Loop pages, files, and collateral for their team project in a single space.

dashboard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of reports or other data that is arranged in a panel format on a single page, or series of pages, in a web browser or SharePoint site.

diagnostics.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of Windows that checks for problems associated with network connections.

windows diagnostics.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of Windows that checks for problems associated with network connections.

domain name registry.translation: cơ quan cấp chứng nhận đăng ký tên miền
domain name registry.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An organization that controls a top-level domain. Although it does not own the relationship with the customer (a domain name registrar does), it keeps basic information about second-level domains in its database, such as the domain's registration date, expiration date, "lock" status, registrant, and registrar.

port.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To change a program in order to be able to run it on a different platform.

statechart diagram.translation: sơ đồ biểu đồ trạng thái
statechart diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A representation of a state machine, attached to a class or method, that describes the response of the class to outside stimuli.

state machine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graph of states and transitions that describes the response of an object of a given class to the receipt of outside stimuli. A state machine is attached to a class or method. A statechart diagram represents a state machine.

late start date.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The last possible date a task could be started if all predecessor and successor tasks also start and finish on their late start and late finish dates.

task calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The base calendar that you can apply to individual tasks to control their scheduling, usually independent of the project calendar or any assigned resources' calendars. By default, all tasks use the project calendar.

room structure diagram.translation: Biểu đồ Mô hình hóa Hướng Đối tượng trong Thời gian Thực
room structure diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical model of a system's components and their relationships (the structure), and of the system's response to events (its behavior).

real-time object-oriented modeling diagr.translation: Biểu đồ Mô hình hóa Hướng Đối tượng trong Thời gian Thực
real-time object-oriented modeling diagr.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical model of a system's components and their relationships (the structure), and of the system's response to events (its behavior).

off-axis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the presets for 3D rotation effects. When selected, specifies that the object will be rotated off-axis.

static structure diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A diagram that shows the static structure of a model; that is, the elements that exist (such as classes and types), the internal structure of the elements, and their relationships to one another.

cpi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A programming interface used to build and maintain unattended installation answer files and configuration sets by adding security fixes, changing drivers, and so forth.

cost performance index.translation: chỉ số hiệu suất chi phí
cost performance index.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ratio of budgeted costs of work performed to actual costs of work performed [BCWP/ACWP]. The cumulative CPI [sum of the BCWP for all tasks divided by the sum of the ACWP for all tasks] can be used to predict whether a project will go over budget.

shared database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu chia sẻ
shared database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database that is shared out to other users. These users create their own local copies, which are periodically synchronized with the shared database.

install.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: When referring to hardware, to physically connect the device to your computer, to load device drivers onto your computer, and to configure device properties and settings.

full screen.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Capable of using or being displayed on the full area of a display screen. Applications running in windowing environments, although they might use the entire area of the screen, commonly allocate different areas to different windows, any of which can be enlarged to fill the entire screen.

full-screen.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Capable of using or being displayed on the full area of a display screen. Applications running in windowing environments, although they might use the entire area of the screen, commonly allocate different areas to different windows, any of which can be enlarged to fill the entire screen.

everyone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of user account.

turn off.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To make an entity nonfunctional.

disable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To make an entity nonfunctional.

document inspector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows users to check and remove personal and other sensitive information from a document.

row area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of PivotTable view that contains row fields.

row heading.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The numbered gray area to the left of each row.

disc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Financial Excel function that returns the discount rate for a security.

ruler mark.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mark on the vertical or horizontal ruler that shows a unit or subunit of the measurement unit that is used for the publication.

screen review utility.translation: tiện ích xem thông tin trên màn hình
screen review utility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An accessibility aid for people who are blind or have learning disabilities, such as dyslexia. These aids make on-screen information available as synthesized speech or a refreshable Braille display.

scrolling region.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that contains other controls and that can display vertical or horizontal scroll bars. Scrolling regions are used for layout purposes only and are not bound to fields or groups in the data source.

security-enabled workgroup.translation: nhóm làm việc hỗ trợ bảo mật
security-enabled workgroup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Access workgroup in which users log on with a user name and password and in which access to database objects is restricted according to permissions granted to specific user accounts and groups.

selection net.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A means of selecting more than one shape at a time by dragging the Pointer tool to define an area that encloses all the shapes to be selected.

sequence diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An interaction diagram that shows the objects participating in a particular interaction and the messages they exchange arranged in a time sequence.

series field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field that is displayed in the series area of a chart and that contains series items. A series is a group of related data points.

server filter by form.translation: Bộ lọc Máy chủ theo Biểu mẫu
server filter by form.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technique that uses a version of the current form or datasheet with empty fields in which you can type values you want the filtered records to contain. The data is filtered by the server before it's retrieved from the database.

service bureau.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A company that provides various services related to publishing, such as prepress production, desktop publishing, typesetting, imagesetting, and optical scanning of graphics.

shape-to-shape connection.translation: kết nối hình dạng tới hình dạng
shape-to-shape connection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A method of connecting shapes. The actual point of connection might change when you move the connected shapes. You make shape-to-shape connections by dragging a connector from the center of one shape to the center of another shape.

campaign response.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A reply by a recipient of a campaign activity. Campaign responses can result from many channels, including email, telephone, and fax.

sharer file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file using resources from another file, which can be another project file or a file containing only resource information, called a resource pool.

side pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pane displayed on the left side of the Project and Project Web Access interfaces. In Project, the side pane contains Project Guide information; in Project Web Access, the side pane contains links.

signal event.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a statechart or activity diagram, an indication that one object has received a signal from another. A signal can be declared by using the keyword signal on a class in a class diagram.

single-mapped cell.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cell that has been linked to a non-repeating element in an XML map.

single-pane view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window in which only one view appears, such as the Task Sheet, Network Diagram view, Resource Graph view, or Calendar view.

size.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To change the dimensions of a shape by dragging one of its handles after it has been selected with the pointer tool.

skill code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of enterprise outline code that allows you to specify the skills that a resource has.

slippage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time that a task has been delayed from its original baseline plan. The slippage is the difference between the scheduled start or finish date for a task and the baseline start or finish date.

slow page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A page that takes a long time (30 seconds or more) to download in a Web browser.

special paper.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Paper that has colored, preprinted patterns or borders on it. You can use these papers to create a colorful and stylish look without a color printer or copier.

special skill.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Capability, knowledge, and aptitude that are relatively rare.

split task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A task that is scheduled for non-contiguous periods of time. For example, a two-day task that does not require contiguous work might be split so that the first day of work is scheduled for Monday, and the second day is scheduled for Thursday.

spread.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small overlap that extends the shape of the upper of two differently colored, abutting objects. A spread extends beyond the area that it knocks out.

spreadsheet component.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Office Web Component that provides the interactive functionality of a spreadsheet on a Web page. You can enter data, add formulas and functions, apply filters, change formatting, and recalculate.

sql server computer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer running Microsoft SQL Server with a configured database.

standard font.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default text font for worksheets. The standard font determines the default font for the Normal cell style.

standard rate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A base rate that you assign to resources [such as people, equipment, or material] and that Project uses to calculate resource cost totals.

state context.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A nested series of states, which represents the current state of a system.

static picture.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A snapshot of information, often from another document or program, that is not linked to the document or program in which the information was created.

status date.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A date that you set [rather than the current date] for reporting the time, cost, or performance condition of a project.

budget.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of money, on either a daily or monthly basis, that an advertiser allots for an entire advertising campaign.

status manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A manager responsible for tracking the task updates and assignments within a project. Separate from the project manager. Each task in a project can have a different status manager.

status report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A description of the status of a member's project work and related work.

stereotype.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A representation of a usage distinction. A stereotype is a subclass of an existing element with the same attributes and relationships as that element but with a different intent and possibly additional constraints.

string comparison.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The use of an operator to determine whether one string is greater than or equal to another string. Use the Option Compare statement to specify binary (case sensitive) or text (non-case sensitive) comparison.

subcategory.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A new category that is based on an existing category. For example, instead of tracking computers along with your other equipment, you might want to create a Computer subcategory from the Equipment category to track them as a separate group. Similarly, you can further organize a Restaurants category to include American and Chinese subcategories.

ruler subdivision.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The division between grid lines and between intervals of the ruler.

subphase.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A summary task that is nested within another summary task. With the Project outlining features, you can designate subphases.

subselect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To select individual shapes within a group.

subtask.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A smaller activity within a task.

summary task.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A task that is made up of subtasks and summarizes those subtasks. Use outlining to create summary tasks. Project automatically determines summary task information [such as duration and cost] by using information from the subtasks.

surrogate timesheet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A timesheet that you create in Project Web Access and submit on behalf of someone who works for you.

survey.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of questions designed to collect employee feedback, opinions, and perceptions on various aspects of their work environment.

swimlane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An horizontal or vertical line that divides a diagram into partitions and which is used to arrange related parts of a process.

synchronized copy.translation: bản sao được đồng bộ hóa
synchronized copy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A copy of a department that you create on a new page of a large organization chart, so that you can determine how your chart breaks across pages. When you create a synchronized copy, any changes you make appear in both.

system boundary.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a use case diagram, a boundary surrounding the use cases that indicates the system. You can resize the system boundary by dragging a selection handle on the System Boundary shape.

tag line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A brief, memorable statement that summarizes the purpose of an organization or emphasizes an important aspect of a product or service.

tagged value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A keyword-value pair that can be attached to any model element. The keyword is called a tag, and it represents a property applicable to one or many elements. Both the keyword and the value are strings.

task delegation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of one team member assigning a task to another team member in Project Server. When a task is delegated to another team member, that team member actually does the work on the task.

task dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A relationship between two linked tasks; linked by a dependency between their finish and start dates. There are four kinds of task dependencies: Finish-to-start [FS], Start-to-start [SS], Finish-to-finish [FF], and Start-to-finish [SF].

task id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number that Project automatically assigns to a task as you add it to the project. The task ID indicates the position of the task with respect to the other tasks.

task information.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Information provided about a specific task.

task report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Printed information about a project's tasks or activities. Task reports usually include information about start dates, work completed, and expected durations.

task type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A characterization of a task based on which aspect of the task is fixed and which aspects are variable. There are three task types: Fixed Units, Fixed Work, and Fixed Duration. The default task type in Project is Fixed Units.

task view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature that helps customers quickly switch between all the open apps and programs, and any desktops they create.

team web site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A customizable Web site with features that help a team work together. The default site has pages for document libraries, announcements, and team events. Only members, specified by the site creator, can use the site.

tent-fold card.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A top-fold card with four pages. Page one becomes the front cover, pages two and three are the inside pages, and page four is the back of the card.

text block.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The text area associated with a shape that appears when you click the shape with the text tool or select it with the pointer tool.

theme color.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of a set of colors that is used in a file. Theme colors, theme fonts, and theme effects compose a theme.

theme effect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An effect made up of a set of visual attributes that is applied to elements in a file. Theme effects, theme colors, and theme fonts compose a theme.

delivery protocol.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of communication rules used to route notification messages to external delivery systems.

theme font.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of a set of major and minor fonts that is applied to a file. Theme fonts, theme colors, and theme effects compose a theme.

thumbnail pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of pane that presents the current scanned document as one or more small images.

time event.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An event that occurs after a designated period of time or on the occurrence of a given date or time. A time event is indicated by the keyword after, followed by an expression that evaluates to an amount of time.

timephased.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to a task, resource, or assignment information that is distributed over time.

timescale.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The time period indicator at the top of the Gantt views, the Resource Graph view, the Task Usage view, and the Resource Usage view. You can customize it to show up to three tiers that can display various time units: top, middle, and bottom.

timesheet manager.translation: người quản lý bảng chấm công
timesheet manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person to whom your timesheet is submitted. If the user and the timesheet manager are the same person, an automatic approval will be performed upon submittal.

to-do list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of tasks that are not associated with a project schedule.

top-level web site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default, top-level site provided by a Web server or virtual server. To gain access to the top-level Web site, you supply the URL of the server without specifying a page name or subsite.

total row.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special row in a list or table that provides a selection of aggregate functions useful for working with numerical data.

totals row.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special row in a list or table that provides a selection of aggregate functions useful for working with numerical data.

total slack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time that a task can slip before it delays the project.

totals query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query that displays a summary calculation, such as an average or sum, for values in various fields from a table or tables. A totals query is not a separate kind of query; rather, it extends the flexibility of select queries.

tracer arrow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An arrow that shows the relationship between the active cell and its related cells. Tracer arrows are blue when pointing from a cell that provides data to another cell, and red if a cell contains an error value, such as #DIV/0!.

transition point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The start or endpoint of a transition segment.

transition to history.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An incoming transition segment that ends on an outer state context and does not have a continuing transition segment within the context.

trendline label.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Optional text for a trendline, including either the regression equation or the R-squared value, or both. A trendline label can be formatted and moved; it cannot be sized.

trusted location.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A folder or file path on your computer or a location on your intranet from which it is safe to run code. Default trusted locations include the Templates, Addins, and Startup folders, and you can specify your own trusted locations.

trusted publisher store.translation: danh sách nhà phát hành tin cậy
trusted publisher store.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of software publisher certificates used to digitally sign code, such as macros. Because you explicitly trust the software publishers, their code is allowed to run on your computer without needing to prompt for permission.

underallocation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The result of assigning a resource to work fewer hours than the resource has available.

unique permission.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A permission setting for using a list, library, or site that is different from the permission settings of its parent site.

uniqueness constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A constraint that prohibits repetition of individual data or combinations of data.

unit availability.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Amount of time, expressed as a percentage or a decimal number, that a resource can be scheduled for assigned work. It refers to the availability of a resource; for example, a resource may be available 50%, 100%, or 300% of full time.

unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unit of learning that addresses a portion of the content for a class and may include assignments, materials, and other lessons.

unit of measure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The type of measurement system used in a drawing. In formulas, used after a number to specify the unit of measure that the number represents.

up-down bars.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In line charts with multiple data series, bars that indicate the difference between data points in the first and last series.

use case diagram.translation: biểu đồ trường hợp sử dụng
use case diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A diagram that shows the external actors who will interact with your system and how they will use it. The diagram consists of a system boundary, actors, use cases, and use case relationships (communicates, uses, and extends).

value axis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A chart axis that displays scaled numerical values.

variable grid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Grid lines that change as you change the magnification of a drawing. When you zoom in, grid lines are closer together. When you zoom out, grid lines are farther apart.

variable material consumption.translation: mức sử dụng vật tư biến đổi
variable material consumption.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The time-based quantity of material resource to be used in an assignment. A variable consumption indicates that the amount of material that is used changes if the task duration or assignment length changes.

vertex.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A handle at intersections between segments, lines or curves that comprise a shape.

parse.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To break input into smaller chunks so that a program can act upon the information.

vertical ruler.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A bar displayed along the left side of a document window. You can use the vertical ruler to adjust the top and bottom page margins and the row height in tables.

view bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A screen element along the left edge of the Project window that provides buttons for the most commonly used views. The View Bar provides a convenient means of changing views by just clicking the icons that appear on the View Bar.

wall reference line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The line that extends from the wall begin point to the wall endpoint. Although the wall reference line is typically centered on the wall or aligned with one edge of the wall, you can locate it any distance you want from the wall.

webinbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message center in Project where a workgroup manager can view Web-based messages from workgroup members who are using Microsoft Project Central. The manager can update the project schedule based on the responses of workgroup members.

weighted duration.translation: lượng thời gian có trọng số
weighted duration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Weighted average of the expected, pessimistic, and optimistic dates and durations. By default, PERT analysis calculation gives heaviest weight to the expected duration, and lightest weight to the pessimistic and optimistic durations.

gregorian calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A calendar in widespread use. It was introduced in 1582 A.D. as a revision to the Julian calendar.

windows user account.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: All the information that defines a user to the operating system, including the user name and any required password, membership in groups, and the rights and permissions that are associated with the user.

workgroup id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A case-sensitive alphanumeric string that is 4 to 20 characters long and that you enter when creating a new workgroup information file by using the Workgroup Administrator. This uniquely identifies the Admin group for this workgroup file.

workgroup information file.translation: tệp thông tin nhóm làm việc
workgroup information file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file that Access reads at startup that contains information about the users in a workgroup. This information includes users' account names, their passwords, and the groups of which they are members.

workgroup manager.translation: người quản lý nhóm làm việc
workgroup manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person who creates and maintains the project schedule and uses workgroup messages to assign tasks to the workgroup members; also uses the workgroup features to update tasks in the project as members reply.

workspace site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subsite based on the Document Workspace or Meeting Workspace site templates.

xml element.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML structure that consists of a start tag, an end tag, and the information between the tags. Elements can have attributes and can contain other elements.

general entity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The combination of characters and symbols that replace other characters when an XML document is parsed, usually those that have other meanings in XML. For example, < represents the < symbol, which is also the opening bracket for a tag. A General Entity is an entity that is used within the XML document itself, as opposed to a parameter entity, which is only referenced in the DTD.

xml general entity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The combination of characters and symbols that replace other characters when an XML document is parsed, usually those that have other meanings in XML. For example, < represents the < symbol, which is also the opening bracket for a tag. A General Entity is an entity that is used within the XML document itself, as opposed to a parameter entity, which is only referenced in the DTD.

xml entity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The combination of characters and symbols that replace other characters when an XML document is parsed, usually those that have other meanings in XML. For example, < represents the < symbol, which is also the opening bracket for a tag. A General Entity is an entity that is used within the XML document itself, as opposed to a parameter entity, which is only referenced in the DTD.

yes/no field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of field with content set to either Yes or No. For example, the Recurring field indicates whether the task is a recurring task.

link.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A connection between an element in a hypertext document, such as a word, phrase, symbol, or image, and a different element in the document or in another location, a webpage, file, or script.

numeric picture switch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A switch (\#) or instruction that specifies how Microsoft Word will display the numeric result of a field.

format switch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A switch (\*) or instruction that specifies the capitalization, numeral style, and character formatting that Microsoft Word uses in a field result.

focus of control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a sequence diagram, the time period during which an object or actor is performing an action. Activation is represented by a thin rectangle.

activity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pattern of work performed together for a single purpose. An activity may use or produce work products and may be tracked by a work item.

disk.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A reusable magnetic storage medium. The floppy disk used today is the rigid 3.5-inch microfloppy that holds 1.44 MB. It is called floppy because the first varieties were housed in bendable jackets.

actual.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to information that shows what has actually occurred. For example, the actual start date for a task is the day that the task actually started.

allocation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In operating systems, the process of reserving memory for use by a program.

transition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An animation effect that specifies how the display changes as a user moves from one item (such as a slide or Web page) to another.

row selector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small box or bar that, when clicked, selects an entire row in table or macro Design view, or when you sort and group records in report Design view.

scene-coherent 3-d.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The camera angles and light settings that you can use to control the orientation, shadow, and perspective for grouped shapes.

sql-specific query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query that consists of an SQL statement. Subqueries and pass-through, union, and data-definition queries are SQL-specific queries.

stacking order.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The order in which shapes overlap other shapes on the page and the order in which shapes are selected.

use case.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a use case diagram, a representation of a set of events that occurs when an actor uses a system to complete a process. Normally, a use case is a relatively large process, not an individual step or transaction.

control flow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group of connected control flow elements that perform tasks.

critical path.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The series of tasks that must be completed on schedule for a project to finish on schedule. Each task on the critical path is a critical task.

underline.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To format a selection of text so that the text is printed with a line slightly below it.

deadline date.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A target date that indicates when you want a task to be completed and allows you to track the status of the task against that target without imposing a constraint on the schedule.

digitally signed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Having a digital signature.

overtime.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of work on an assignment that is scheduled beyond the regular working hours of an assigned resource and charged at the overtime rate.

pay rate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Resource cost per hour. Project includes two types of pay rates: standard rates and overtime rates.

phase.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group of related tasks that completes a major step in a project.

resource allocation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of distributing a computer system's facilities to different components of a job in order to perform the job.

conceptual model.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool used in the analysis phase of software development to help decompose a problem into individual concepts or objects and clarify the vocabulary of the domain.

critical path method.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A project management method of calculating the total duration of a project based on individual task durations and their dependencies.

cpm.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A project management method of calculating the total duration of a project based on individual task durations and their dependencies.

local computer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The computer that you are currently logged on to as a user. More generally, a local computer is a computer that you can access directly without using a communications line or a communications device, such as a network adapter or a modem.

local machine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The computer that you are currently logged on to as a user. More generally, a local computer is a computer that you can access directly without using a communications line or a communications device, such as a network adapter or a modem.

criteria.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Conditions you specify to limit which records are included in the result set of a query or filter.

lag time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A delay between tasks that have a dependency. For example, if you need a two-day delay between the finish of one task and the start of another, you can establish a finish-to-start dependency and specify a two-day lag time [has a positive value].

lines per inch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The measurement of the line screen frequency of a halftone screen that is used when printing a bitmap picture. For commercial printing, using higher lines per inch typically results in a more finely detailed picture.

lpi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The measurement of the line screen frequency of a halftone screen that is used when printing a bitmap picture. For commercial printing, using higher lines per inch typically results in a more finely detailed picture.

network diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A diagram that shows dependencies between project tasks. Tasks are represented by boxes, or nodes, and task dependencies are represented by lines that connect the boxes.

typed text.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Text that you enter by using a keyboard or that your Tablet PC converts from handwriting or speech.

xhtml.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A markup language that extends HTML and reformulates it as XML.

extensible html.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A markup language that extends HTML and reformulates it as XML.

roll up.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To collect subsets of data from multiple locations in one location.

resource view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view that displays resource information. Resource views include the Resource Sheet, the Resource Graph, the Resource Usage, and the resource forms views.

global shortcut menu.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A custom shortcut menu that replaces the built-in shortcut menu for the following objects - fields in table and query datasheets; forms and form controls in Form view, Datasheet view, and Print Preview; and reports in Print Preview.

bottom-up estimating.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An estimating method in which the base costs of individual work items or resources are calculated into task, resource, and project cost totals.

binding dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A kind of dependency that indicates a binding of parameterized class, or template, parameters to actual values to create a bound, or nonparameterized, element.

assignment units.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The percentage of a work resource's time, or units, that the resource is assigned to a task.

microsoft family safety.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of Windows features that provides parents and individuals with the ability to customize key aspects of the online experience in order to protect their children and/or themselves.

family safety.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of features designed to promote healthy digital and physical habits and protect individuals in a family group.

database engine tuning advisor.translation: Trình tư vấn Điều chỉnh Công cụ Cơ sở dữ liệu
database engine tuning advisor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The tool for tuning the physical database design that helps users to select and create an optimal set of indexes, indexed views, and partitioning.

embed code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A piece of HTML code that adds an object, such as a video, to an HTML page.

inbox folder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The folder that by default receives new messages.

inbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The folder that by default receives new messages.

stop list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specific collection of so-called stopwords, which tend to appear frequently in documents, but are believed to carry no usable information.

stop word list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specific collection of so-called stopwords, which tend to appear frequently in documents, but are believed to carry no usable information.

stoplist.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specific collection of so-called stopwords, which tend to appear frequently in documents, but are believed to carry no usable information.

stopword.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A word that tends to appear frequently in documents and carries no usable information.

stop word.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A word that tends to appear frequently in documents and carries no usable information.

pack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of components.

pack and go wizard.translation: Trình hướng dẫn Đóng Gói để Sử dụng tiếp
pack and go wizard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A wizard that packages a publication and its linked files into a single file that you can take to another computer to be edited, or to a commercial printer or a copy shop to be printed.

optional attendee.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A person who is not required to attend a meeting.

proposal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A formal bid for a job or sale of products.

project proposal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A suggested project plan. Proposals provide better high-level analysis, and enable you to apply your business processes to track potential projects.

seed number.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An initial value used to generate pseudorandom numbers.

seed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To add a database, either a blank database or a copy of the production database, to the storage group copy. This becomes the baseline database for the passive copy of the storage group.

visibility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A property of a replica that indicates which members of the replica set it can synchronize with and which conflict resolution rules apply. Replicas fall into three visibility types: global, local, and anonymous.

multiplicity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of entities that can exist on each side of a relationship.

cardinality.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of entities that can exist on each side of a relationship.

business activity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An action to be performed, such as a task, or a communication item that is sent or received, for example, email, phone calls, and appointments.

mailing address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A location to which products that have been ordered should be sent.

chunk.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specified amount of data.

numeric array.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An array composed of a collection of keys and a collection of values, where each key is associated with one value. The values can be of any type, but the keys must be numeric.

three-dimensional model.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer simulation of a physical object in which length, width, and depth are real attributes: a model, with x-, y-, and z-axes, that can be rotated for viewing from different angles.

model.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mathematical or graphical representation of a real-world situation or object. For example, a mathematical model of the distribution of matter in the universe, a spreadsheet (numeric) model of business operations, or a graphical model of a molecule.

3d model.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer simulation of a physical object in which length, width, and depth are real attributes: a model, with x-, y-, and z-axes, that can be rotated for viewing from different angles.

apply.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To put into use.

auto size.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: For an object, to resize automatically if the containing object or the overall window is resized.

secured connection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A connection established over a secure HTTPS channel.

ssl connection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A connection established over a secure HTTPS channel.

color editor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An interface control for setting the color of a brush or the color of a property on an object (such as Background).

color picker.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An interface control for setting the color of a brush or the color of a property on an object (such as Background).

content control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control designed to contain content such as placeholder or sample text or images that is updated by the user, or pre-defined lists of items from which users can select.

container element.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object that can contain one or more child objects.

drag-and-drop.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to an operation or feature that involves moving objects on the screen with a mouse, a similar input device or a eventually a finger.

cap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An upper limit or maximum value.

end cap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: For paths that contain unconnected ends, such as lines, the end of a stroke.

allotments used.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field in the contract line dialog where the user enters the number of allotments used.

outer glow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An effect that applies a halo of color around the perimeter of an object.

glow effect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An effect that applies a halo of color around the perimeter of an object.

glow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An effect that applies a halo of color around the perimeter of an object.

show.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item of original video programming, such as the video content created by Microsoft technical experts for docs.microsoft.com.

tail-log backup.translation: sao lưu nhật ký đoạn cuối
tail-log backup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A log backup taken from a possibly damaged database to capture the log that has not yet been backed up. A tail-log backup is taken after a failure in order to prevent work loss.

tangent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The gradient of a curve at a point. You can modify a curve that is part of a path object by using the control handles that represent the tangent of the curve.

transparency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The quality that defines how much light passes through an object's pixels.

ungroup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To release objects that have been combined together as a single object.

metafile.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file that contains or defines other files. Many operating systems use metafiles to contain directory information about other files on a given storage device.

message window.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window which displays a particular message for the user.

foreground page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The top (layer) page of a drawing.

background page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A page that you can assign to another page to create multiple layers in a drawing.

signature line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that allows users to digitally sign a form or document.

dialect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The syntax and general rules used to parse a string or a stream.

byte order mark.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Unicode character used to indicate that text is encoded in UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32.

bom.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Unicode character used to indicate that text is encoded in UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32.

database file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the physical files that make up a database.

batching.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of sending changes in small groups instead of in a one-shot transfer of the data in its entirety.

client.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity, such as a device or program, that connects to another entity over a network.

replica.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A copy of a database that is a member of a replica set and can be synchronized with other replicas in the set.

conflict detection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of determining which operations were made by one replica without knowledge of the other, such as when two replicas make local updates to the same item.

clock vector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of clock vector elements that represents updates to a replica. Any change that occurs between 0 and the tick count is contained in the vector.

tick count.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A monotonically increasing number that is used to uniquely identify a change to an item in a replica.

replica tick count.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A monotonically increasing number that is used to uniquely identify a change to an item in a replica.

synchronization session.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unidirectional synchronization in which the source provider enumerates its changes and sends them to the destination provider, which applies them to its store.

sync provider.translation: trình cung cấp đồng bộ hóa
sync provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software component that allows a replica to synchronize its data with other replicas.

synchronization provider.translation: trình cung cấp đồng bộ hóa
synchronization provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software component that allows a replica to synchronize its data with other replicas.

provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity which provides some services.

source provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A synchronization provider that enumerates any changes and sends them to the destination provider.

source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The information Copilot has access to that it can use to generate a response. This can be a plugin, file, email, other entities, and information in a specific page or section of a web portal.

destination provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A synchronization provider that provides its current knowledge, accepts a list of changes from the source provider, detects any conflicts between that list and its own items, and applies changes to its data store.

replica id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A value that uniquely identifies a replica.

replica key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A 4-byte value that maps to a replica ID in a replica key map.

synchronization application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software component, such as a personal information manager or music database, that hosts a synchronization session and invokes synchronization providers to synchronize disparate data stores.

knowledge.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Smart Lookup tab that provides quick answers to users’ searches when possible.

global identifier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unique identifier that is assigned to a data item. The identifier must be unique across all clients. A global identifier is a flexible identifier and so can be any format, but it is typically a GUID and an 8-byte prefix.

global id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unique identifier that is assigned to a data item. The identifier must be unique across all clients. A global identifier is a flexible identifier and so can be any format, but it is typically a GUID and an 8-byte prefix.

flexible identifier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An identifier that is assigned to various synchronization entities, such as replicas. The identifier can be of fixed or variable length.

flexible id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An identifier that is assigned to various synchronization entities, such as replicas. The identifier can be of fixed or variable length.

consistency unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The minimal unit of data synchronization. Because all changes that have the same consistency unit are sent together, synchronization can never be interrupted with part of a consistency unit applied.

range.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A block of cells selected for similar treatment in a spreadsheet. A range of cells can extend across a row, down a column, or over a combination of the two, but all cells in the range must be contiguous, sharing at least one common border.

change unit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The minimal unit of change tracking in a store. In change propagation, only the units that are changed must be sent; whereas, in conflict detection, independent changes to the same unit are considered a conflict.

conflict resolution method.translation: phương pháp giải quyết xung đột
conflict resolution method.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The method that is used to determine which change is written to the store in the event of a conflict. Typical conflict resolution methods are as follows: last writer wins, source wins, destination wins, custom, or deferred. For custom resolution, the resolving application reads the conflict from the conflict log and selects a resolution. For deferred resolution, the conflict is logged together with the conflicting change data and the made-with knowledge of the change.

clock vector element.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pair of values, consisting of a replica key and a tick count, that represents a change to a replica.

quality of experience.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A measurement of a user’s perception of the quality of an audio communication session. For example, in a voice communication, QoE monitors echoes and background noises such as hissing in the line.

qoe.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A measurement of a user’s perception of the quality of an audio communication session. For example, in a voice communication, QoE monitors echoes and background noises such as hissing in the line.

tile.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of a number of separately printed parts of an oversized publication, such as a banner or poster, that cannot be printed as a single sheet. Separate tiles can be assembled to recreate the whole publication.

page size.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The size of the finished page of a printed publication, after trimming.

paper size.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The size of the sheet of paper on which you print the publication, before trimming.

defined name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A word or string of characters in a formula that represents a cell, range of cells, formula, or constant value.

table name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A name for an Excel table, which is a collection of data about a particular subject that is stored in records (rows) and fields (columns).

change propagation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of applying changes from one replica to another.

full-screen mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to capture the entire screen, similar to pressing PRINT SCREEN.

portrait orientation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An orientation where the long dimension of a rectangular area (for example, screen, photo, or paper) is vertical.​

portrait.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The black and white filter that users can apply to a photo or video clip.

creator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A role within Microsoft Mesh app responsible for developing the environments in Unity, saving the templates and naming the worlds/collections.

author.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user who creates or edits a document.

exposure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: How vulnerable a person or an organization's assets are to various security threats and compliance risks.

exposure bias.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control on most digital cameras that lets you control the under -or over- exposure of the image.

exposure bias compensation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control on most digital cameras that lets you control the under -or over- exposure of the image.

exposure compensation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control on most digital cameras that lets you control the under -or over- exposure of the image.

ribbon tab.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: When a ribbon is divided into multiple views, any one of the views. Every tab contains functionally related commands and other controls that are organized in groups. Typically, ribbon tabs are labeled.

dynamic grid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Dotted lines that show the most desirable location for the center of the next shape being dropped on the page, based on where previous shapes have been placed.

star.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To mark an entity with a star.

rendering.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The action of combining the report layout with the data from the data source for the purpose of viewing the report.

poller.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component or interface that monitors the status of other components. It performs this function by repeatedly polling the other component to provide its current status.

dial.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A circular control with one or more sliders that a user moves to change values.

virtual surround sound.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The audio effect ​that creates the perception that there are many more sources of sound then are currently present. This is a well-known and industry term for the technique of creating a surround sound experience for users listening to audio with regular stereo headphones.

virtual surround.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The audio effect ​that creates the perception that there are many more sources of sound then are currently present. This is a well-known and industry term for the technique of creating a surround sound experience for users listening to audio with regular stereo headphones.

arithmetic overflow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A condition that results from calculating a column value that exceeds the column's specified size.

high whisker.translation: dải dữ liệu trung bình cao
high whisker.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The highest value that is not an outlier on a box plot chart.

icon.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphic whose form visually invokes the concept it represents.

adorner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that can add functional handles to a visual element that enable a user to manipulate the element in some way (resize, rotate, reposition, etc.).

outline effect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An effect that applies to the exterior border around each character of your text or shape.

fill effect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An effect that applies to the appearance of the interior of an enclosed text character or other shape.

shortcut key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any combination of keys that must be pressed simultaneously.

key combination.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A combination of keystrokes that can be used to perform a task that would otherwise require a mouse or other pointing device.

source file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file that contains the data that a program will process and store in a destination file.

rotation handle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The round handle that appears at the top of a selected shape that you can use to rotate the shape.
