builder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool that simplifies a task.

a record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource record in the Domain Name System that associates a specific IP address with a domain name. This is the record that contains the information that connects your domain name to your actual Web site content when people type your domain name into a browser.

address record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource record in the Domain Name System that associates a specific IP address with a domain name. This is the record that contains the information that connects your domain name to your actual Web site content when people type your domain name into a browser.

cname.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource record in the Domain Name System that associates a computer's true (canonical) name with any alias names also used by the computer. Some domain registrars use CNAME records to redirect or redelegate domain names.

canonical name record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource record in the Domain Name System that associates a computer's true (canonical) name with any alias names also used by the computer. Some domain registrars use CNAME records to redirect or redelegate domain names.

cname record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource record in the Domain Name System that associates a computer's true (canonical) name with any alias names also used by the computer. Some domain registrars use CNAME records to redirect or redelegate domain names.

cpc.translation: chi phí trên mỗi lần nhấp chuột
cpc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount an advertiser’s account is charged each time the advertiser’s ad is clicked by a search user or site visitor.

cost per click.translation: chi phí trên mỗi lần nhấp chuột
cost per click.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount an advertiser’s account is charged each time the advertiser’s ad is clicked by a search user or site visitor.

domain name registrar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The owner of the customer relationship with customers who buy second-level domains. There may be many registrars for a single top-level domain. Registrars maintain detailed customer information in their databases, such as the customer's contact address, telephone number, and email address. Customers usually manage their second-level domains at the registrar's Web site, and the registrar updates the registry database when necessary (for example, when a customer renews a domain name).

redirection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of telling your current domain name registrar to point your domain name to a new Web site. You do this by changing the name server information at your domain name registrar. When you redelegate a domain, your domain name registration remains with your current registrar and you will continue to be responsible for domain name fees and renewal with that organization.

domain redelegation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of telling your current domain name registrar to point your domain name to a new Web site. You do this by changing the name server information at your domain name registrar. When you redelegate a domain, your domain name registration remains with your current registrar and you will continue to be responsible for domain name fees and renewal with that organization.

redelegation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of telling your current domain name registrar to point your domain name to a new Web site. You do this by changing the name server information at your domain name registrar. When you redelegate a domain, your domain name registration remains with your current registrar and you will continue to be responsible for domain name fees and renewal with that organization.

iec.translation: Ủy ban Kỹ thuật điện Quốc tế
iec.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of two international standards bodies responsible for developing international data communications standards. The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) works closely with the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) to define standards of computing. They jointly published the ISO/IEC SQL-92 standard for SQL.

international electrotechnical commissio.translation: Ủy ban Kỹ thuật điện Quốc tế
international electrotechnical commissio.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of two international standards bodies responsible for developing international data communications standards. The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) works closely with the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) to define standards of computing. They jointly published the ISO/IEC SQL-92 standard for SQL.

mail exchange record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource record in the Domain Name System (DNS) specifying how Internet email should be routed using the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP). Each MX record contains a preference and a host name, so that the collection of MX records for a given domain name point to the servers that should receive email for that domain, and their priority relative to each other.

mx record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource record in the Domain Name System (DNS) specifying how Internet email should be routed using the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP). Each MX record contains a preference and a host name, so that the collection of MX records for a given domain name point to the servers that should receive email for that domain, and their priority relative to each other.

focal length.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The distance between the camera’s lens and the image plane.

metering.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In photography, the process of measuring the light in a scene to automatically adjust the exposure setting.

asmp.translation: đa xử lý không đối xứng
asmp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A form of multiprocessing in which a single processor acts as a master to a series of subordinate processors.

asymmetric multiprocessing.translation: đa xử lý không đối xứng
asymmetric multiprocessing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A form of multiprocessing in which a single processor acts as a master to a series of subordinate processors.

feedback.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The UI element that provides access to a site or process for submitting feedback on the product, product version, or service being used.

microsoft® office basic 2007.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A suite of Microsoft productivity software that supports common business tasks, including word processing, email, presentations, and data management and analysis.

affiliate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An organization or person that promotes Skype on its website or (re)sells its regular products.

drive.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hardware device that reads data from and writes data to floppy disks.

display.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A visual output device aimed at displaying various type of information.

enterprise.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An organization with more than 1000 employees and more than 500 personal computers.

search engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that searches for key words in documents, databases, Internet content or other files.

star query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query that joins a fact table and a number of dimension tables.

license.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To grant a person or entity the right to use a software product, as described in the terms of the license agreement.

records management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The role group that gives users permissions to create and manage organization-wide rules, also known as transport rules. Members of the role group can also track messages sent and received by users.

repository.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A central storage location that stores specific data, such as files under source control, container images, and so on.

contacts list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of entities such as people, groups, or organizations with whom users communicate.

contact list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of entities such as people, groups, or organizations with whom users communicate.

buddy list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of entities such as people, groups, or organizations with whom users communicate.

log off.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To terminate a session with a computer accessed through a communications line usually a computer that is both distant and open to many users.

log out.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To terminate a session with a computer accessed through a communications line usually a computer that is both distant and open to many users.

shortcut.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A link to any item accessible on your computer or on a network, such as a program or application, file, folder, disk drive, printer, or another computer.

keyboard shortcut.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A combination of keystrokes that can be used to perform a task that would otherwise require a mouse or other pointing device.

data source view.translation: chế độ xem nguồn dữ liệu
data source view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A named selection of database objects--such as tables, views, relationships, and stored procedures, based on one or more data sources--that defines the schema referenced by OLAP and data mining objects in an Analysis Services databases. It can also be used to define sources, destinations, and lookup tables for DTS tasks, transformations, and data adapters.

dsv.translation: chế độ xem nguồn dữ liệu
dsv.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A named selection of database objects--such as tables, views, relationships, and stored procedures, based on one or more data sources--that defines the schema referenced by OLAP and data mining objects in an Analysis Services databases. It can also be used to define sources, destinations, and lookup tables for DTS tasks, transformations, and data adapters.

terms.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Invoicing feature that allows users to choose from different terms for payment.

terms and conditions.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The contractual provisions and major terms agreed to by the parties to an agreement.

use.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To make use of a software product.

handset.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of a telephone that includes a speaker and a voice transmitter and that you hold with your hand up to your ear.

invitee.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A person who has been invited to an event.

reply.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Flipgrid, a video submitted in reply to another student video (usually by students, but in some cases also by guests, such as parents).

warning message.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message that appears on the screen to alert the user to something that must not be addressed.

switch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Logical Excel function that evaluates an expression against a list of values and returns the result corresponding to the first matching value. If there is no match, an optional default value may be returned.

interactive voice response.translation: hệ thống tương tác tự động bằng giọng nói
interactive voice response.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An automated telephone information system that interacts with a caller through fixed voice menus and real-time data from databases.

ivr.translation: hệ thống tương tác tự động bằng giọng nói
ivr.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An automated telephone information system that interacts with a caller through fixed voice menus and real-time data from databases.

end.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To stop communications or a network connection.

end a call.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To end a phone call.

ignore.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To mark an email conversation so that all current and future messages in the conversation are automatically moved to the Deleted Items folder.

caller.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person who is calling another person or place.

mdx formula.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The online analytical processing (OLAP) equivalent of an SQL query.

print.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In computing, to send information to a printer.

service plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of Exchange features, organization-wide resource limits, and permissions that are automatically configured or applied when a new hosted organization is provisioned in the service.

service plan template.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML file used to define the elements of a service plan or a mailbox plan.

sign-up address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An email address that a user can create to use when they buy products online or register for updates from a Web site and don't want to use their main email address.

word stemming.rule: Microsoft Terminology. For example, the word "swimming" is reduced to the stem "swim." Because the word "swam" can also be reduced to "swim," reductive stemming can create a list of all possible word forms that can be used by the query processor alongside the query string.

provisioning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. numa node.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group of processors with its own memory and possibly its own I/O channels.

change.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To modify the value of a property or attribute.

cti.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A company that provides reporting compliance services.

remote call control.translation: điều khiển cuộc gọi từ xa

quick steps.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that provides access to gallery of frequently-used actions with the touch of a button. Users can customize the gallery to execute a combination of operations in one click.

working hours.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user's work day hours as specified in Microsoft Office Outlook by the day of the week and the start and end times.

ring.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A servicing release cadence to receive development builds. Each ring is defined by a different release frequency and level of stability.

schema.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A definition of the structure of a particular type of data, which includes a definition of the allowed attributes and allowed relationships with other objects.

tags.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows the user to apply custom or default markers to items (e.g. Outlook messages or OneNote content) in order to categorize information for easy retrieval and sorting.

categories.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The section of the Store that shows subgroups of apps and games, grouped by intended use or function.

record set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data structure made up of a group of database records. It can originate from a base table or from a query to the table.

autofill.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To automatically complete content in a form based on previously entered information.

auto fill.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature that allows the user to fill cells with data that follows a pattern or that is based on data in other cells.

gated link.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A protected link between two or more objects. text messaging.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of creating and sending text messages between or to mobile phones and devices using the SMS protocol.

sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Kinect device.

biometrics.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of measurable characteristics used to label and describe individuals.

control gallery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A library of controls that support user interface development. Some of these controls function as containers for other controls or content, such as images and media.

little endian.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to a processor memory architecture that stores numbers so that the least significant byte is placed first.

reverse byte ordering.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to a processor memory architecture that stores numbers so that the least significant byte is placed first.

dump.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A duplicate of a program, a disk, or data, made either for archiving purposes or for safeguarding files.

location and other sensors.translation: cảm biến vị trí và cảm biến khác

element.translation: phần tử, yếu tố, thành phần

default location.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A location that you can set for your device that can be used by Windows, apps, and services when an exact location isn't available, such as on a desktop PC without GPS.​ ​

top results.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An arrangement of search results ordered by relevance using a special search algorithm.

bird’s eye.translation: Chế độ xem từ trên không

global positioning system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. gps.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A radio navigation system developed by the U.S. Department of Defense that uses a constellation of 24 earth satellites, which are monitored by ground-based control stations, to provide precise, continuous worldwide positioning and timing information.

ace.translation: ACE (Mục nhập kiểm soát truy cập)

access database engine.translation: Bộ máy cơ sở dữ liệu Access
access database engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Part of the Access database system that retrieves and stores data in user and system databases. The engine can be thought of as a data manager on which database systems are built.

action list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The list that appears when you click the arrow in the Action column of the Macro object tab.

data collection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of gathering information by sending and receiving HTML forms or InfoPath forms from Access.

database application.translation: ứng dụng cơ sở dữ liệu

database documenter.translation: Trình lập tư liệu Cơ sở dữ liệu

macro builder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The object tab in which you create and modify a macro.

multivalued field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A lookup field that can store more than one value.

relationships window.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object tab in which you view, create, and modify relationships between tables and queries.

section header.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The horizontal bar above a form or report section in Design view that displays the type and name of the section.

osp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A provider of online services like email, messaging, and others (example: Windows Live, Yahoo, Google).

roaming.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of maintaining connectivity outside of one's usual service or coverage area.

When you send an email, these placeholders are replaced with the data that meet the conditions that have been set in the workflow rule. For example, if you send an email to an account holder about a contract cancellation date, you can use a dynamic data field to automatically find and insert the correct cancellation date for that contract.

slug.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field that can be used in a workflow rule or template as a placeholder for specific values or text in an email. nul.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A "device," recognized by the operating system, that can be addressed like a physical output device (such as a printer) but that discards any information sent to it.

park.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To transfer a call to a holding point instead of holding the call at the phone device.

photo viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The mode of Windows Photo Viewer which consists of a top level window displaying one photograph at a time, with navigation controls.

slideshow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view of a set of photos that displays them one at a time, sequentially.

state/province.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A UI element where the state or province of the location of a record, such as an account or contact, is indicated.

single session-only disc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A recordable media (such as CD-RW) to which you can only write once without reformatting.

multi session-capable disc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A recordable media to which you can write several times without reformatting.

remote desktop virtualization host.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows server that is running Microsoft Hyper-V Server.

rdvh.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows server that is running Microsoft Hyper-V Server.

microsoft office isolated conversion env.translation: Môi trường Chuyển đổi Cách ly Microsoft Office
microsoft office isolated conversion env.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that is added to the Microsoft Office Compatibility Pack to open Word, Excel, and PowerPoint binary format files and securely convert them to the Office 2007 file formats.

moice.translation: Môi trường Chuyển đổi Cách ly Microsoft Office
moice.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that is added to the Microsoft Office Compatibility Pack to open Word, Excel, and PowerPoint binary format files and securely convert them to the Office 2007 file formats.

iterator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object or routine for traversing the items in a list, array, collection, or stream one at a time.

enumerator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object or routine for traversing the items in a list, array, collection, or stream one at a time.

suggested contacts.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that makes Outlook auto-complete lists available through the default Exchange mailbox.

credential manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A common credential store and interface that is used to save and manage user credentials, such as user names and passwords, so you can easily log on to Web sites and connect to other resources, such as computers.

vault.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The OneDrive folder that is protected using two-factor authentication.

personal vault.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of vault that contains Web passwords and secure notes that you can place on a USB flash drive and use on another computer.

erase.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To delete a user's account by suspending it for 14 day, after which time the account information and activity is wiped from the system, with the exception of the user's messages and files.

hard delete.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A process of permanently deleting something by removing it from the store or moving it to the dumpster when dumpster functionality is enabled.

data diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report type that maps shapes in a Visio diagram to data stored in lists, workbooks, or databases.

iterate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To execute one or more statements or instructions repeatedly. Statements or instructions so executed are said to be in a loop.

picture button.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control in a form that consists of an actionable image. At run time the user can click the image to run rules or actions similar to a button.

pass.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To forward a piece of data from one part of a program to another.

voice note.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A note that contains recorded information.

microsoft sticky notes.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft app that creates sticky notes that can be shared between devices, that cloud sync, that are stored on Exchange, and that provide contextual reminders and actions that can be performed based on the content.

sticky notes.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft app that creates sticky notes that can be shared between devices, that cloud sync, that are stored on Exchange, and that provide contextual reminders and actions that can be performed based on the content.

sticky note.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual piece of content that resembles a physical sticky note, is displayed across multiple apps and platforms, and that is created using Sticky Notes.

telework.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To work in one location (often at home) and communicate with a main office at a different location through a personal computer equipped with a modem and communications software.

telecommute.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To work in one location (often at home) and communicate with a main office at a different location through a personal computer equipped with a modem and communications software.

wrap around.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To continue movement, as with the cursor or a search operation, to the beginning or to a new starting point rather than stopping when the end of a series is reached. For example, the screen cursor might wrap around to the first column of the next line rather than stopping when it reaches the last column of the current line. Likewise, a program starting a search or replace operation in the middle of a document might be instructed to wrap around to the beginning rather than stop when it reaches the end of the document.

infopath form web part.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web Part that displays a browser-enabled InfoPath form.

microsoft sharepoint server state servic.translation: Dịch vụ Tình trạng Microsoft SharePoint Server
microsoft sharepoint server state servic.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SharePoint Server service that maintains temporary state information for InfoPath Forms Services.

form library url repair tool.translation: Công cụ Sửa URL Thư viện Biểu mẫu
form library url repair tool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that updates absolute URLs in form templates associated with SharePoint Form Libraries (i.e., InfoPath XSNs) as well as Universal Data Connection files.

powerpoint broadcast slide show.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that enables presenters in the rich client to broadcast a slide show to remote viewers watching in a Web browser. Throughout the presentation, the remote attendees will see the current slide being shown by the presenter.

broadcast slide show.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that enables presenters in the rich client to broadcast a slide show to remote viewers watching in a Web browser. Throughout the presentation, the remote attendees will see the current slide being shown by the presenter.

presentation section.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A labeled group of consecutive slides that helps the user navigate and organize presentations.

section.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A part of a form, report, or data access page such as a header, footer, or detail section.

insert screen shot.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows the user to insert the contents of an open window or a screen clipping into the current document without the need to utilize external applications.

microsoft office upload center.translation: Trung tâm Tải lên của Office
microsoft office upload center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A central hub for viewing pending uploads to http servers (mainly SharePoint) and correcting upload errors.

upload center.translation: Trung tâm Tải lên của Office
upload center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A central hub for viewing pending uploads to http servers (mainly SharePoint) and correcting upload errors.

office upload center.translation: Trung tâm Tải lên của Office
office upload center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A central hub for viewing pending uploads to http servers (mainly SharePoint) and correcting upload errors.

groove documents tool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool in Groove for storing and sharing files; primary use is intended to be as connection to SharePoint (via Site Client).

office auto-revisions.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that makes automatic versions of user documents during each autosave operation and allows the user to revert to previous copies of the document with ease.

mailtips.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that alerts users to potential issues with email recipients before the message is sent.

pair.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To establish a Bluetooth link or connection between two Bluetooth–enabled devices.

zip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The file name extension of a compressed archive file encoded in ZIP format, as by PKZIP.

document id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unique, persistent identifier assigned to a document or other item in SharePoint Server that allows it to be referenced and retrieved regardless of its location.

title bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A horizontal bar at the top of a window that displays the name of the window.

caption bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A horizontal bar at the top of a window that displays the name of the window.

document id lookup url.translation: URL Tra cứu ID Tài liệu
document id lookup url.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A URL that is based on a query using the Document ID rather than the physical location of the item.

document set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special type of folder that enables users to manage a deliverable or work product spanning multiple documents as a single entity.

drop off library.translation: Thư viện Tự động Định tuyến Tài liệu
drop off library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SharePoint document library where users can upload files that are then routed automatically to the correct library or folder in the site based upon rules defined by the site administrator.

precomposed character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A single character that represents a sequence of characters, usually a combination of a base character and one or more diacritics.

mini translator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that displays a definition or translation of a word or piece of text in a ScreenTip when the pointer is moved over the selection.

federated im.translation: có liên quan đến IM có liên kết
federated im.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to federated instant messaging.

federated instant message.translation: tin nhắn tức thời có liên kết
federated instant message.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An instant message with a federated contact.

internal im.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Instant messaging with internal users.

cellular network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A radio network that provides coverage for cellular telephone communications.

cellular.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A radio network that provides coverage for cellular telephone communications.

reflect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Teams check-in app that supports educators in building a classroom environment that recognizes the whole student by providing students with regular opportunities to identify, navigate, and share their emotions.

compilation error.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An error which occurs while compiling an application. These compilation errors typically occur because syntax was entered incorrectly.

windows homegroup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows feature that enables users to share pictures, music, videos, documents, and printers with other people on a home network.

bulk load.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An action of inserting a large set of rows into a table.

free-form mode.translation: chế độ Hình dạng tự do
free-form mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to draw an irregular line, such as a circle or a triangle, around an object that you want to capture.

free-form snip.translation: chế độ Hình dạng tự do
free-form snip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to draw an irregular line, such as a circle or a triangle, around an object that you want to capture.

full-screen snip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to capture the entire screen, similar to pressing PRINT SCREEN.

rectangle mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to draw a precise line, or rectangle, around an object that you want to capture.

rectangular snip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to draw a precise line, or rectangle, around an object that you want to capture.

window mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to select a window, such as a browser window or dialog box, that you want to capture.

window snip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Snipping Tool, a tool to select a window, such as a browser window or dialog box, that you want to capture.

transition style.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An abstract grouping of similar transition effects.

backstage view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A full-page UI view that exposes file-level functionality in Office applications. This is a companion feature to the Office Ribbon and helps users discover and use the features that fall outside of the authoring features on the Ribbon.

microsoft office backstage view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A full-page UI view that exposes file-level functionality in Office applications. This is a companion feature to the Office Ribbon and helps users discover and use the features that fall outside of the authoring features on the Ribbon.

backstage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A full-page UI view that exposes file-level functionality in Office applications. This is a companion feature to the Office Ribbon and helps users discover and use the features that fall outside of the authoring features on the Ribbon.

64-bit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or descriptive of the amount of data -64 bits, or 8 bytes- that certain computer systems or programs can process at one time.

attribute hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A flat hierarchy (typically having an All level and a member level) containing a single attribute. It is created from one column in a dimension table, if supported by the cube.

sql server analysis services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An online analytical data engine used in decision support and business analytics, providing the analytical data for business reports and client applications such as Power BI, Excel, Reporting Services reports, and other data visualization tools.

ssas.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An online analytical data engine used in decision support and business analytics, providing the analytical data for business reports and client applications such as Power BI, Excel, Reporting Services reports, and other data visualization tools.

analysis services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An online analytical data engine used in decision support and business analytics, providing the analytical data for business reports and client applications such as Power BI, Excel, Reporting Services reports, and other data visualization tools.

base 64 encoding.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A binary-to-text encoding scheme whereby an arbitrary sequence of bytes is converted to a sequence of printable ASCII characters.

base64.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A binary-to-text encoding scheme whereby an arbitrary sequence of bytes is converted to a sequence of printable ASCII characters.

data mining model training.translation: đào tạo mô hình khai thác dữ liệu
data mining model training.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process a data mining model uses to estimate model parameters by evaluating a set of known and predictable data.

data scrubbing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of building a data warehouse out of data coming from multiple online transaction processing (OLTP) systems.

log reader agent.translation: Tác nhân Bộ đọc Nhật ký
log reader agent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The replication agent which is used by all transactional publications. It moves transactions marked for replication from the transaction log on the publisher to the distribution database.

net-library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SQL Server communications component that isolates the SQL Server client software and the Database Engine from the network APIs.

nullability.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The attribute of a column, parameter, or variable that specifies whether it allows null data values.

game provider.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A digital distribution provider of games such as MSN Games, Yahoo Games, Steam, Stardock, GameTap, and so on.

test file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file used as part of a testing process to check the validity or correctness of a program or procedure.

accessibility checker.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that helps users of some Office applications to improve the accessibility of documents they create.

offline instant message.translation: tin nhắn tức thời ngoại tuyến
offline instant message.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An instant message that is transmitted while the sender or recipient is offline.

bipolar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In information transfer and processing, pertaining to or characteristic of a signal in which opposite voltage polarities represent on and off, true and false, or some other pair of values.

protected view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that offers improved security by loading a document in a read-only view, rather than in the full editor, for scenarios that pose a greater potential security risk.

presentation package.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A package containing everything you need to show one or many PowerPoint presentations on another computer. This package can be saved to a folder or burned to a CD.

trusted documents.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows the user to indicate that a document is trusted, and therefore can be opened without security notifications, so long as the file path and creation time of the document remain unchanged.

global variable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A variable that is accessible from anywhere in a program.

what's new.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The container inside a flex pane that provides users with information on new features and capabilities of applications utilizing product callouts and instructional content.

invited.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The contact picture label that indicates someone has been invited to do something, but has not responded yet.

photos.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The app that enables the users to view, organize, edit and share all of their photos from multiple sources.

device pairing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of establishing a Bluetooth link or connection between two Bluetooth–enabled devices.

pairing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of establishing a Bluetooth link or connection between two Bluetooth–enabled devices.

recorded tv library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows library that allows users to store, manage and share all their recorded TV items.

social networking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The use of Web sites and services that provide enhanced information and interaction capabilities with regard to people and resources.

bistable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of a system or device that has two possible states, such as on and off.

network traffic.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of visits to a website, or the amount of user activity on a website or on a network.

traffic.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of visits to a website, or the amount of user activity on a website or on a network.

live preview.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows you to preview the appearance of a formatting option or command before actually applying it to selected text or objects.

business process modeling notation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard notation for process management developed by the Business Process Management Initiative.

bpmn.translation: Ký hiệu và mô hình hoá quy trình kinh doanh
bpmn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical representation for specifying business processes in a business process model.

spelling service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web service that provides spelling checker functionality.

reparenting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of dynamically rearranging a hierarchy of SharePoint sites, typically used during a migration.

re-parenting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of dynamically rearranging a hierarchy of SharePoint sites, typically used during a migration.

composite application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An application that consists of both client-side and Web-based components.

down.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Not functioning, in reference to computers, printers, communications lines on networks, and other such hardware.

retention stage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A stage in a retention policy, consisting of an event-action pair.

windows powershell.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A command-line shell and task-based scripting technology that provides IT administrators comprehensive control and automation of system administration tasks.

powershell.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A command-line shell and task-based scripting technology that provides IT administrators comprehensive control and automation of system administration tasks.

context switch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The changing of the identity against which permissions to execute statements or perform actions are checked.

spp notification service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows service that provides software licensing activation and notification.

directaccess.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows feature that provides a direct connection to a corporate network for people working outside of the office. It is a superior alternative to VPN.

windows search.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A PC (desktop and beyond) search platform that allows search of the local hard drive plus network locations like SharePoint sites and the Internet.

disconnect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To break a connection.

intermittent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to something, such as a signal or connection, that is not unbroken but occurs at periodic or occasional intervals.

redial.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To call the last person called from a phone or device.

revenue.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An increase in an organization's assets or a decrease in an organization's liabilities during a reporting period.

detect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To find something which was hidden or not readily apparent.

dimension granularity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The lowest level available to a particular dimension in relation to a particular measure group. The "natural" or physical grain is always that of the key that joins the main dimension table to the primary fact table.

entity integrity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A state in which every row of every table can be uniquely identified.

smartshapes.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technology that lets you develop shapes that behave like the objects they represent in the real world. You do this by defining formulas that represent shape attributes, such as width and height, and shape behavior, such as what the shape does when a user right-clicks it.

accent process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression, a timeline, or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Works well for illustrating both Level 1 and Level 2 text.

alternating flow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show groups of information or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Emphasizes the interaction or relationships among the groups of information.

arrow ribbon.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show either related or contrasting concepts with some connection, such as opposing forces. The first two lines of Level 1 text are used for text in the arrows. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

balance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An amount that is the difference between the sum of debit entries and the sum of credit entries entered into an account during a financial period.

basic bending process.translation: Tiến trình Rẽ nhánh Cơ bản
basic bending process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Maximizes both horizontal and vertical display space for shapes.

synchronized multimedia integration lang.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based language being developed by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) that would enable Web developers to divide content into separate streams (audio, video, text, and images), send them to a client computer, and then have them displayed as a single stream. This separation reduces the time required for transmission over the Internet.

smil.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based language being developed by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) that would enable Web developers to divide content into separate streams (audio, video, text, and images), send them to a client computer, and then have them displayed as a single stream. This separation reduces the time required for transmission over the Internet.

basic block list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped blocks of information. Maximizes both horizontal and vertical display space for shapes.

basic chevron process.translation: Tiến trình Hình V Cơ bản
basic chevron process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression; a timeline; sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow; or to emphasize movement or direction. Level 1 text appears inside an arrow shape while Level 2 text appears below the arrow shapes.

basic cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to represent a continuing sequence of stages, tasks, or events in a circular flow. Emphasizes the stages or steps rather than the connecting arrows or flow. Works best with Level 1 text only.

basic matrix.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show the relationship of components to a whole in quadrants. The first four lines of Level 1 text appear in the quadrants. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

basic pie.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show how individual parts form a whole. The first seven lines of Level 1 text correspond to the evenly distributed wedge or pie shapes. The top Level 1 text shape appears outside of the rest of the pie for emphasis. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

basic process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow.

basic pyramid.translation: Hình Kim tự tháp Cơ sở
basic pyramid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show proportional, interconnected, or hierarchical relationships with the largest component on the bottom and narrowing up. Level 1 text appears in the pyramid segments and Level 2 text appears in shapes alongside each segment.

basic radial.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show the relationship to a central idea in a cycle. The first line of Level 1 text corresponds to the central shape, and its Level 2 text corresponds to the surrounding circular shapes. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

basic target.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show containment, gradations, or hierarchical relationships. The first five lines of Level 1 text are associated with a circle. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

basic timeline.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow, or to show timeline information. Works well with both Level 1 and Level 2 text.

basic venn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show overlapping or interconnected relationships. The first seven lines of Level 1 text correspond with a circle. If there are four or fewer lines of Level 1 text, the text is inside the circles. If there are more than four lines of Level 1 text, the text is outside of the circles. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

bending picture accent list.translation: Danh sách Điểm nhấn có Hình ảnh Rẽ nhánh
bending picture accent list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped blocks of information. The small circular shapes are designed to contain pictures. Works well for illustrating both Level 1 and Level 2 text. Maximizes both horizontal and vertical display space for shapes.

block cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to represent a continuing sequence of stages, tasks, or events in a circular flow. Emphasizes the stages or steps rather than the connecting arrows or flow.

chevron list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression through several processes that make up an overall workflow. Also works for illustrating contrasting processes. The Level 1 text corresponds to the first arrow shape on the left, while the Level 2 text corresponds to horizontal sub-steps for each shape that contains Level 1 text.

circular bending process.translation: Tiến trình Rẽ nhánh Vòng tròn
circular bending process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a long or non-linear sequence or steps in a task, process, or workflow. Works best with Level 1 text only. Maximizes both horizontal and vertical display space for shapes.

closed chevron process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression, a timeline, or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow, or to emphasize movement or direction. Can be used to emphasize information in the starting shape. Works best with Level 1 text only.

continuous arrow process.translation: Tiến trình Hình mũi tên Liên tục
continuous arrow process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a timeline or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Works best with Level 1 text because each line of Level 1 text appears inside the arrow shape. Level 2 text appears outside the arrow shape.

continuous block process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Works best with minimal Level 1 and Level 2 text.

continuous cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to represent a continuing sequence of stages, tasks, or events in a circular flow. Emphasizes the connection between all components. Works best with Level 1 text only.

continuous picture list.translation: Danh sách có Hình ảnh Liên tiếp
continuous picture list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show groups of interconnected information. The circular shapes are designed to contain pictures.

converging arrows.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show ideas or concepts that converge to a central point. Works best with Level 1 text only.

converging radial.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show relationships of concepts or components to a central idea in a cycle. The first line of Level 1 text corresponds to the central circular shape and the lines of Level 2 text correspond to the surrounding rectangular shapes. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

counterbalance arrows.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show two opposing ideas or concepts. Each of the first two lines of Level 1 text corresponds to an arrow and works well with Level 2 text. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

cycle matrix.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show the relationship to a central idea in a cyclical progression. Each of the first four lines of Level 1 text corresponds to a wedge or pie shape, and Level 2 text appears in a rectangular shape to the side of the wedge or pie shape. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

detailed process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used with large amounts of Level 2 text to show a progression through stages.

diverging arrows.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show ideas or concepts that progress outward from a central source. Works best with Level 1 text only.

diverging radial.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show relationships to a central idea in a cycle. The first Level 1 line of text corresponds to the central circular shape. Emphasizes the surrounding circles rather than the central idea. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

equation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mathematical statement that indicates equality with the use of an equal sign (=) between two expressions. In programming languages, assignment statements are written in equation form.

funnel.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A representation of progress toward a sales goal: identify leads, qualify, develop, propose, and close.

gear.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show interlocking ideas. Each of the first three lines of Level 1 text corresponds to a gear shape, and their corresponding Level 2 text appears in rectangles next to the gear shape. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

grid matrix.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show the placement of concepts along two axes. Emphasizes the individual components rather than the whole. The first four lines of Level 1 text appear in the quadrants. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

grouped list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show groups and sub-groups of information, or steps and sub-steps in a task, process, or workflow. Level 1 text corresponds to the top-level horizontal shapes, and Level 2 text corresponds to vertical sub-steps under each related top-level shape. Works well for emphasizing sub-groups or sub-steps, hierarchical information, or multiple lists of information.

hierarchy list.translation: Danh sách có Cấu trúc phân cấp
hierarchy list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show hierarchical relationships progressing across groups. Can also be used to group or list information.

horizontal bullet list.translation: Danh sách Dấu đầu dòng Ngang
horizontal bullet list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped lists of information. Works well with large amounts of text. All text has the same level of emphasis, and direction is not implied.

horizontal hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show hierarchical relationships progressing horizontally. Works well for decision trees.

horizontal picture list.translation: Danh sách Có Hình ảnh Dọc
horizontal picture list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped information with an emphasis on related pictures. The top shapes are designed to contain pictures.

horizontal labeled hierarchy.translation: Cấu trúc phân cấp có Nhãn Dọc
horizontal labeled hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show hierarchical relationships progressing horizontally and grouped hierarchically. Emphasizes heading or level 1 text. The first line of Level 1 text appears in the shape at the beginning of the hierarchy, and the second and all subsequent lines of Level 1 text appear at the top of the tall rectangles.

inverted pyramid.translation: Hình Kim tự tháp Lộn ngược
inverted pyramid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show proportional, or interconnected, or hierarchical relationships with the largest component on the top and narrowing down. Level 1 text appears in the pyramid segments and Level 2 text appears in shapes alongside each segment.

labeled hierarchy.translation: Cấu trúc phân cấp Có nhãn
labeled hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show hierarchical relationships progressing from top to bottom and grouped hierarchically. Emphasizes heading or level 1 text. The first line of Level 1 text appears in the shape at the beginning of the hierarchy, and all subsequent lines of Level 1 text appear to the left of the tall rectangles.

linear venn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show overlapping relationships in a sequence. Works best with Level 1 text only.

multidirectional cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to represent a continuing sequence of stages, tasks, or events that can occur in any direction.

nested target.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show containment relationships. Each of the first three lines of Level 1 text correspond to the upper left text in the shapes, and Level 2 text corresponds to the smaller shapes. Works best with minimal Level 2 lines of text. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

nondirectional cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to represent a continuing sequence of stages, tasks, or events in a circular flow. Each shape has the same level of importance. Works well when direction does not need to be indicated.

opposing arrows.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show two opposing ideas, or ideas that diverge from a central point. Each of the first two lines of Level 1 text corresponds to an arrow. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

organization chart.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A diagram that is used to show hierarchical relationships; for example, company management and employee structures.

picture accent list.translation: Danh sách Điểm nhấn có Hình ảnh
picture accent list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show grouped or related information. The small shapes on the upper corners are designed to contain pictures. Emphasizes Level 2 text over Level 1 text, and is a good choice for large amounts of Level 2 text.

picture accent process.translation: Tiến trình Điểm Nhấn có Hình ảnh
picture accent process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. The rectangular shapes in the background are designed to contain pictures.

picture caption list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped blocks of information. The top shapes are designed to contain pictures and pictures are emphasized over text. Works well for pictures with short text captions.

process arrows.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show information illustrating a process or workflow. Level 1 text appears in the circular shapes and Level 2 text appears in the arrow shapes. Works best for minimal text and to emphasize movement or direction.

process list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show multiple groups of information or steps and sub-steps in a task, process, or workflow. Level 1 text corresponds to the top horizontal shapes, and Level 2 text corresponds to vertical sub-steps under each related top-level shape.

pyramid list.translation: Danh sách Có hình kim tự tháp làm nền
pyramid list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show proportional, interconnected, or hierarchical relationships. Text appears in the rectangular shapes on top of the pyramid background

radial cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show the relationship to a central idea. Emphasizes both information in the center circle and how information in the outer ring of circles contributes to the central idea. The first Level 1 line of text corresponds to the central circle, and its Level 2 text corresponds to the outer ring of circles. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

radial list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show relationships to a central idea in a cycle. The center shape can contain a picture. Level 1 text appears in the smaller circles and any related Level 2 text appears to the side of the smaller circles.

radial venn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show both overlapping relationships and the relationship to a central idea in a cycle. The first line of Level 1 text corresponds to the central shape and the lines of Level 2 text correspond to the surrounding circular shapes. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

repeating bending process.translation: Tiến trình Rẽ nhánh Lặp lại
repeating bending process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Maximizes both horizontal and vertical display space for shapes. Does not emphasize directionality.

segmented cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or a sequence of stages, tasks, or events in a circular flow. Emphasizes the interconnected pieces. Each of the first seven lines of Level 1 text corresponds to a wedge or pie shape. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

segmented process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Emphasizes Level 2 text, since each line appears in a separate shape.

segmented pyramid.translation: Hình kim tự tháp Phân đoạn
segmented pyramid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show containment, proportional, or interconnected relationships. The first nine lines of Level 1 text appear in the triangular shapes. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts. Works best with Level 1 text only.

stacked list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show groups of information or steps in a task, process, or workflow. Circular shapes contain Level 1 text, and the corresponding rectangles contain Level 2 text. Works well for numerous details and minimal Level 1 text.

staggered process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a downward progression through stages. Each of the first five lines of Level 1 text corresponds with a rectangle. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

table hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show groups of information built from top to bottom, and the hierarchies within each group. This layout does not contain connecting lines.

table list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show grouped or related information of equal value. The first Level 1 line of text corresponds to the top shape and its Level 2 text is used for the subsequent lists.

target list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show interrelated or overlapping information. Each of the first seven lines of Level 1 text appears in the rectangular shape. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts. Works well with both Level 1 and Level 2 text.

text cycle.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to represent a continuing sequence of stages, tasks, or events in a circular flow. Emphasizes the arrows or flow rather than the stages or steps. Works best with Level 1 text only.

titled matrix.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show the relationships of four quadrants to a whole. The first line of Level 1 text corresponds to the central shape, and the first four lines of Level 2 text appear in the quadrants. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

trapezoid list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show grouped or related information of equal value. Works well with large amounts of text.

upward arrow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or steps that trend upward in a task, process, or workflow. Each of the first five lines of Level 1 text corresponds to a point on the arrow. Works best with minimal text. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

vertical arrow list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow that move toward a common goal. Works well for bulleted lists of information.

vertical bending process.translation: Tiến trình Rẽ nhánh Thẳng đứng
vertical bending process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow. Maximizes both horizontal and vertical display space for shapes. Places more emphasis on the interrelationships among the shapes than on direction or movement.

vertical block list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show groups of information or steps in a task, process, or workflow. Works well with large amounts of Level 2 text. A good choice for text with a main point and multiple sub-points.

vertical box list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show several groups of information, especially groups with large amounts of Level 2 text. A good choice for bulleted lists of information.

vertical bullet list.translation: Danh sách Dấu đầu dòng Dọc
vertical bullet list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped blocks of information. Works well for lists with long headings or top-level information.

vertical chevron list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow, or to emphasize movement or direction. Emphasizes Level 2 text over Level 1 text, and is a good choice for large amounts of Level 2 text.

vertical equation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show sequential steps or tasks that depict a plan or result. The last Level 1 line of text appears after the arrow. Works best with Level 1 text only.

vertical picture accent list.translation: Danh sách Điểm Nhấn có Hình ảnh Dọc
vertical picture accent list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped blocks of information. The small circles are designed to contain pictures.

vertical picture list.translation: Danh sách có Hình ảnh Dọc
vertical picture list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show non-sequential or grouped blocks of information. The small shapes on the left are designed to contain pictures.

vertical process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show a progression or sequential steps in a task, process, or workflow from top to bottom. Works best with Level 1 text, since the vertical space is limited.

stacked venn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SmartArt graphic layout used to show overlapping relationships. A good choice for emphasizing growth or gradation. Works best with Level 1 text only. The first seven lines of Level 1 text correspond to a circular shape. Unused text does not appear, but remains available if you switch layouts.

intelligent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Having the ability to make decisions based on predictions driven by machine learning analysis.

live.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The cloud service that enables users to communicate and collaborate with people online and access their conversations, photos, documents, contacts, appointments, settings, and services across PC, phone, and other devices.

programmable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Capable of accepting instructions for performing a task or an operation. Being programmable is a characteristic of computers.

serif.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Marked by the use of serifs. For example, Goudy is a serif typeface, whereas Helvetica is a sans serif typeface.

sharing session.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collaborative meeting or formal presentation in which a participant has chosen to share an application or desktop.

co-branding.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of customizing the look and feel of a product to support marketing or promotion of another company.

database catalog.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of a database that contains the definition of all the objects in the database, as well as the definition of the database.

taxonomy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A classification of words, labels, tags, etc. into groups based on similarities.

governance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of policies, roles, responsibilities, and processes that are established in an enterprise to guide, direct, and control how the organization uses technologies to accomplish business goals.

quadratic formula.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A formula giving the roots of a quadratic equation.

undeliverable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Not able to be delivered to an intended recipient. If an email message is undeliverable, it is returned to the sender with information added by the mail server explaining the problem; for example, the email address may be incorrect, or the recipient's mailbox may be full.

unread.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to information that a user has received but has not yet read.

dismiss.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To turn off a system notification such as a reminder, a new message alert or an alarm.

code element.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The minimum bit combination that can represent a unit of encoded text for processing or exchange.

missed call.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A telephone call the user has failed to answer.

policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A risk management policy that determines which employees are in-scope and which types of risk indicators are configured for alerts.

settings.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The interface in Microsoft Edge that allows users to customize their browser's appearance, privacy & security options, and other configuration options.

transfer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To ship inventory items from one location to another.

objective.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A (generally aspirational stretch) purpose that a team is working towards.

event.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any significant occurrence in the system or an application that requires a user to be notified or an entry to be added to a log.

keypad.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A calculator-style block of keys, usually at the right side of a keyboard, that can be used to enter numbers.

recovery password.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A password (or key) provided by Exchange Server (through OWA) that will be used during the process of resetting the PIN/password of the mobile devices.

ringer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The mechanical part that makes the phone ring to indicate an incoming call.

sim pin.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of personal identification number (PIN) for the SIM card, consisting of 4 digits, that is used to gain access to your mobile phone.

uppercase.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or characterized by capital letters.

multifunction device.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A piece of hardware that supports multiple discrete capabilities, such as audio, mixer, and music, on a single card. This device is sometimes treated as a bus that can be enumerated to locate the devices on that bus.

mfd.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A piece of hardware that supports multiple discrete capabilities, such as audio, mixer, and music, on a single card. This device is sometimes treated as a bus that can be enumerated to locate the devices on that bus.

attach.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To include an external document, a file, or an executable program with a message.

publishing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The administrative task of making remote resources available to its users, setting policies that control how users will connect, how they will find the remote resources, and what settings users will connect with.

seo.translation: tối ưu hóa công cụ tìm kiếm
seo.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The act of modifying the pages of a Web site so that its content is more easily discoverable by Internet search engines.

search engine optimization.translation: tối ưu hóa công cụ tìm kiếm
search engine optimization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The act of modifying the pages of a Web site so that its content is more easily discoverable by Internet search engines.

32-bit machine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that works with data in groups of 32 bits at a time. The Apple Macintosh II and higher models are 32-bit machines, in terms of both the word size of their microprocessors and the size of the data buses, as are computers based on the Intel 80386 and higher-level microprocessors.

32 bit machine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that works with data in groups of 32 bits at a time. The Apple Macintosh II and higher models are 32-bit machines, in terms of both the word size of their microprocessors and the size of the data buses, as are computers based on the Intel 80386 and higher-level microprocessors.

capacitor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A circuit component that provides a known amount of capacitance (ability to store an electric charge). A capacitor typically consists of two conductive plates separated by an insulating (dielectric) material. If other factors remain constant, capacitance increases as the plates are made larger or brought closer together. A capacitor blocks direct current but passes alternating current to an extent that depends on its capacitance and on the frequency of the current.

relational engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component of SQL Server that works with the storage engine. It is responsible for interpreting Transact-SQL search queries and mapping out the most efficient methods of searching the raw physical data provided by the storage engine and returning the results to the user.

device metadata retrieval client.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that provides an interface for acquiring rich metadata in order to support showing device detail information in the Device Center and the Device Stage.

dmrc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that provides an interface for acquiring rich metadata in order to support showing device detail information in the Device Center and the Device Stage.

metadata package.translation: gói siêu dữ liệu thiết bị
metadata package.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A .cab file that can only have one locale support and that provides all the hardware display components in order for your device information to be shown in the Control Panel.

device metadata package.translation: gói siêu dữ liệu thiết bị
device metadata package.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A .cab file that can only have one locale support and that provides all the hardware display components in order for your device information to be shown in the Control Panel.

re-image.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To uninstall all software on a computer and reinstall a new Windows image.

program compatibility troubleshooter.translation: bộ hướng dẫn giải quyết trục trặc tương hợp chương trình
program compatibility troubleshooter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An easy-to-use troubleshooter that helps find and fix program compatibility issues.

class module.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A module that can contain the definition for a new object where each instance of a class creates a new object and procedures defined in the module become properties and methods of the object.

vanity url.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An alternate URL that is typically shorter and/or easier to remember and communicate than the original address, or that incorporates a creative name that associates it with a particular product or subject matter.
