concentrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A communications device that combines signals from multiple sources, such as terminals on a network, into one or more signals before sending them to their destination.

data medium.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The physical material on which computer data is stored.

data segment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The portion of memory or auxiliary storage that contains the data used by a program.

dedicated server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer (usually quite powerful) that is used solely as a network server.

listing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entry in a list, catalog, or directory providing information about a Web site, product or item for sale, or service.

repeater.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device used on communications circuits that decreases distortion by amplifying or regenerating a signal so that it can be transmitted onward in its original strength and form. On a network, a repeater connects two networks or two network segments at the physical layer of the ISO/OSI reference model and regenerates the signal.

biometric sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of sensor that collects biometric data for a variety of applications.

motion sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A sensor that uses ultrasound, infrared, heat or vibration stimuli to detect movement.

retinal scanner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A biometric sensor that analyses your eye retina to recognize or authenticate identity.

electrical sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of sensor that can respond to an applied stimulus by generating an electrical signal.

mechanical sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of sensor that is used for mechanical measurement of force, scale, pressure, strain, etc.

environmental sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of sensor that tracks environmental changes such as temperature, atmospheric pressure, humidity, wind speed and wind direction.

proximity sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of sensor that can determine without physical contact if an object/person is nearby, or can be used to measure the distance between the object/person and the sensor device.

radio frequency identification sensor.translation: cảm biến nhận diện tần số radio
radio frequency identification sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of sensor (such as a proximity sensor) that uses radio frequency identification (RFID) for a numerous purposes, such as identification of physical items, automatic log on, location of people, etc.

rfid sensor.translation: cảm biến nhận diện tần số radio
rfid sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of sensor (such as a proximity sensor) that uses radio frequency identification (RFID) for a numerous purposes, such as identification of physical items, automatic log on, location of people, etc.

light sensor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A sensor that responds to a pre-defined amount of light.

downloads marketplace.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Internet site that provides a collection of products and services developed by Microsoft partners for Microsoft Office users.

office store.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Internet site that provides a collection of products and services developed by Microsoft partners for Microsoft Office users.

office marketplace.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Internet site that provides a collection of products and services developed by Microsoft partners for Microsoft Office users.

vss writer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component within an application that interfaces with the VSS platform infrastructure during backups to ensure that application data is ready for shadow copy creation.

unpair.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To remove a Bluetooth link or connection between two Bluetooth–enabled devices.

flip-flop.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A circuit that alternates between two possible states when a pulse is received at the input. For example, if the output of a flip-flop is high and a pulse is received at the input, the output "flips" to low; a second input pulse "flops" the output back to high, and so on.

bistable multivibrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A circuit that alternates between two possible states when a pulse is received at the input. For example, if the output of a flip-flop is high and a pulse is received at the input, the output "flips" to low; a second input pulse "flops" the output back to high, and so on.

fuse.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A circuit element that burns out or breaks when the current passing through it exceeds a certain level. A fuse protects a circuit from damage caused by excess current. It performs the same function as a circuit breaker, but it cannot be reset, so it must be replaced if it breaks. A fuse consists of a short length of wire of a specific composition and thickness; the thicker the wire, the more current it can pass before the wire melts and breaks the circuit.

compatibility view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view mode in Internet Explorer that determines whether content is rendered as if users were viewing it in a previous version of Internet Explorer.

native compiler.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A compiler that produces machine code for the computer on which it is running, as opposed to a cross-compiler, which produces code for another type of computer. Most compilers are native compilers.

package.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group of files that modify Windows features. Package types include service packs, security updates, language packs, and hotfixes. Examples of packages include LanguagePack, Windows Foundation, and FeaturePack.

operation code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The portion of a machine language or assembly language instruction that specifies the type of instruction and the structure of the data on which it operates.

newsletter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report containing news or information, can be printed or distributed electronically.

inline discussion.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A discussion comment that is associated with a particular paragraph, image or table.

potentiometer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A circuit element that can be adjusted to provide varying amounts of resistance. The twist-knob and slider-type volume controls on many radios and television sets are potentiometers.

managed service account.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A new type of domain account designed to provide applications such as SQL Server or Exchange with automatic password management and simplified service principal name (SPN) management.

msa.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The single set of sign-in credentials (email address and password) that provides user access to Microsoft products and services.

virtual account.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Local Service account that does not require password management. A virtual account is separate from the Local Service, Local System, and Network Service accounts. It uses the computer’s account and credentials when it needs network access in a domain environment.

non-broadcast network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11 wireless network in which Service Set Identifier (SSID) suppression is enabled.

hidden network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11 wireless network in which Service Set Identifier (SSID) suppression is enabled.

inprivate browsing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature that prevents Internet Explorer from storing data about your browsing session. This helps prevent anyone else who might be using your computer from seeing where you visited and what you looked at on the Web.

inprivate filtering.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature that blocks third-party web content that could potentially track someone's web activity.

tracking protection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature that blocks third-party web content that could potentially track someone's web activity.

certificate authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A form of IIS authentication in which IIS accepts client-certificates used to prove the client's identity. Using this form of authentication, IIS can optionally map a client certificate to a Windows user account by using an internal mapping table or Active Directory.

ticketing authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An authentication method where a Kerberos authentication server grants a ticket in response to a client computer authentication request that contains valid user credentials. The client computer then uses the ticket to access network resources.

elevated command prompt.translation: lời nhắc chỉ lệnh mức cao
elevated command prompt.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A command prompt that is run in a privileged administrator security context that allows actions that would normally be restricted. Without elevation, command prompts in Windows Client and Windows Server run in a restricted state.

storage location.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The position at which a particular item can be found: either an addressed location or a uniquely identified location on a disk, tape, or similar medium.

repository object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A COM object that represents a data construct stored in a repository type library.

windows live events.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Windows Live service for event planning and invitations.

relative name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The partial DNS domain name configured in individual resource records to locate and qualify the record within a zone. The relative name is joined to the front of the parent domain (domain of origin) for each resource record to form a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) within the zone. In DNS Manager, the relative name will correspond to fields that use record-specific name properties, such as the Host computer name field used in an address (A) resource record.

comment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A note or annotation that an author or reviewer adds to a document.

homegroup computer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that belongs to a homegroup.

homegroup troubleshooter.translation: Bộ hướng dẫn giải quyết trục trặc nhóm gia đình
homegroup troubleshooter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A troubleshooter that helps find and fix problems with viewing computers or shared files in a homegroup.

combine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To group together multiple windows of the same application under a single button on the taskbar’s taskband.

sharpen and soften.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows the user to digitally alter a picture to increase or decrease the sharpness of focus.

whole number.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number without a fractional component--for example, 1 or 173; an integer.

desktop gadget gallery.translation: Bộ sưu tập Tiện ích trên Màn hình máy tính
desktop gadget gallery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An organizer used to add, uninstall, and search for desktop gadgets.

cleartype text tuner.translation: Bộ chỉnh chữ màn hình ClearType
cleartype text tuner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that helps make the text on your screen easier to read for long periods of time.

volume snapshot device.translation: thiết bị chụp nhanh toàn ổ đĩa
volume snapshot device.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A virtual device created by System Restore that is needed to set a system restore point.

sequence check.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A process that verifies that data or records conform to a particular order.

interrupt.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A signal sent by a device to get the attention of the processor when the device is ready to accept or send information.

interrupt request.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A signal sent by a device to get the attention of the processor when the device is ready to accept or send information.

irq.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A signal sent by a device to get the attention of the processor when the device is ready to accept or send information.

home automation controller.translation: bộ điều khiển tự động hoá gia đình
home automation controller.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software or device that helps control your home smart devices automatically.

card reader.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An input device used chiefly for identification purposes that reads information that has been magnetically encoded, usually in two tracks, on a plastic card, such as a credit card or an employee badge.

subnotebook.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A notebook that is smaller in size and lighter in weight than a full-sized notebook, while retaining the same functionality.

mini-notebook.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A notebook that is smaller in size and lighter in weight than a full-sized notebook, while retaining the same functionality.

window gallery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A gallery containing thumbnail views of open application windows.

solid-state drive.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A primary storage device based on solid-state memory, such as flash memory, that provides nonvolatile storage with benefits of performance, reliability and power saving.

ssd.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A primary storage device based on solid-state memory, such as flash memory, that provides nonvolatile storage with benefits of performance, reliability and power saving.

ssd disk.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A primary storage device based on solid-state memory, such as flash memory, that provides nonvolatile storage with benefits of performance, reliability and power saving.

zero-day attack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A security attack that takes advantage of computer security holes for which no solution is yet available.

zero day attack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A security attack that takes advantage of computer security holes for which no solution is yet available.

0-day attack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A security attack that takes advantage of computer security holes for which no solution is yet available.

fulfillment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of delivering goods and services ordered by a consumer. Fulfillment involves establishing a reliable procedure for tracking orders and delivering products.

corrupted.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Damaged. Mostly used in regard to files or data.

peer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any of the devices on a layered communications network that operate on the same protocol level.

skin.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A customized user interface that overlays an existing user interface. A skin customizes the look of the program but does not affect its functionality. Programs that allow the use of skins usually make standards available for the creation and distribution of new skins.

backup and restore.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of maintaining backup files and putting them back onto the source medium if necessary.

click-to-run.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A streaming technology that quickly installs Office over the Internet, internal networks, local file systems, or from offline media.

click-to-run technology.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A streaming technology that quickly installs Office over the Internet, internal networks, local file systems, or from offline media.

content delivery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of caching the pages of a Web site on geographically dispersed servers to enable faster delivery of Web pages. When a page is requested at a URL that is content-delivery enabled, the content-delivery network routes the user's request to a cache server closer to the user. Content delivery frequently is used for high-traffic Web sites or for specific high-traffic events.

content caching.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of caching the pages of a Web site on geographically dispersed servers to enable faster delivery of Web pages. When a page is requested at a URL that is content-delivery enabled, the content-delivery network routes the user's request to a cache server closer to the user. Content delivery frequently is used for high-traffic Web sites or for specific high-traffic events.

content distribution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of caching the pages of a Web site on geographically dispersed servers to enable faster delivery of Web pages. When a page is requested at a URL that is content-delivery enabled, the content-delivery network routes the user's request to a cache server closer to the user. Content delivery frequently is used for high-traffic Web sites or for specific high-traffic events.

process diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A diagram that shows the relationship of items in a list. It is primarily used when the items are sequential in nature.

error handling.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of dealing with errors (or exceptions) as they arise during the running of a program. Some programming languages, such as C++, Ada, and Eiffel, have features that aid in error handling.

catalog merge.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of combining information from a data source with a template to create pages that display multiple records per page.

information retrieval.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of finding, organizing, and displaying information, particularly by electronic means.

initialization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of assigning initial values to variables and data structures in a program.

attribute flow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An authoritative source for an attribute value that can flow its value to other destination directories and systems.

microsoft media foundation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A COM-based multimedia platform and infrastructure for digital media in Microsoft Windows. It focuses on content protection, audio and video quality, and interoperability for digital rights management (DRM).

media foundation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A COM-based multimedia platform and infrastructure for digital media in Microsoft Windows. It focuses on content protection, audio and video quality, and interoperability for digital rights management (DRM).

form control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual box or button with which users enter information on an electronic form.

a11y.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A quality of a product to be directly or indirectly usable by individuals with disabilities.

accessibility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A quality of a product to be directly or indirectly usable by individuals with disabilities.

group calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The shared calendar that you can create in Office for a group of users to schedule events, track milestones, create meetings, and engage in conversations around events. Users can add events from a group calendar to their personal calendars.

child-friendly site.translation: trang web thân thiện với trẻ em
child-friendly site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A website whose content is understandable and usable by kids and that is appropriate for them. The language is typically aimed at a grade-school reading level, and the concepts presented are accessible to younger minds.

kid-friendly site.translation: trang web thân thiện với trẻ em
kid-friendly site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A website whose content is understandable and usable by kids and that is appropriate for them. The language is typically aimed at a grade-school reading level, and the concepts presented are accessible to younger minds.

child-friendly website.translation: trang web thân thiện với trẻ em
child-friendly website.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A website whose content is understandable and usable by kids and that is appropriate for them. The language is typically aimed at a grade-school reading level, and the concepts presented are accessible to younger minds.

kid-friendly website.translation: trang web thân thiện với trẻ em
kid-friendly website.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A website whose content is understandable and usable by kids and that is appropriate for them. The language is typically aimed at a grade-school reading level, and the concepts presented are accessible to younger minds.

web filtering.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A method of blocking access to websites based on their content. For example, In Windows Live Family Safety, parents can specify a filtering level, such as Strict or Basic, for their child.

group owner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A person authorized to manage and make certain changes to a group, such as to approve a membership request.

subscription file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An audio or video file that you rent from an online store, typically for a monthly fee.

maintenance troubleshooter.translation: Bộ hướng dẫn giải quyết trục trặc bảo trì
maintenance troubleshooter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A troubleshooter that performs common maintenance tasks in Windows, such as cleaning up unused files and shortcuts.

hardware and devices troubleshooter.translation: Bộ hướng dẫn giải quyết trục trặc phần cứng và thiết bị
hardware and devices troubleshooter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A troubleshooter that helps find and fix problems about hardware and devices.

search connector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A search location exposed via .osdx templates and made possible via the OpenSearch technology. It connects the local search indexer to a remote index and provides the end user with the ability to search for files on a Web site or on an intranet site from within Windows.

microsoft update solution center.translation: Trung tâm Giải pháp Microsoft Update
microsoft update solution center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web site from Microsoft which provides solutions for the top issues about Windows Update or Microsoft Update, and enables you to contact a support professional.

management console.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network-enabled host running Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) management software. This software requests information from SNMP agents.

management system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network-enabled host running Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) management software. This software requests information from SNMP agents.

problem solving.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of devising and implementing a strategy for finding a solution or for transforming a less desirable condition into a more desirable one.

data macros.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows users to build business logic in a new and easy-to-use authoring environment. The declarative, macro-style logic will run on client and server and includes both UI-level and data-level actions.

slicers.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that provides one-click filtering controls that make it easy to narrow down the portion of a data set that's being looked at.

sparkline.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A miniature chart that can be inserted into text or embedded within a cell on a worksheet to illustrate highs, lows, and trends in your data.

schedule view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Outlook Calendar view in which each calendar is listed vertically (not side-by-side). This view is optimized for viewing a schedule for a group and scheduling a meeting for a group.

picture presentation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that converts each slide in a presentation into a single image and rebuilds a new, compressed PPT presentation that can easily be shared, but not edited.

type checking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process performed by a compiler or interpreter to make sure that when a variable is used, it is treated as having the same data type as it was declared to have.

macro designer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that helps users to define logic for Access forms and tables that run in the browser.

macro manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A dialog that shows all the data macros in the database. Data macros can be deleted or renamed here.

marketing event planning and execution.translation: Lập kế hoạch và Thực thi Sự kiện Tiếp thị
marketing event planning and execution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A template that outlines the main categories that you should consider when beginning to plan a marketing event. Use this template to assist you in walking through key event elements while you are in the planning stages.

macro catalog.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A catalog that is part of the Macro Designer and contains all available macros and actions.

excel mobile viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A viewer that allows users to display Excel workbooks on a phone’s browser. A file is rendered as an HTML page with sufficient fidelity to convey important data or charts and illustrations.

word mobile viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A viewer that allows users to display Word documents on a phone’s browser. A file is rendered as an HTML page with sufficient fidelity to convey text and images on a small screen.

smartart graphic picture layout.translation: Bố cục Ảnh đồ họa SmartArt
smartart graphic picture layout.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that automates the task of positioning images and combining them with text in documents. It produces attractive, editable designs that highlight photos and accompanying text and make it easy for novices to produce compelling, high quality photo layouts.

smartart picture layout.translation: Bố cục Ảnh đồ họa SmartArt
smartart picture layout.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that automates the task of positioning images and combining them with text in documents. It produces attractive, editable designs that highlight photos and accompanying text and make it easy for novices to produce compelling, high quality photo layouts.

compact row axis.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that enables the user to compact or collapse rows when viewing several levels of data.

line pencil.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pencil tool that simulates the look and feel of drawing lines with a pencil.

pencil.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool that allows users to use ink to draw using their mouse, finger, or an inking tool, and whose ink resembles pencil graphite.

synchronization orchestrator.translation: trình phối hợp đồng bộ hóa
synchronization orchestrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An orchestrator that initiates and controls synchronization sessions.

remote media connection.translation: kết nối phương tiện từ xa
remote media connection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows Media Player (WMP) specific feature that allows you to use the Internet to access music, pictures and videos available on your home network. The feature must be activated on at least two computers in order to work.

calendar printing assistant.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft program that allows users to select and print a variety of customizable calendar templates.

calendar printing assistant for microsof.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft program that allows users to select and print a variety of customizable calendar templates.

desk phone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A telephone that sits on a desk and is to be used with Lync Server and Office Communications Server.

unlock.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To use some means of authentication to access the full functionality of a device or data.

dial pad.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A numeric keypad that is part of a device, is displayed on a device, or is in a computer program that you use to enter information in the context of a phone call.

dialpad.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A numeric keypad that is part of a device, is displayed on a device, or is in a computer program that you use to enter information in the context of a phone call.

deep linking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of creating a hyperlink to a specific page within a Web site or Web-based application instead of to the site’s home page.

pen plotter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A traditional graphics plotter that uses pens to draw on paper. Pen plotters use one or more colored pens, either fiber-tipped pens or, for highest-quality output, drafting pens.

null pointer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pointer to nothing: usually a standardized memory address, such as 0. A null pointer usually marks the last of a linear sequence of pointers or indicates that a data search operation has come up empty.

nil pointer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pointer to nothing: usually a standardized memory address, such as 0. A null pointer usually marks the last of a linear sequence of pointers or indicates that a data search operation has come up empty.

account name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of an email address that identifies a user or an account on an email system.

notification message.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An email message that is sent by a notification activity.

object type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An opaque data structure that defines a protected entity that is implemented and manipulated by the operating system. For example, the system service that reads a file operates on an open file object.

infopath forms services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server built upon and integrated with the Microsoft Windows SharePoint Services platform to enable Web-based use of InfoPath form templates, by rendering editable InfoPath forms in HTML in the browser.

comparator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device for comparing two items to determine whether they are equal. In electronics, for example, a comparator is a circuit that compares two input voltages and indicates which is higher.

compressor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that limits some aspect of a transmitted signal, such as volume, in order to increase efficiency.

kb.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Web site that provides customers with access to a database of articles written by Microsoft Support professionals.

operator.translation: toán tử, thao tác viên, cán bộ
operator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A sign or symbol that specifies the type of calculation to perform within an expression. There are mathematical, comparison, logical, and reference operators.

trojan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that appears to be useful or harmless but that contains hidden code designed to exploit or damage the system on which it is run.

trojan code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that appears to be useful or harmless but that contains hidden code designed to exploit or damage the system on which it is run.

trojan horse.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that appears to be useful or harmless but that contains hidden code designed to exploit or damage the system on which it is run.

password reset.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A procedure by which a user's password can be changed to a known value, in situations where the user has forgotten or lost their password.

diode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that passes current in only one direction. A diode is usually a semiconductor.

active server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The server-based component of Microsoft's Active Platform. Comprised of a set of technologies that includes DCOM (distributed component object model), Active Server Pages, Microsoft Transaction Server, and message queues, Active Server provides support for developing component-based, scalable, high-performance Web applications on Microsoft Windows NT servers. Active Server is designed to allow developers to concentrate on creating Internet and intranet software in a variety of languages without having to focus on the intricacy of the network itself.

electromagnet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that creates a magnetic field when electric current passes through it. An electromagnet typically contains an iron or steel core with wire wrapped around it. Current is passed through the wire, producing a magnetic field. Electromagnets are used in disk drives to record data onto the disk surface.

solution pack for microsoft dynamics.translation: Gói Giải pháp cho Microsoft Dynamics
solution pack for microsoft dynamics.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of resources that enables customers who are running a default configuration of Microsoft Dynamics CRM to deploy Office for Sales (OFS) out of the box without any modification. OFS defined entities and methods will be automatically mapped to corresponding entities and methods in the customer's Microsoft Dynamics CRM system.

team planner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view that shows all of the resources on a project and their work over time. This makes it easy to rearrange work, schedule new work, and manage a team's load.

decision support.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Systems designed to support the complex analytic analysis required to discover business trends.

on-object user interface.translation: Giao diện người dùng trên đối tượng
on-object user interface.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user interface that appears near a selected object, usually after the user right-clicks a selection, for example, a context menu that pops up above or beside a selected object and displays a list of commands that fit the selection.

on-object ui.translation: Giao diện người dùng trên đối tượng
on-object ui.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user interface that appears near a selected object, usually after the user right-clicks a selection, for example, a context menu that pops up above or beside a selected object and displays a list of commands that fit the selection.

ooui.translation: Giao diện người dùng trên đối tượng
ooui.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user interface that appears near a selected object, usually after the user right-clicks a selection, for example, a context menu that pops up above or beside a selected object and displays a list of commands that fit the selection.

explicit transaction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group of SQL statements enclosed within transaction delimiters that define both the start and end of the transaction.

purchase order.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A formal request for goods or services. The purchase order shows the quantity of goods or services ordered, expected receipt date, and supplier name. The purchase order may also include other information pertaining to the delivery of the goods or services.

po.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A formal request for goods or services. The purchase order shows the quantity of goods or services ordered, expected receipt date, and supplier name. The purchase order may also include other information pertaining to the delivery of the goods or services.

web portal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user interface implemented by a software application via a component of a web server, such as IIS.

workflow instance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A running instance of a workflow definition, when a request is made.

join condition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A comparison clause that specifies how tables are related by their join columns.

calendar program.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A piece of software that functions as an electronic calendar used for scheduling.

calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Teams tab where users can manage their calendars, allowing them to schedule meetings and access recordings without needing to switch apps.

powerpc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A microprocessor architecture developed in 1992 by Motorola and IBM, with some participation by Apple. A PowerPC microprocessor is RISC-based and superscalar, with a 64-bit data bus and 32-bit address bus. It also has separate data and instruction caches, although the size of each varies by implementation. All PowerPC microprocessors have multiple integer and floating-point units. The voltage and operating speed varies with the implementation. Starting with the PowerPC 740, the microprocessors were manufactured with copper, instead of aluminum, for better performance and reliability.

servo.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of a servomechanism, controlled by the servomechanism's feedback circuit, that produces the final mechanical output.

servomotor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of a servomechanism, controlled by the servomechanism's feedback circuit, that produces the final mechanical output.

servomechanism.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control system in which the final output is mechanical movement. A servomechanism uses feedback to control the position, velocity, or acceleration of a mechanical component.

servo system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control system in which the final output is mechanical movement. A servomechanism uses feedback to control the position, velocity, or acceleration of a mechanical component.

back.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Back button on the controller.

connector space.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A staging area that contains representations of selected objects and attributes in a connected data source.

metaverse.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The data store that is used by ILM to contain the aggregated identity information from multiple connected data sources, providing a single global, integrated view of all combined objects.

working time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The time that a resource is in the office, and that is not dedicated to project tasks or effort. Represents a resource's true availability.

self-join.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A join in which records from a table are combined with other records from the same table when there are matching values in the joined fields. A self-join can be an inner join or an outer join. In database diagrams, a self-join is called a reflexive relationship.

sql writer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A VSS compliant writer provided by the SQL Server that handles the VSS interaction with SQL Server.

synchronization engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software system that retrieves information from a source data store and synchronizes (pushes) to a target data store. Examples of synchronization engines are the ILM 2007 and FIM 2010 synchronization engines, and the service that synchronizes data rows in the SQL Server Express database with objects in the Microsoft Office Outlook data store.

syncengine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software system that retrieves information from a source data store and synchronizes (pushes) to a target data store. Examples of synchronization engines are the ILM 2007 and FIM 2010 synchronization engines, and the service that synchronizes data rows in the SQL Server Express database with objects in the Microsoft Office Outlook data store.

reject.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To refuse to accept a file or message.

relational store.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data repository structured in accordance with the relational model.

quick start guide.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The initial user reference guide or piece of documentation for using a device or feature.

discretize.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To put values of a continuous set of data into groups so that there are a discrete number of possible states.

directory synchronization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of matching user accounts and mail-enabled contacts and groups from the local Active Directory directory service.

active directory synchronization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of matching user accounts and mail-enabled contacts and groups from the local Active Directory directory service.

directory sync.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The application that provides one-way synchronization from an organization's on-premises Active Directory directory service to Microsoft Azure Active Directory.

client access server.translation: máy chủ cho phép Máy khách Truy cập
client access server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of components and services that enable users to access their Exchange mailboxes through the Outlook Web Access application.

tag tree.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The hierarchical HTML tag structure of an opened HTML document that appears in a task pane window.

search filter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A term that can be added to a search to filter the results by a specific property (for example, by author). Relevant search filters appear under the search box in any open folder.

advanced sync settings.translation: Thiết đặt đồng bộ nâng cao
advanced sync settings.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Settings for managing bandwidth and storage parameters for directory synchronization.

active directory site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of Internet Protocol subnets, usually used to connect a group of computers that are physically close to each other.

active directory object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity that can hold an identity in a Windows environment, such as computers, printers, mobile devices, users, groups, and so on.

directory object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity that can hold an identity in a Windows environment, such as computers, printers, mobile devices, users, groups, and so on.

active directory credentials.translation: thông tin đăng nhập Active Directory
active directory credentials.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of sign-in credentials (username and password) for an Active Directory account.

active directory account.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The identity of a user, which can be used to grant access to resources or authority to perform certain tasks.

menu bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A rectangular bar displayed in an application's window, often at the top, from which menus can be selected by the user.

heap corruption.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of corruption that affects the data in the Windows heap, such as damages caused by a buffer overrun, writing to a stray pointer or a double-free.

microsoft online services directory sync.translation: Công cụ Đồng bộ hóa Thư mục Microsoft Online Services
microsoft online services directory sync.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The application that provides one-way synchronization from an organization's on-premises Active Directory directory service to Microsoft Azure Active Directory.

connectivity explorer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window that shows pipeline components and all components to which the pipeline is connected.

microsoft online services sign in applic.translation: Đăng nhập vào Microsoft Online Services
microsoft online services sign in applic.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The application that is installed on a Microsoft Online Services end user’s computer to provide a single sign-in point for Microsoft Online Services.

microsoft online services sign in.translation: Đăng nhập vào Microsoft Online Services
microsoft online services sign in.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The application that is installed on a Microsoft Online Services end user’s computer to provide a single sign-in point for Microsoft Online Services.

microsoft exchange online.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Online Services service that delivers advanced email features, calendaring, contact, and task management capabilities.

touch keyboard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A contiguous on-screen keyboard.

microsoft sharepoint online.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft hosted version of Windows SharePoint Services, the Microsoft-hosted solution that helps employees create and manage custom team and project-focused intranet sites for collaboration and document sharing.

sharepoint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft hosted version of Windows SharePoint Services, the Microsoft-hosted solution that helps employees create and manage custom team and project-focused intranet sites for collaboration and document sharing.

microsoft office communications online.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft hosted version of Office Communications Server.

tuning adapter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A two-way device provided by a cable provider that enables some one-way digital CableCARD-based consumer electronic devices such as high-definition DVRs and Media Center PCs to access digital cable channels delivered using switched digital video.

ta.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A two-way device provided by a cable provider that enables some one-way digital CableCARD-based consumer electronic devices such as high-definition DVRs and Media Center PCs to access digital cable channels delivered using switched digital video.

cobol.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A verbose, English-like compiled programming language developed between 1959 and 1961 and still in widespread use today, especially in business applications typically run on mainframes. A COBOL program consists of an Identification Division, which specifies the name of the program and contains any other documentation the programmer wants to add; an Environment Division, which specifies the computers being used and the files used in the program for input and output; a Data Division, which describes the format of the data structures used in the program; and a Procedure Division, which contains the procedures that dictate the actions of the program.

common business-oriented language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A verbose, English-like compiled programming language developed between 1959 and 1961 and still in widespread use today, especially in business applications typically run on mainframes. A COBOL program consists of an Identification Division, which specifies the name of the program and contains any other documentation the programmer wants to add; an Environment Division, which specifies the computers being used and the files used in the program for input and output; a Data Division, which describes the format of the data structures used in the program; and a Procedure Division, which contains the procedures that dictate the actions of the program.

netbook.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small, affordable laptop that is designed to perform a limited number of tasks such as web browsing and email.

small notebook pc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small, affordable laptop that is designed to perform a limited number of tasks such as web browsing and email.

cdn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A distributed system of servers deployed in multiple data centers that cache content from origin servers and then serve it to customers. This action reduces the load on the origin servers and provides high- availability and performance to customers.

content delivery network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A distributed system of servers deployed in multiple data centers that cache content from origin servers and then serve it to customers. This action reduces the load on the origin servers and provides high- availability and performance to customers.

reminder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A notification on the app bar that appears at a specified interval before an appointment, meeting, or task announcing when the activity is set to occur.

multitouch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A real-time, physical action applied to an object, in which multiple contact points are used simultaneously.

multi-touch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The combination of hardware (touchscreen or touchpad) and software elements that provides a way to control programs by touching multiple points on the screen simultaneously.

scripting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to the automation of user actions or the configuration of a standard state on a computer by means of scripts.

account balance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An amount that is the difference between the sum of debit entries and the sum of credit entries entered into an account during a financial period.

cd recorder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device used to write CD-ROMs. Because a disc can be written only once on these machines, they are used most commonly to create CD-ROMs for data archives or to produce CD-ROM masters that can be duplicated for mass distribution.

cd burner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device used to write CD-ROMs. Because a disc can be written only once on these machines, they are used most commonly to create CD-ROMs for data archives or to produce CD-ROM masters that can be duplicated for mass distribution.

data binning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of grouping data into specific bins or groups according to defined criteria.

fet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of transistor in which the flow of current between the source and the drain is modulated by the electric field around the gate electrode. FETs are used as amplifiers, oscillators, and switches and are characterized by an extremely high input impedance (resistance) that makes them particularly suitable for amplification of very small signals. Types of FETs include the junction FET and the metal-oxide semiconductor FET (MOSFET).

field-effect transistor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of transistor in which the flow of current between the source and the drain is modulated by the electric field around the gate electrode. FETs are used as amplifiers, oscillators, and switches and are characterized by an extremely high input impedance (resistance) that makes them particularly suitable for amplification of very small signals. Types of FETs include the junction FET and the metal-oxide semiconductor FET (MOSFET).

word xml format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The formal name for Word 12 file format. thin rendering.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of rendering server-based spreadsheets, diagrams, or other documents in a browser using an application server.
