powerpoint render.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A converter that supports dynamic viewing of PowerPoint presentations (with animation) in a Web environment.

relative strength index.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A momentum oscillator that compares upward movements of a stock's closing price with downward movements, and results in values that range from 0 to 100.

dial tone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A sound emitted by the receiver of a telephone that indicates that a number can be dialed.

drawing guide.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A guide used to position shapes and objects on slides.

powerpoint static.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A converter that supports static viewing of PowerPoint presentations (without animation) in a Web environment.

microsoft office live workspace.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft online collaboration Web solution that provides a secure online workspace to store & share documents that integrates with existing Microsoft programs.

microsoft search server 2010 express.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft enterprise-grade core search solution, designed to search content in common data repositories including file shares, Web sites, SharePoint sites, Microsoft Exchange Server Public Folders, and Lotus Notes databases.

search server 2010 express.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft enterprise-grade core search solution, designed to search content in common data repositories including file shares, Web sites, SharePoint sites, Microsoft Exchange Server Public Folders, and Lotus Notes databases.

fault tolerance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ability of computer hardware or software to ensure data integrity when hardware failures occur. Fault-tolerant features appear in many server operating systems and include mirrored volumes, RAID-5 volumes, and server clusters.

administrative setup.translation: thiết lập của người quản trị
administrative setup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mode of setup that allows network administrators to silently deploy to client computers.

administrator setup.translation: thiết lập của người quản trị
administrator setup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mode of setup that allows network administrators to silently deploy to client computers.

laptop.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A portable computer that combines a processor, screen, and keyboard in a single case. The screen folds down onto the keyboard when not in use.

artificial intelligence.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A branch of computer science concerned with creating software that simulates aspects of human intelligence.

ai.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A branch of computer science concerned with creating software that simulates aspects of human intelligence.

automated teller machine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special-purpose terminal that bank customers can use to make deposits, obtain cash, and perform other transactions.

atm.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A high-speed, connection-oriented, virtual circuit-based packet switching protocol used to transport many different types of network traffic. ATM packages data in 53-byte, fixed-length cells that can be switched quickly between logical connections on a network.

binomial distribution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In statistics, a list or a function that describes the probabilities of the possible values of a random variable chosen by means of a Bernoulli sampling process.

stewardship portal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of MDS that provides centralized control over master data, including members and hierarchies and enables data model administrators to ensure data quality by developing, reviewing, and managing data models and enforcing them consistently across domains.

visio services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server technology that enables users to load, and display Visio drawings on Microsoft SharePoint Server 2010.

visio services in microsoft sharepoint s.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server technology that enables users to load, and display Visio drawings on Microsoft SharePoint Server 2010.

lotus cc:mail.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An email program originally introduced by cc:mail, Inc., and currently produced by the Lotus Development Corporation. Lotus cc:Mail runs on multiple networking platforms and the Internet and is closely integrated with Lotus Notes collaborative software.

cc:mail.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An email program originally introduced by cc:mail, Inc., and currently produced by the Lotus Development Corporation. Lotus cc:Mail runs on multiple networking platforms and the Internet and is closely integrated with Lotus Notes collaborative software.

dpm role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The grouping of users, objects, and permissions that is used by DPM administrators to manage DPM features that are used by end users.

dpm system recovery tool.translation: Công cụ Phục hồi Hệ thống DPM
dpm system recovery tool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Software provided with DPM to facilitate a Windows Server 2003 bare metal recovery for the DPM server and the computers that DPM protects.

dpm srt.translation: Công cụ Phục hồi Hệ thống DPM
dpm srt.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Software provided with DPM to facilitate a Windows Server 2003 bare metal recovery for the DPM server and the computers that DPM protects.

auto-consistency check.translation: tự động kiểm tra tính nhất quán
auto-consistency check.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that automatically runs a consistency check on protected data sources when it detects an inconsistent replica.

auto-protection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In DPM, a feature that automatically identifies and adds new data sources for protection.

data co-location.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In DPM, a feature that enables protection of multiple data sources on a single volume or on the same tape. This allows you to store more data on each volume or tape.

dpm engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A policy-driven engine that DPM uses to protect and recover data.

inactive data source.translation: nguồn dữ liệu không hoạt động
inactive data source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data source that has been backed up on the DPM server but is no longer being actively protected.

primary protection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of protection in which data on the protected server is directly protected by a primary DPM Server.

secondary protection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of protection in which data on the protected server is protected by a primary DPM server and the replica on the primary DPM server is protected by a secondary DPM server.

sql server instance auto-protection.translation: tự động bảo vệ phiên bản SQL Server
sql server instance auto-protection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of protection that enables DPM to automatically identify and protect databases that are added to instances of SQL Server that are configured for auto-protection.

dpm self-service tool for sql server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool for SQL Server that enables backup administrators to authorize end users to recover backups of SQL Server databases from DPM, without further action from the backup administrator.

dpm sst for sql server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool for SQL Server that enables backup administrators to authorize end users to recover backups of SQL Server databases from DPM, without further action from the backup administrator.

attorney-client privilege.translation: đặc quyền giữa luật sư và thân chủ
attorney-client privilege.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A legal doctrine that is intended to protect the confidentiality of communications between an attorney and his or her client. The underlying rationale is that by assuring confidential communications, lawyers and their clients will feel free to discuss sensitive legal matters thoroughly.

bad word.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specific word or phrase that is specified on the basis of an organization's messaging policy and used in keyword filtering (content filtering) to identify and prevent unwanted email messages from being delivered to users in the organization.

server-side session.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The runspace on the datacenter (host) server, which contains the commands used by the remote user in a client-side session.

client-side session.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Windows PowerShell session on a user's local computer, which has the basic Windows PowerShell commands available to it.

active mailbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A mailbox that has been accessed at least once in the last 30 days.

connected data source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A directory, database, file, or other data repository that is typically offsite and that needs to be accessed remotely.

outlook live management agent.translation: Tác nhân Quản lý Outlook Live
outlook live management agent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Identity Lifecycle Manager (ILM) 2007 management agent provided by Microsoft to connect to Outlook Live. It is an ILM component that consists of properties, rules, and rules extensions that determine how an object is processed.

olma.translation: Tác nhân Quản lý Outlook Live
olma.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Identity Lifecycle Manager (ILM) 2007 management agent provided by Microsoft to connect to Outlook Live. It is an ILM component that consists of properties, rules, and rules extensions that determine how an object is processed.

elma.translation: Tác nhân Quản lý Outlook Live
elma.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Identity Lifecycle Manager (ILM) 2007 management agent provided by Microsoft to connect to Outlook Live. It is an ILM component that consists of properties, rules, and rules extensions that determine how an object is processed.

discovery manager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A person who has a business need to search the mailboxes in their organization for email and other message types that contain specific keywords.

concurrent operation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer operation in which two or more processes (programs) have access to the microprocessor's time and are therefore carried out nearly simultaneously. Because a microprocessor can work with much smaller units of time than people can perceive, concurrent processes appear to be occurring simultaneously but in reality are not.

concurrent processing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer operation in which two or more processes (programs) have access to the microprocessor's time and are therefore carried out nearly simultaneously. Because a microprocessor can work with much smaller units of time than people can perceive, concurrent processes appear to be occurring simultaneously but in reality are not.

external contact.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: People outside the Outlook Live organization who can be added to public groups and displayed in your organization's address book and other address lists. External contacts have email addresses outside the organization and can't sign in to your domain.

forced rename state.translation: tình trạng đổi tên bắt buộc
forced rename state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The state that a Windows Live ID takes when the user account with which it is associated is deleted from Outlook Live, but the Windows Live ID for the account isn't deleted. The credentials for that Windows Live ID are still valid and recognized, but the Windows Live ID is put into a forced rename state. If someone tries to sign in using that Windows Live ID and its password, they're asked to rename the Windows Live ID. They can rename the Windows Live ID, but because the new email address can't exist in the Outlook Live domain, the Windows Live ID is no longer functional in Outlook Live.

metaverse entry.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Identity Lifecycle Manager (ILM) 2007 object that has been projected into the metaverse from a connector space object and is linked to at least one object in the connector space. A metaverse entry represents the aggregated view of objects from one or several connected data sources.

mx token.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of numbers found in the MX server field in the MX Record Configuration section on the Domain Settings page of the Windows Live Admin Center. The MX token value is unique for each domain. It is required to create an MX record or a CNAME record at DNS hosting services.

proxy address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The address by which a Exchange Server recipient object is recognized in a foreign messaging system. In Outlook Live, proxy addresses let people receive email that is sent to different email addresses.

other e-mail address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The address by which a Exchange Server recipient object is recognized in a foreign messaging system. In Outlook Live, proxy addresses let people receive email that is sent to different email addresses.

remote domain.translation: tên miền điều khiển từ xa
remote domain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specially-configured domain that defines settings for mail flow based on the destination domain of each email message. Administrators can configure specific settings for a specific destination domain, or configure default settings for all destination domains. In this way, they can control the types of messages that are sent to a domain. They can also apply message format policies and acceptable character sets for messages that are sent from users in their organization to the remote domain.

shared address space.translation: tên miền sử dụng ở nhiều nơi
shared address space.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) address space or domain suffix that is shared by two different messaging systems. For example, you may have to share the SMTP address space between Microsoft Exchange and a third-party email system, or between Exchange environments that are configured in different Active Directory forests. In these scenarios, users in each email system have the same domain suffix as part of their email addresses.

split domain.translation: tên miền sử dụng ở nhiều nơi
split domain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) address space or domain suffix that is shared by two different messaging systems. For example, you may have to share the SMTP address space between Microsoft Exchange and a third-party email system, or between Exchange environments that are configured in different Active Directory forests. In these scenarios, users in each email system have the same domain suffix as part of their email addresses.

semantic error.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An error in meaning; a statement in a program that is syntactically correct (legal) but functionally incorrect.

database administrator.translation: quản trị viên cơ sở dữ liệu
database administrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person who manages a database. The administrator determines the content, internal structure, and access strategy for a database, defines security and integrity, and monitors performance.

dba.translation: quản trị viên cơ sở dữ liệu
dba.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person who manages a database. The administrator determines the content, internal structure, and access strategy for a database, defines security and integrity, and monitors performance.

token-based activation.translation: kích hoạt dựa trên mã thông báo
token-based activation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specialized activation option available for approved Microsoft Volume Licensing customers that enables customers to use public key infrastructure (PKI) and digital certificates (or “tokens,” typically stored on smart cards) to activate Windows Vista Enterprise and Windows Server 2008 SP2 locally without contacting either customer-hosted KMS or the Microsoft-hosted activation service using MAK.

product key card.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A physical card on which a product key is printed.

pkc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A physical card on which a product key is printed.

powerpivot gallery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special-purpose SharePoint document library that provides rich preview and document management for published Excel workbooks that contain PowerPivot data as well as other document types.

storage allocation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In operating systems, the process of reserving memory for use by a program.

memory allocation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In operating systems, the process of reserving memory for use by a program.

solution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A value or values which, when substituted for a variable in an equation, make the equation true.

performance tools.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Tools that you can use to evaluate the performance of a solution. Performance tools can have different purposes; some are designed to evaluate end-to-end performance while others focus on evaluating performance of a particular aspect of a solution.

managed solution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A complete solution that has been packaged. After this solution has been installed, the extent to which it can be modified is specified by the publisher.

solution component.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A part of a solution that someone extending CRM can use to achieve specific functionality.

solution publisher.translation: đối tác phát triển giải pháp
solution publisher.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A partner, such as an ISV, who develops solutions on top of a software platform.

default solution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A "catch-all" solution that contains a reference to all unprotected components.

trial subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription that hasn't been activated and works for only a limited amount of time.

trial account.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription that hasn't been activated and works for only a limited amount of time.

sub-grid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A grid added to a form by a customizer that provides users with access to a group of records, which are usually contextually related.

task form.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A narrow and long form that appears in the task pane, which is used to view and edit related data for lookups.

required component.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component that is required for the current component to properly work. For example, a workflow requires an entity to run.

activity status.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The condition, at a particular time, of an activity.

gauge.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A one-dimensional data display that represents a specific value as a data point within a range.

quick parts gallery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A gallery to which users can add reusable content to be displayed in Quick Parts and the Building Blocks Organizer.

enterprise metadata.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Metadata pertaining to content across an enterprise.

dns hosting service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A service that runs Domain Name System (DNS) servers. Most, but not all, domain name registrars include DNS hosting service with registration.

business contact manager for microsoft o.translation: Công cụ Cơ sở dữ liệu Business Contact Manager dành cho Microsoft Outlook 2010
business contact manager for microsoft o.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A downloadable tool that provides users with administration capabilities such as creating, sharing, backing up or restoring a database.

business contact manager for outlook 201.translation: Công cụ Cơ sở dữ liệu Business Contact Manager dành cho Microsoft Outlook 2010
business contact manager for outlook 201.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A downloadable tool that provides users with administration capabilities such as creating, sharing, backing up or restoring a database.

working capital.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The measure of the funds available to an organization to continue its operations; this financial metric is the difference between an organization’s current assets and its current liabilities.

how to tell.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A marketing initiative to assist consumers in identifying genuine Microsoft software.

genuine microsoft software.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Software that is published by Microsoft, properly licensed, and fully supported by Microsoft or a trusted partner.

wga notifications.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Notifications that indicate a new installation of Windows did not pass validation.

windows genuine advantage notifications.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Notifications that indicate a new installation of Windows did not pass validation.

raster.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A rectangular pattern of lines; on a video display, the horizontal scan lines from which the term raster scan is derived.

e-newsletter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A newsletter sent by email to educate, alert, and persuade recipients, known as subscribers, about a company, its products, and other communications messages. This type of campaign is part of an integrated set of electronic marketing techniques.

business to business.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Relating to the sales category pertaining to transactions and related activity between a business and buyers who are not consumers, such as government bodies, companies, and resellers.

business-to-business.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Relating to the sales category pertaining to transactions and related activity between a business and buyers who are not consumers, such as government bodies, companies, and resellers.

b2b.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The service that allows you to securely share your company's applications and services with guest users and external partners from any organization, while maintaining control over your own corporate data.

tracing service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A service responsible for writing diagnostic logging and usage logging information from SharePoint applications to log files on disk.

sharepoint tracing service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A service responsible for writing diagnostic logging and usage logging information from SharePoint applications to log files on disk.

site collection solution gallery.translation: bộ sưu tập giải pháp tuyển tập site
site collection solution gallery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A capability that enables site collection administrators to manage and add new solutions to their site collections.

back-end database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu phụ trợ
back-end database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a two-database approach, the server-side database that contains the tables that hold your solution's data, and that is accessed by your solution through links in the front-end database.

image gallery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A repository for storing and managing visual resources, such as images and themes.

advanced query syntax.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A search query syntax that helps produce more precise search results by using targeted queries that search specific properties in a message type. AQS defines certain keywords which can be used to refine the search query, such as specifying boolean operations on searched terms (AND, OR, NOT) as well as to specify further filters based on file metadata or file type. It can also be used to limit results from specific information stores like regular files, offline files cache, or email stores.

aqs.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A search query syntax that helps produce more precise search results by using targeted queries that search specific properties in a message type. AQS defines certain keywords which can be used to refine the search query, such as specifying boolean operations on searched terms (AND, OR, NOT) as well as to specify further filters based on file metadata or file type. It can also be used to limit results from specific information stores like regular files, offline files cache, or email stores.

parity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to the resiliency type for a volume that stripes data and parity information across physical disks in a Microsoft Storage Spaces storage pool.

exchange control panel.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The web-based management tool for Microsoft Exchange administrators and enterprise email users.

exchange admin center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The web-based management tool for Microsoft Exchange administrators and enterprise email users.

exchange administration center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The web-based management tool for Microsoft Exchange administrators and enterprise email users.

mail control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The primary navigation tab for mail flow management features in Outlook Live: Transport rules, called “rules” in Outlook Live service; Supervision policies, including closed campus supervision policy and bad words supervision policy, and anti-bullying supervision policy; IP safelisting; Domain types: hosted or shared.

microsoft live@edu service management po.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Web-based management interface for Live@edu administrators. Administrators enroll their domain there initially, and then use the portal to keep their contact information up to date; access DNS record information; view the status of enrolled domains; manage IP safelists; request support for single sign-on; submit or escalate a support request; link to all other resources.

supervision policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of email policy settings that can help primary and secondary school administrators comply with some requirements of the Children's Internet Protection Act (CIPA). Using these policy settings, administrators can control who can send email to and receive email from the users in their organization, and filter and reject email that contains objectionable words.

closed campus supervision policy.translation: chính sách giám sát chặn email của trường học
closed campus supervision policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: E-mail policy settings that apply inbound and outbound email restrictions so students can send email to or receive email from addresses inside the organization only. Administrators can set up organization-wide exceptions so email can be sent to or from specific domains and public groups. Administrators can also configure per-user exceptions so students can send email to and receive email from specific addresses outside the organization.

anti-bullying supervision policy.translation: chính sách giám sát chống bắt nạt
anti-bullying supervision policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An email policy that administrators use to prevent a bully from sending email messages to specific people by adding the bully's email address as an entry on the "victim's" supervision list. This functionality supports anti-harassment policies in schools and other organizations.

supervision list entry.translation: mục nhập danh sách giám sát
supervision list entry.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual item on the list of email addresses or users that are subject to or excepted from the actions of the closed campus supervision policy or anti-bullying supervision policy. For example, a bully's email address would be an entry on the supervision list of a "victim", and a parent's email address might be added as an entry on the supervision list of their child, who is a student subject to the closed campus supervision policy.

supervision list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The list of email addresses or users that are subject to or excepted from the actions of the closed campus supervision policy or anti-bullying supervision policy.

bad word supervision policy.translation: chính sách giám sát từ thô tục
bad word supervision policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: E-mail policy settings that prevent sending and receiving email that has specifically banned content. Administrators can use this policy to reject email that contains profanity or other objectionable words, also known as "bad words".

migration batch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of user accounts that are being submitted in a CSV file for migration from an on-premises messaging system to an email system in the cloud.

migration batch request.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The action of submitting a migration batch for migration from an on-premises messaging system to an email system in the cloud.

list view threshold.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A threshold in the Resource Throttling feature that specifies the maximum number of items that a database operation can involve at one time. Operations that exceed this limit are prohibited.

date range.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The time span between the start and end dates.

report part.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report item that has been published separately to a report server and that can be reused in other reports.

self-service business intelligence.translation: nghiệp vụ thông minh tự phục vụ
self-service business intelligence.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Analytic tools and processes that enable users in an organization to access data to create, use, and share reports without relying on IT for report creation.

self-service bi.translation: nghiệp vụ thông minh tự phục vụ
self-service bi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Analytic tools and processes that enable users in an organization to access data to create, use, and share reports without relying on IT for report creation.

delegated administrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft partner who is associated with one or more companies and authorized to provide certain administrative tasks for said companies. A delegated administrator may be the same or different than a customer’s subscription advisor. Referred to within Microsoft as a “delegated administrator partner (DAP).”

delegated admin.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft partner who is associated with one or more companies and authorized to provide certain administrative tasks for said companies. A delegated administrator may be the same or different than a customer’s subscription advisor. Referred to within Microsoft as a “delegated administrator partner (DAP).”

managed metadata service.translation: dịch vụ siêu dữ liệu được quản lý
managed metadata service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shared service that publishes a term store and, optionally, a set of content types.

project services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SharePoint application service that enables Project Server functionality.

partitioned snapshot.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In merge replication, a snapshot that includes only the data from a single partition.

dynamic snapshot.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In merge replication, a snapshot that includes only the data from a single partition.

search service application.translation: Ứng dụng dịch vụ tìm kiếm
search service application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SharePoint service application that is deployed and managed on premises and that enables enterprise search functionality.

word automation services.translation: Dịch vụ Tự động hóa Word
word automation services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A service application in SharePoint Server that provides unattended, server-side conversion of documents into formats that are supported by the Microsoft Word client application.

word viewing service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The SharePoint service that enables viewing of Word documents from a Web browser.

infopath designer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The design environment in the InfoPath client that enables users to create or modify form templates.

microsoft infopath designer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The design environment in the InfoPath client that enables users to create or modify form templates.

administrator role group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A universal security group with administrative rights assigned to it. These administrative rights are specified by built-in management roles, which are part of the role-based access control (RBAC) permissions model in Exchange Server 2010.

role group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A universal security group with administrative rights assigned to it. These administrative rights are specified by built-in management roles, which are part of the role-based access control (RBAC) permissions model in Exchange Server 2010.

role assignment policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of one or more end-user management roles that enable users to manage the settings of their Outlook Live account and public groups.

discovery mailbox.translation: Hộp thư Khám phá điện tử
discovery mailbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A system mailbox in which copies of the mailbox search results are stored.

discovery system mailbox.translation: Hộp thư Khám phá điện tử
discovery system mailbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A system mailbox in which copies of the mailbox search results are stored.

ediscovery mailbox.translation: Hộp thư Khám phá điện tử
ediscovery mailbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A system mailbox in which copies of the mailbox search results are stored.

ip safelist.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The collection of IP addresses that are in a gateway servers list or internal mail servers list of IP addresses that should not be treated as spam.

safelist.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The collection of IP addresses that are in a gateway servers list or internal mail servers list of IP addresses that should not be treated as spam.

role entry.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The individual entry on a management role. Role entries provide access to cmdlets, scripts, and other special permissions that let users perform a specific task. A role entry is often a single cmdlet and the parameters that members of a role group can run when the role is assigned to the role group.

role scope.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The scope of influence or impact of a role assignment. The scope defines what objects a role group member can manage. In Outlook Live, there is the recipient scope and the configuration scope.

role group member.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A member of an administrator role group, which is a universal security group with administrative rights assigned to it. The roles assigned to the role group are applied to each member who is added to the role group. This grants each user all the permissions allowed by the roles assigned to the role group.

terms of use.translation: tính năng điều khoản sử dụng
terms of use.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that provides a method for organizations to present disclaimers for legal or compliance requirements to end users.

data-tier application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A application that captures the SQL Server database and instance objects used by a client-server or 3-tier application.

dac.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A application that captures the SQL Server database and instance objects used by a client-server or 3-tier application.

dac instance.translation: phiên bản ứng dụng lớp dữ liệu
dac instance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A copy of a DAC deployed on an instance of the Database Engine. There can be multiple DAC instances on the same instance of the Database Engine.

data-tier application instance.translation: phiên bản ứng dụng lớp dữ liệu
data-tier application instance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A copy of a DAC deployed on an instance of the Database Engine. There can be multiple DAC instances on the same instance of the Database Engine.

dac package.translation: gói ứng dụng lớp dữ liệu
dac package.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML manifest that contains all of the objects defined for the DAC; the package gets created when a developer builds a DAC project.

data-tier application package.translation: gói ứng dụng lớp dữ liệu
data-tier application package.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML manifest that contains all of the objects defined for the DAC; the package gets created when a developer builds a DAC project.

dacpac.translation: gói ứng dụng lớp dữ liệu
dacpac.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML manifest that contains all of the objects defined for the DAC; the package gets created when a developer builds a DAC project.

dac placement policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A PBM policy that comprises a set of conditions, which serve as prerequisites on the target instance of SQL Server where the DAC can be deployed.

dac project.translation: dự án ứng dụng lớp dữ liệu SQL Server
dac project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Visual Studio project used by database developers to create and develop a DAC. DAC projects get full support from Visual Studio and VSTS source code control, versioning, and development project management.

sql server data-tier application project.translation: dự án ứng dụng lớp dữ liệu SQL Server
sql server data-tier application project.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Visual Studio project used by database developers to create and develop a DAC. DAC projects get full support from Visual Studio and VSTS source code control, versioning, and development project management.

managed instance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An instance of SQL Server monitored by a utility control point.

drop shadow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shaded outline that appears behind an object or text and creates the illusion of depth.

shadow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A virtual representation of a player in a game that learns and replicates that player's gameplay style and tendencies.

sql server utility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A way to organize and monitor SQL Server resource health. It enables administrators to have a holistic view of their environment.

sql server utility explorer.translation: Trình khám phá Tiện ích SQL Server
sql server utility explorer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hierarchical tree displaying the objects in the SQL Server Utility.

unmanaged instance.translation: phiên bản không được quản lý
unmanaged instance.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An instance of SQL Server not monitored by a utility control point.

utility control point.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network node that provides the central reasoning point for the SQL Server Utility. It uses Utility Explorer in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) to organize and monitor SQL Server resource health.

ucp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A network node that provides the central reasoning point for the SQL Server Utility. It uses Utility Explorer in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) to organize and monitor SQL Server resource health.

msdb.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database that stores scheduled jobs, alerts, and backup/restore history information.

sql server utility dashboard.translation: Bảng điều khiển Tiện ích SQL Server
sql server utility dashboard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A dashboard that provides an at-a-glance summary of resource health for managed SQL Server instances and data-tier applications. Can also be referred to as the SQL Server Utility detail view or the list view with details.

dac package file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The XML file that is the container of a DAC package.

facet property.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A predefined property that applies to a specific facet in Policy-Based Management.

people.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A category of Copilot prompts that helps users nurture relationships on a personal and professional level.

more.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item on the Actions menu that displays additional actions the user can select.

events.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The add-in for Skype users to create shared events for their group.

groups.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature that unifies components across applications, such as people, conversations, calendars, emails, and files, to create a seamless collaboration experience. Creating a group anywhere in Microsoft 365 will automatically provision a corresponding Yammer conversation feed, an Outlook inbox and calendar, and a SharePoint document library for every Group member. Groups make these components persistent across applications, so that changes made to components in part of Microsoft 365 will carry through to the others, thus enabling a unified experience.

spaces.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The virtual SharePoint space that is viewable on mixed-reality devices and any browser that allows users to consume intranet content, work in groups, collaborate, communicate and customize their organization.

downloads.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The link to the site to download client versions of Windows Live products such as Windows Live Mail, Windows Live Messenger, etc.

all services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The link to the overview page of all Windows Live, MSN, and Microsoft products on offer.

contact info.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Information, such as name, phone number, email address, or address, that is used to contact someone.

policy-based management.translation: quản lý dựa trên chính sách
policy-based management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of built-in functions that return server state information about values, objects, and settings in SQL Server. Policy Based Management allows a database administrator to declare the desired state of the system and checks the system for compliance with that state.

pbm.translation: quản lý dựa trên chính sách
pbm.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of built-in functions that return server state information about values, objects, and settings in SQL Server. Policy Based Management allows a database administrator to declare the desired state of the system and checks the system for compliance with that state.

evaluate formula.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An option that enables the user to see the different parts of a nested formula evaluated in the order the formula is calculated.

eager loading.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pattern of loading where a specific set of related objects are loaded along with the objects that were explicitly requested in the query.

explicit loading.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pattern of loading where related objects are not loaded until explicitly requested by using the Load method on a navigation property.

foreign key association.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An association between entities that is managed through foreign key properties.

manage user-defined fields.translation: Quản lý các trường do người dùng xác định
manage user-defined fields.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An option, found on the Business Contact Manager menu, that enables the user to customize multiple fields.

identifying relationship.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A relationship where the primary key of the principal entity is part of the primary key of the dependent entity. In this kind of relationship, the dependent entity cannot exist without the principal entity.

independent association.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An association between entities that is represented and tracked by an independent object.

lazy loading.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pattern of data loading where related objects are not loaded until a navigation property is accessed.

deferred loading.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pattern of data loading where related objects are not loaded until a navigation property is accessed.

email migration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Outlook Live feature in the Web management interface that enables migration of the contents of user mailboxes from an on-premises IMAP messaging system to Outlook Live (or Exchange Online).

enroll.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To enable mobile device management (MDM) with Microsoft Intune on a personal computer or other device.

deploy.rule: Dịch là 'Triển khai' đối với phần mềm/hệ thống.

provisioning domain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The domain name of the Outlook Live domain that you are configuring with Outlook Live Directory Sync (OLSync)(previously known as GALSync 2010). When you deploy OLSync, you manually enter at least one provisioning domain, for example, student.contoso.edu, during the ILM 2007 configuration process. The provisioning domain must be an accepted domain in your Outlook Live deployment.

blocked sender.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A domain or a person that an end user doesn't want to receive email messages from. Messages received from any email address or domain listed in the users' Blocked Senders list are sent directly to the user's Junk E-Mail folder.

mail-enabled user.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Active Directory security principal object that has at least one associated SMTP address

import users.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The administrator user interface in Outlook Live used to import new users with a CSV file.

csv import file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A comma separated value (CSV) file used to provision many new users at one time.

import process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of provisioning new users using a CSV file.

dynamic management view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of built-in views that return server state information about values, objects, and settings in SQL Server.

dmv.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of built-in views that return server state information about values, objects, and settings in SQL Server.

write scope.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The administrative boundary in which members of an Exchange 2010 role group can make changes. For the Outlook Live hosted service, the write scope is the entire Outlook Live organization. For on-premises implementations of Microsoft Exchange Server 2010, write scopes may be smaller in breadth, such as those defined by a specific organizational unit or a database.

discovery management.translation: Quản lý Tìm kiếm Nhiều Hộp thư
discovery management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The role group that gives users the permissions needed to use Multi-Mailbox Search.

help desk.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The role group that gives users the permissions to reset passwords for users and manage settings on the Options page for users' Outlook Live account. To help troubleshoot user issues, members can also view, but not modify, all mailboxes, public groups, and external contacts in the organization.

recipient management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The role group that gives users the permissions to create and manage mailboxes, public groups, and external contacts. Members can also import new users, track messages sent and received by users, and manage Exchange ActiveSync settings for the organization.

um management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The role group that gives users the permissions to manage Unified Messaging (UM) server configurations, UM properties on mailboxes, UM prompts, and UM auto attendant configuration.

view-only organization management.translation: Vai trò Quản lý Chỉ được Xem
view-only organization management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The administrator role group that gives users permissions to view, but not modify, all mailboxes, public groups, and external contacts in the organization. Members can also view settings for role assignment policies, transport rules, and supervision policies.

safe sender.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A domain or a person that a user wants to always receive email messages from. Users add recipients and domains to the Safe Senders list.

multi-mailbox search.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature in Exchange 2010 and Outlook Live that enables users to search the mailboxes in their organization for email and other message types that contain specific keywords. The results of a search are then copied to a mailbox that you have specified so that you can review, organize, and export the search results.

unsearchable item.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item that can't be indexed for a mailbox search using Multi-Mailbox Search. This includes unrecognized message types and messages that contain attachments that are encrypted or have an unrecognized format.

group moderator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A person who is assigned the ability to approve and reject any messages sent to a public group or a dynamic distribution group.

room mailbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource mailbox that is assigned to a meeting location such as a conference room, auditorium, or training room. Room mailboxes can be included as resources in meeting requests, providing a simple and efficient way of organizing meetings for an organization.

legal hold.translation: tạm giữ vì lý do pháp lý
legal hold.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hold that that is created by using either In-Place Hold or Litigation Hold.

litigation hold.translation: Tính năng Bảo quản thư trong trường hợp tranh chấp pháp lý
litigation hold.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature that allows the preservation of items in user mailboxes and the protection of the items from deletion by users or automated processes.

follower.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An Xbox user who has added you to their friends list.

decision engine.translation: công cụ hỗ trợ ra quyết định
decision engine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Software or service able to process a large amount of data and provide reports that help users make more informed decisions.

super-user credentials.translation: thông tin xác thực người dùng cấp cao
super-user credentials.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Elevated credentials that have rights to access objects that ordinary users without elevated credentials can't access.

em dash.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The — character, based on the width of an uppercase M and used primarily to set off sentence elements.

pop subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription that gathers messages from POP3 mailboxes and delivers the messages to a designated Outlook Live mailbox so that the Outlook Live end user can centralize their email accounts and only have to check one mailbox.

unmanaged windows live id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows Live ID created in a domain, and using the domain name, before the domain was enrolled in Outlook Live. After the Windows Live ID is imported into the Outlook Live domain, it is subject to the security and privacy policies of the organization.

e-mail as sign in id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows Live ID created in a domain, and using the domain name, before the domain was enrolled in Outlook Live. After the Windows Live ID is imported into the Outlook Live domain, it is subject to the security and privacy policies of the organization.

easi id.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows Live ID created in a domain, and using the domain name, before the domain was enrolled in Outlook Live. After the Windows Live ID is imported into the Outlook Live domain, it is subject to the security and privacy policies of the organization.

preliminary data validation.translation: xác thực dữ liệu sơ bộ
preliminary data validation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of validating data before it is processed. This validation helps detect and exclude some errors from the intended process, which might be the import or migration of users using a CSV file, for example.

authoritative name server.translation: máy chủ phân giải tên có thẩm quyền
authoritative name server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A DNS server that is responsible for the DNS records that are associated with a domain.

calendar sharing service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows users to publish calendars on Microsoft Office Online and share them with others.

holdability.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ability of leaving result sets on hold that have been processed and are normally closed after this.

microsoft excel 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft spreadsheet software with tools for analyzing, charting, and communicating data.

microsoft excel home and student 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft spreadsheet software, with tools for analyzing, charting, and communicating data, designed for home and students.

microsoft excel mobile 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft spreadsheet software designed for use with handheld computing devices.

microsoft infopath 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft product that enables teams and organizations to create and work with rich, dynamic forms. InfoPath supports any customer-defined XML schema and integrates with Web services.

object cache live count.translation: số đối tượng hoạt động trong đệm ẩn đối tượng
object cache live count.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The total number of objects that are currently active in the object cache. These objects can quickly be retrieved from the cache.

object cache gc count.translation: số GC từ đệm ẩn đối tượng
object cache gc count.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The total number of objects from the object cache that have been removed from memory by the garbage collector.

microsoft office professional 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. office professional 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. office professional plus 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. microsoft office standard 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. office standard 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the suite of Microsoft productivity software that supports common business tasks, including word processing (Word), email (Outlook), presentations (PowerPoint), and data management and analysis (Excel).

windows phone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A phone that runs Windows 10 Mobile.

wp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The device that runs Windows Phone Operating System.

cashback.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The menu item on the Bing menu that links to http://www.bing.com/cashback/.

documents.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The link to the free online workspace for accessing, editing, and sharing Excel, Word, PowerPoint and OneNote documents across your PC, smartphone, and web browser.

do more.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Windows Mobile header link that opens a menu that contains more options.

devices.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The card that allows users to hunt for activity that poses a security threat across devices using customizable queries.

microsoft onenote 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft product that enables users to capture, organize, and reuse notes electronically on laptop computers, desktop computers, or tablet personal computers.

microsoft onenote home and student 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft product that enables users to capture, organize, and reuse notes electronically on laptop computers, desktop computers, or tablet personal computers, designed for home and students.

microsoft onenote mobile 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft software that enables users to capture, organize and reuse notes electronically, designed for use with handheld computing devices.

microsoft outlook 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft messaging and collaboration client software for personal computers accessing Microsoft Exchange Server-based email and collaboration services.

powerpoint mobile 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft presentation graphics product for creating presentations and adding graphic effects like multimedia objects and special effects with text, designed for use with handheld computing devices.

shared photos.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The link to photos that only you and people that you select can view (versus public photos that anyone can view).

pc site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Windows Mobile footer link to the site that is built for viewing from a PC.

mobile site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Windows Mobile footer link to the site that is built for viewing from mobile devices.

microsoft project professional 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft project management software used to plan, manage, and communicate a project schedule and other information among workgroup members, project managers, and other stakeholders, and providing additional collaborative enterprise project management capabilities when used with Microsoft Office Project Server 2010.

microsoft project standard 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft project management software used to plan, manage, and communicate a project schedule and other information among workgroup members, project managers, and other stakeholders.

case resolution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An activity that includes such information as the description of the resolution and the billable time of the case.

contract template.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A template that contains the standard attribute of a contract such as billing frequency and allotment type.

service calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A scheduling component that is used to view and manage appointments and service activities.

microsoft publisher 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft business desktop publishing program that enables users to easily create professional-looking marketing materials by providing built-in professional design expertise and enhanced automation tools.

microsoft visio premium 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft business diagramming and drawing software used to create charts, diagrams, and other schematic illustrations, including new templates for Business Process Modeling Notation (BPMN), Six Sigma, and Microsoft Office SharePoint Workflow, new process management tools such as subprocess to help with standardization and re-use, and rules and logic validation to ensure accuracy and consistency across the organization. microsoft visio professional 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft business diagramming and drawing software used to create charts, diagrams, and other schematic illustrations, designed for professionals in IT, engineering, and software development.

microsoft visio standard 2010.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The year 2010 edition of the Microsoft business diagramming and drawing software used to create charts, diagrams, and other schematic illustrations, designed for business users.
