call history.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The User Interface (UI) element in various communications apps and in contact cards that provides access to a list of previous communication via that app or with a particular contact.

batch job.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of computer processes that can be run without user interaction.

filtered html.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An HTML format with Microsoft Office-specific tags removed.

time stamp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A certification specifying that a particular message existed at a specific time and date. In a digital context, trusted third parties generate a trusted time stamp for a particular message by having a time stamping service append a time value to a message and then digitally signing the result.

sql-92.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The version of the SQL standard published in 1992.

marquee.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Moving text that is used on a data access page to draw the user's attention to a specific page element, such as a headline or an important announcement.

disc burner.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device used to copy files to recordable CDs and DVDs.

microsoft® office groove® server 2007 ma.translation: Trình quản lý Microsoft® Office Groove® Server 2007
microsoft® office groove® server 2007 ma.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web-based interface for managing all aspects of Microsoft Office Groove 2007 deployments. These include user account configuration, domain creation and certification, policy setting and enforcement, and reporting and compliance.

modem.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A communications device that converts between digital data from a computer or terminal and analog audio signals that can pass through a standard telephone line.

modulator/demodulator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A communications device that converts between digital data from a computer or terminal and analog audio signals that can pass through a standard telephone line.

tree diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of block diagram with tree shapes to represent hierarchies, such as family trees or tournament plans.

scroll lock key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: On the IBM PC/XT and AT and compatible keyboards, a key on the top row of the numeric keypad that controls the effect of the cursor control keys and sometimes prevents the screen from scrolling. On the enhanced and Macintosh keyboards, this key is to the right of the function keys on the top row. Many modern applications ignore the Scroll Lock setting.

nonrepeatable read.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An inconsistency that occurs when a transaction reads the same row more than once, and a separate transaction modifies that row between reads.

url smashing.translation: tạo URL từ kết hợp điều kiện truy vấn
url smashing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of matching a search string (with spaces removed) against URL addresses to return the most relevant result.

master category list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The list of categories that you can use to group items or to find items. This list contains general categories such as Business, Personal, and Phone Calls. You can add categories to and delete categories from this list.

uniqueidentifier data type.translation: loại dữ liệu mã định danh duy nhất
uniqueidentifier data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data type containing a unique identification number stored as a 16-byte binary string used for storing a globally unique identifier (GUID).

remote login identification.translation: nhận dạng đăng nhập từ xa
remote login identification.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The login identification assigned to a user for accessing remote procedures on a remote server.

web service reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A reference that enables a project to consume one or more Web services.

web reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A reference that enables a project to consume one or more Web services.

microsoft® office onenote® mobile.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Microsoft software designed for use with handheld computing devices that enables users to capture, organize and reuse notes electronically.

visited hyperlink.translation: siêu kết nối được bấm vào
visited hyperlink.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hyperlink on a Web page that a site visitor has activated by using a mouse device, keyboard, or other type of pointing device.

viewed hyperlink.translation: siêu kết nối được bấm vào
viewed hyperlink.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hyperlink on a Web page that a site visitor has activated by using a mouse device, keyboard, or other type of pointing device.

followed hyperlink.translation: siêu kết nối được bấm vào
followed hyperlink.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hyperlink on a Web page that a site visitor has activated by using a mouse device, keyboard, or other type of pointing device.

object library.translation: thư viện đối tượng, thư viện sự vật
object library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file that contains definitions of objects and their methods and properties.

unmute speakers.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A button on Audio Controls that turns off mute on the user's speakers.

pass-through query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An SQL-specific query you use to send commands directly to an ODBC database server.

cause and effect diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of diagram that documents all the factors that contribute to or affect a given situation (all the causes that lead to a certain effect).

ishikawa diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of diagram that documents all the factors that contribute to or affect a given situation (all the causes that lead to a certain effect).

fishbone diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of diagram that documents all the factors that contribute to or affect a given situation (all the causes that lead to a certain effect).

characteristic diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of diagram that documents all the factors that contribute to or affect a given situation (all the causes that lead to a certain effect).

microsoft download center.translation: Trung tâm Tải xuống của Microsoft
microsoft download center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Web site that provides product updates and security patches for Microsoft products.

information access service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A part of an IrDA infrared communication protocol used so that devices can learn about the services offered by another device.

ias.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A part of an IrDA infrared communication protocol used so that devices can learn about the services offered by another device.

affinity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: For Network Load Balancing, the method used to associate client requests to cluster hosts.

inking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of using a tablet pen to create drawings or handwriting.

file server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file-storage device on a local area network that is accessible to users on the network. A file server not only stores files but manages them and maintains order as network users request files and make changes to them.

subtext.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Part of a text.

gaussian blur.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The SVG effect that blurs an image as if it were in an out-of-focus lens.

tent card.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the page size options available in Publisher for printing a folded card. This option prints two pages per sheet of paper.

hardware failure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A malfunction of a physical component such as a disk head failure or memory error.

catalog merge area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The area in a catalog merge template into which merge fields are inserted. When a merge is completed, data from a data source populates each field, and the catalog merge area will repeat and display multiple records on each page.

precedent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cell that is referred to by a formula in another cell. For example, if cell D10 contains the formula =B5, cell B5 is a precedent to cell D10.

distributed partitioned view.translation: dạng xem chia nhỏ phân phối
distributed partitioned view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view that joins horizontally partitioned data from a set of member tables across more than one server, making the data appear as if from one table.

rs utility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Report scripting tool.

rs.exe.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Report scripting tool.

adjusted percentage.translation: tỷ lệ phần trăm điều chỉnh
adjusted percentage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount to be taken off the price of each unit of the product or service.

fixed server role.translation: vai trò máy chủ cố định
fixed server role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A predefined role that exists at the server level. The scope of the role is limited to the SQL Server instance in which it is defined.

swap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To switch between active calls.

method of contact.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The preferred method of communication with the Business Contact; for example, phone, email message, letter, fax, and so on.

brainstorming diagram.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of diagram that shows the interrelationships among topics in a hierarchy. You can think of it as a graphical illustration of a text outline.

leaf member.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A member that has no descendents.

gradient.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A gradual progression.

presence information.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of attributes that provides an indication of a person's status, activity, location, willingness to communicate, and contact information.

cabinet file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A single file that stores multiple compressed files. These files are commonly used in software installation and to reduce the file size and the associated download time for Web content.

.cab file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A single file that stores multiple compressed files. These files are commonly used in software installation and to reduce the file size and the associated download time for Web content.

interface definition language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In object-oriented programming, a language that lets a program or object written in one language communicate with another program written in an unknown language. An IDL is used to define interfaces between client and server programs. For example, an IDL can provide interfaces to remote CORBA objects.

idl.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In object-oriented programming, a language that lets a program or object written in one language communicate with another program written in an unknown language. An IDL is used to define interfaces between client and server programs. For example, an IDL can provide interfaces to remote CORBA objects.

threshold.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A filter effect in Windows Movie Maker.

threshold value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A limit against which other values can be compared. When a value crosses this limit, it can trigger an alert or other action.

html source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The unrendered HTML code including tags and syntax.

account expiration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A time limit that is applied to the life of an account, so that it can be used only for a predetermined period of time.

plug-in.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An auxiliary software component that extends or enhances the features of other software.

home server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Exchange server that contains a user's mailbox.

residential server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Exchange server that contains a user's mailbox.

quick tag tree.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The hierarchical HTML tag structure of an opened HTML document that appears in a window docked beneath the quick tag selector.

button control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical control that enables a user to provide input to an application.

detach.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To remove from association with something.

return code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In programming, a code that is used to report the outcome of a procedure or to influence subsequent events when a routine or process terminates (returns) and passes control of the system to another routine. Return codes can, for example, indicate whether an operation was successful or not and can thus be used to determine what is to be done next.

reference dimension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A relationship between a dimension and a measure group in which the dimension is coupled to the measure group through another dimension.

equipment mailbox.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of resource mailbox that is assigned to a non-location-specific resource such as a laptop projector, microphone, or company car. Equipment mailboxes can be included as resources in meeting requests, providing a simple and efficient way to utilize resources for an organization.

alphanumeric pager.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pocket-sized wireless electronic device that uses radio signals to record incoming phone numbers or short text messages. Some pagers allow users to send messages as well.

beeper.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pocket-sized wireless electronic device that uses radio signals to record incoming phone numbers or short text messages. Some pagers allow users to send messages as well.

banner advertisement.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphic ad that spans the full width of the page and is normally 120 pixels high.

banner ad.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphic ad that spans the full width of the page and is normally 120 pixels high.

activex object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object supplied by a component that supports Automation.

automation object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object supplied by a component that supports Automation.

unenforced relationship.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A link between tables that references the primary key in one table to a foreign key in another table, and which does not check the referential integrity during INSERT and UPDATE transactions.

vertical partitioning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of splitting a single table into multiple tables based on selected columns. Each of the multiple tables has the same number of rows but fewer columns.

attribute field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field in the data source that can contain data and that is an attribute, instead of an element. Attribute fields cannot contain other fields.

log entry.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A record in a log file.

mask.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A filter that selectively includes or excludes certain values.

font resource.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphic design applied to a collection of numbers, symbols, and characters and that describes a certain typeface, along with other qualities such as size, spacing, and pitch.

font.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphic design applied to a collection of numbers, symbols, and characters and that describes a certain typeface, along with other qualities such as size, spacing, and pitch.

digital signature.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data that binds a sender's identity to the information being sent. A digital signature may be bundled with any message, file, or other digitally encoded information, or transmitted separately. Digital signatures are used in public key environments and provide authentication and integrity services.

dimension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A structural attribute of a cube that organizes data into levels. For example, a Geography dimension might include the members Country, Region, State or Province, and City.

management pack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of files that you install for use with Operations Manager and that allow you to monitor applications and add functionality to Operations Manager.

line load.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A proportion of the maximum capacity of a communication circuit that is in use.

surface area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of ways in which a piece of software can be attacked.

visual total.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A displayed, aggregated cell value for a dimension member that is consistent with the displayed cell values for its displayed children.

rss subscriptions.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that enables a user to capture all of the RSS feeds they subscribe to in a folder that automatically updates at specified intervals.

zip code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In the United States, the postal code assigned to all addresses.

master database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The system database that records all the system-level information for an instance of SQL Server.

page up key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A keyboard key (often labeled "PgUp") that is often used to move the cursor up to the top of the previous page or a specific number of lines. Its function may vary in different programs.

bullet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A typographical symbol, such as a filled or empty circle, diamond, box, or asterisk, used to set off a small block of text or each item in a list.

bullet character.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A typographical symbol, such as a filled or empty circle, diamond, box, or asterisk, used to set off a small block of text or each item in a list.

bullet image.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A typographical symbol, such as a filled or empty circle, diamond, box, or asterisk, used to set off a small block of text or each item in a list.

conferencing information.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The identifier, password, and any other information that a user needs to participate in a conference that is conducted through a conferencing service provider.

open opportunity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An opportunity that has not yet been won or lost and is at any of the following sales stages: prospecting, qualification, needs analysis, proposal, price quote, negotiation, or review.

policy bar code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An image that encodes a unique identifier for a Windows SharePoint Services object, where the value of the unique identifier can also be represented textually.

digital signature standard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard that uses the Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) for its signature algorithm and Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-1) as its message hash algorithm. DSA is a public-key cipher that is used only to generate digital signatures and cannot be used for data encryption.

dss.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of programs and related data designed to help with analysis and decision making. A decision support system provides more help in formulating decisions than a management information system (MIS) or an executive information system (EIS). It includes a database, a body of knowledge about the subject area, a "language" used to formulate problems and questions, and a modeling program for testing alternative decisions.

battery.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A power source for a portable device.

crop.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To trim the vertical or horizontal edges of an object. Pictures are often cropped to focus attention on a particular area.

desired zone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The zone in which AppleTalk network integration appears on the network.

tracer token.translation: mã thông báo bộ tạo dấu vết
tracer token.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A performance monitoring tool available for transactional replication. A token (a small amount of data) is sent through the replication system to measure the amount of time it takes for transactions to reach the Distributor and Subscribers.

drawing explorer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window that shows a hierarchical view of a document and updates to reflect the current drawing hierarchy as items (such as shapes or pages) are added or deleted.

data encryption key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A bit string that is used in conjunction with an encryption algorithm to encrypt and decrypt data.

dek.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A bit string that is used in conjunction with an encryption algorithm to encrypt and decrypt data.

encryption key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A bit string that is used in conjunction with an encryption algorithm to encrypt and decrypt data.

indexed view.translation: dạng xem được lập chỉ mục
indexed view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view with a unique clustered index applied on it to improve the performance of some types of queries.

task object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Data Transformation Services (DTS) object that defines pieces of work to be performed as part of the data transformation process. For example, a task can execute an SQL statement or move and transform heterogeneous data from an OLE DB source to an OLE DB destination using the DTS Data Pump.

permissions level.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The extent of access a user has to a site. The default permissions levels are Read, Edit, Design, and Full Control.

dynamic locking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process used by SQL Server to determine the most cost-effective locks to use at any one time.

capitalized.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Written or printed with an initial capital or in capitals.

dial by name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that enables a caller to enter a person’s name using the keys on a telephone.

range partitioning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A way of partitioning a table or index by specifying partitions to hold rows with ranges of values from a single partitioning column.

safeguard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technology, policy, or procedure that counters a threat or protects assets.

managed property.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A property that defines how items will be saved to the search index, how you may search for the property and whether or not the property is shown in search results.

normal style.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default paragraph style used in documents based on the Normal template (Normal.dot).

dial-up.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or being a connection that uses the public switched telephone network rather than a dedicated circuit or some other type of private network.

config file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file that contains machine-readable operating specifications for a piece of hardware or software or that contains information on another file or on a specific user, such as the user's logon ID.

paragraph formatting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Formatting that controls the appearance of a paragraph. Examples include indentation, alignment, line spacing, and pagination.

rdf site summary.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based syndication technology that enables websites to distribute content, such as news headlines and blog posts, efficiently to readers.

really simple syndication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based syndication technology that enables websites to distribute content, such as news headlines and blog posts, efficiently to readers.

rich site summary.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based syndication technology that enables websites to distribute content, such as news headlines and blog posts, efficiently to readers.

rss.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based syndication technology that enables websites to distribute content, such as news headlines and blog posts, efficiently to readers.

ip spoofing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The act of inserting a false sender IP address into an Internet transmission in order to gain unauthorized access to a computer system.

distinguished folder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A folder in a mailbox that can be referenced by Web services requests to identify a folder by name.

mirror server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a database mirroring configuration, the server instance where the mirror database resides. The mirror server is the mirroring partner whose copy of the database is currently the mirror database. The mirror server is a hot standby server.

plan cache.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of the SQL Server memory pool that is used to store execution plans for Transact-SQL batches, stored procedures, and triggers.

procedure cache.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of the SQL Server memory pool that is used to store execution plans for Transact-SQL batches, stored procedures, and triggers.

unbound report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report that isn't connected to a record source such as a table, query, or SQL statement.

subject line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The part of a message header that is used by the sender to indicate the object of the message.

a-d converter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that converts a continuously varying (analog) signal, such as sound or voltage, from a monitoring instrument to binary code for use by a computer.

analog-to-digital converter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that converts a continuously varying (analog) signal, such as sound or voltage, from a monitoring instrument to binary code for use by a computer.

matrix data region.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report item on a report layout that displays data in a variable columnar format.

clipboard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An area of storage for objects, data, or their references after a user carries out a Cut or Copy command.

rdbms.translation: hệ thống quản lý cơ sở dữ liệu tương quan
rdbms.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database system that organizes data into related rows and columns as specified by a relational model.

relational database management system.translation: hệ thống quản lý cơ sở dữ liệu tương quan
relational database management system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database system that organizes data into related rows and columns as specified by a relational model.

service level.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The level of support that customer service is required to provide for a case. The service contract a customer purchases determines the service level for its associated cases.

jscript.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An interpreted, object-based scripting language that borrows from C, C++, and Java. It is the Microsoft implementation of the ECMA 262 language specification.

dll.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An operating system feature that allows executable routines (generally serving a specific function or set of functions) to be stored separately as files with .dll extensions. These routines are loaded only when needed by the program that calls them.

dynamic-link library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An operating system feature that allows executable routines (generally serving a specific function or set of functions) to be stored separately as files with .dll extensions. These routines are loaded only when needed by the program that calls them.

numeric keypad.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A calculator-style block of keys, usually at the right side of a keyboard, that can be used to enter numbers.

pdf.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Adobe specification for electronic documents that use the Adobe Acrobat family of servers and readers.

portable document format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Adobe specification for electronic documents that use the Adobe Acrobat family of servers and readers.

dial plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A grouping of telephony users with some specific properties, such as unique telephone extension numbers, that allow the Private Branch eXchange (PBX) to determine what action to take with dialed digits.

picture placeholder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A rectangle that represents an imported graphic in your document. You can increase scrolling speed by temporarily replacing graphics with picture placeholders.

current region.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The block of filled-in cells that includes the currently selected cell or cells. The region extends in all directions to the first empty row or column.

property fields.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: independent attributes associated with items, or members, in an OLAP cube. For example, if city items have size and population properties stored in the server cube, a PivotTable report can display the size and population of each city.

sharing invitation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A notification for sharing items, such as calendars, documents or folders, with others.

transmission.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The sending of information over a communications line or a circuit.

flyer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A circular or pamphlet for distribution, normally used for advertisements.

real time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The actual time in which events occur.

pivottable report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An interactive, cross tabulated Excel report that summarizes and analyzes data, such as database records, from various sources including ones external to Excel.

property set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of properties.

command language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of keywords and expressions that are accepted as valid by the command interpreter.

component platform interface.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A programming interface used to build and maintain unattended installation answer files and configuration sets by adding security fixes, changing drivers, and so forth.

absolute cell reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An address of a cell in a worksheet that does not change when the address is copied to a new cell.

absolute reference.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An address of a cell in a worksheet that does not change when the address is copied to a new cell.

mirrored media set.translation: tập phương tiện được phản chiếu
mirrored media set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A media set that contains two to four identical copies (mirrors) of each media family. Restore operations require only one mirror per family, allowing a damaged media volume to be replaced by the corresponding volume from a mirror.

active statement.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A SQL statement that has been run but whose result set has not yet been canceled or fully processed.

notes e-mailed to me.translation: Nhắc tôi về email đã gửi
notes e-mailed to me.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The folder that contains any .one files that have been sent to you as an email message attachment.

flagged.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Marked with a flag.

installed language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The base language used that governs how several language characteristics will behave, such as the language of the primary dictionary, and the direction and alignment of text (left-to-right or right-to-left).

architecture.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The physical construction or design of a computer system and its components.

high-low lines.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In 2-D line charts, lines that extend from the highest to the lowest value in each category. High-low lines are often used in stock charts.

drawing object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any graphic you draw or insert, which can be changed and enhanced. Drawing objects include AutoShapes, curves, lines, and WordArt.

gloss optimizer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pigment ink/cartridge used in digital printing which provides resistance to water, fading and smudging, thus producing photographic prints with uniform gloss coverage.

text placeholder.translation: chỗ dành sẵn cho văn bản
text placeholder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A symbolic value used instead of a real value which in this case is text.

signed integer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An integer that has a positive or negative sign.

user principal name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user account name (sometimes referred to as the user logon name) and a domain name identifying the domain in which the user account is located and which is the standard usage for logging on to a Windows domain.

upn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user account name (sometimes referred to as the user logon name) and a domain name identifying the domain in which the user account is located and which is the standard usage for logging on to a Windows domain.

polling query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A singleton query that returns a value Analysis Services can use to determine if changes have been made to a table or other relational object.

handout.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A printed version of a presentation that can include multiple slides per page and space for audience notes.

client computer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity, such as a device or program, that connects to another entity over a network.

cost accounting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The branch of accounting concerned with identifying and evaluating the cost of producing a product.

child category.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity used in catalogs to group a set of products together in a hierarchy. A child category is a subordinate of a parent category. For example, Music is a parent category, and Rock, Country, and Classical are child categories. You create parent and child categories to organize the products displayed on your site.

vector markup language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based specification for the exchange, editing, and delivery of 2-D vector graphics on the Web. An application of XML (Extensible Markup Language), VML uses XML tags and Cascading Style Sheets to create and place vector graphics, such as circles and squares, in an XML or HTML document, such as a Web page. These graphics, which are rendered in the native operating system, can include color and are editable in a variety of graphics programs.

vml.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An XML-based specification for the exchange, editing, and delivery of 2-D vector graphics on the Web. An application of XML (Extensible Markup Language), VML uses XML tags and Cascading Style Sheets to create and place vector graphics, such as circles and squares, in an XML or HTML document, such as a Web page. These graphics, which are rendered in the native operating system, can include color and are editable in a variety of graphics programs.

note-taking tool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that enables users to capture notes, such as text, images, audio, video and Web content.

trail byte.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The byte value that is the second half of a double-byte character.

shrink.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To remove unused space from data tables.

network load balancing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows network component that uses a distributed algorithm to load-balance Internet Protocol (IP) traffic across a number of hosts, helping to enhance the scalability and availability of mission-critical, IP-based services, such as Remote Desktop Services, Web services, virtual private networking, and streaming media. It also provides high availability by detecting host failures and automatically redistributing traffic to the surviving hosts.

nlb.rule: Microsoft Terminology. meet now.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature of meeting applications that allows users to instantly invite others to join a meeting, e.g. by creating a URL for the meeting.

isdn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A high-speed digital technology that uses existing telephone lines to provide Internet access.

fraction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A number that is not a whole number, such as ½ (vulgar fraction) or 0.5 (decimal fraction), formed by dividing one quantity into another.

external user.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An anonymous user who connects to an account from outside the firewall.

format bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A toolbar within an application used for modifying the format of the document being displayed, such as changing font size or type.

default hyperlink.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In an image map, the hyperlink that site visitors follow when they click an area of the picture where there are no hot spots.

metadata.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Information about the properties or structure of data that is not part of the values the data contains.

sign in as.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The label for the list that enables a user to select a status before signing in. Possible status options are Available, Busy, Do Not Disturb, and so on.

video game.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A class of computer programs in which one or more users interact with the computer as a form of entertainment.

game.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A class of computer programs in which one or more users interact with the computer as a form of entertainment.

direct memory access.rule: Microsoft Terminology. familiar office program.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the classic Microsoft applications that can be considered to be easily recognizable by consumers. For example, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

multiserver administration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of automating administration across multiple instances of SQL Server.

uncompress.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To restore the contents of a compressed file to its original form.

counter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that is used on a Web page to count the number of times that the Web page was accessed.

left align.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To align text along the left margin.

isochronous.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to processes where data must be delivered within certain time constraints. media family.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data written by a backup operation to a backup device used by a media set. enter key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The key that is used at the end of a line or command to instruct the computer to process the command or text. In word processing programs, the Enter key is used at the end of a paragraph. Also called: Return key.

partial database restore.translation: khôi phục cơ sở dữ liệu một phần

regression.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The statistical process of predicting one or more continuous variables, such as profit or loss, based on other attributes in the dataset.

snapshot replication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A replication in which data is distributed exactly as it appears at a specific moment in time and does not monitor for updates to the data.

code page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A table that relates the character codes (code point values) used by a program to keys on the keyboard or to characters on the display. This provides support for character sets and keyboard layouts for different countries or regions.

fraudulent.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Engaging in fraud or deceptive.

hold status.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The status of a feature to exempt items on SPS from being subject to the policy set on the site.

source document.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The document where a linked or embedded object was originally created.

page orientation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The direction a publication will be printed on a sheet of paper. You can choose either portrait, which is the taller-than-wide orientation, or landscape, which is the wider-than-tall orientation.

purble pairs.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A part of the Purble Place game where the player has to flip a tile over to reveal a picture, and then try to find its match somewhere else.

activity indicator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An indicator that provides the user with information about the state of a process.

remote data.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Data stored in an OLE DB data source that is separate from the current instance of SQL Server.

redo phase.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The phase during recovery that applies (rolls forward) logged changes to a database to bring the data forward in time.

conditional expression.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An expression which results in a true or false value when calculated.

boolean expression.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An expression which results in a true or false value when calculated.

title area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The area at the top of a Windows Journal note where you can write a title. The title appears as the suggested file name when you save the note.

literal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A value used exactly as you see it.

summary.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A shortened version of information that contains only the main points.

optional.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to a component, parameter and so on that is not required or automatic.

small caps.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A font effect in which lowercase text appears as capital letters in a reduced font size.

standard keyboard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An input device that consists of individual keys and that is used to convey information from the user to a computer or data communication circuit.

wait state.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A processing cycle of the microprocessor during which it only waits for data from an input/output device or from memory. While a single wait state is not humanly perceptible, the cumulative effect of wait states is to slow system performance.

dimmed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to the state of a control in which normal functionality is not available to a user.

managing editor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A label that refers to the email address of the person responsible for editorial content.

my reports.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A personalized workspace.

master key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The key used by the client and server for all session key generation. The master key is used to generate the client-read key, the client-write key, the server-read key, and the server-write key. Master keys can be exported as simple key BLOBs.

role-playing dimension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A single database dimension joined to the fact table on a different foreign keys to produce multiple cube dimensions.

search folders.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A search folder created in Outlook that provides a view of all email items matching specific search criteria and where the items are still stored in one or more Outlook folder.

access code.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A string of characters entered by a user to verify his or her identity to a network or to a local computer, device, or client, or to sign in to an account, app, and so on.

web restrictions.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of Parental Controls that allows users to block Web sites that they don't want to view.

x.400.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An international messaging standard that can be used by a variety of messaging systems. X.400 uses a strict addressing method that reflects a hierarchical environment. The use of X.400 has been largely supplanted by the combination of SMTP and MIME.

drag.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To move an item on the screen (1) by touching the item on a screen and then sliding the finger across the screen or (2) by pressing and holding down the left mouse button while moving the mouse.

clickthrough rate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of times an ad was clicked, divided by the number of times the ad was shown (impressions).

low vision.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Visual impairment that results in great reduction in vision capabilities and that cannot be aided by glasses or contact lenses. It could, however, be aided by special devices.

cal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A license that specifies the number of computers that can connect to and use software located on a server.

client access license.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A license that specifies the number of computers that can connect to and use software located on a server.

directory management service.translation: Dịch vụ Quản lý Danh bạ

motion path.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The path that a specified object or text will follow as part of an animation sequence for a slide.

content library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data repository, in which items such as text, text boxes, pictures, tables, shapes, etc. can be stored and re-used within the same document and across multiple documents.

router.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that sends, or routes, information between two networks (for example, between a home network and the Internet).

banded.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Characterized by row or column-specific formatting. Often describes rows or columns of data that use alternating colors or shading to enhance readability.

referenced key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A primary key or unique key referenced by a foreign key.

base object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The object that a synonym references.

business tools menu.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The menu on the Outlook menu bar that provides access to Business Contact Manager functions.

locale.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of rules and data specific to a language and a geographic area. Locales include information on sorting rules, date and time formatting, numeric and monetary conventions, and character classification.

constrained delegation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ability to specify that a service or computer account can perform Kerberos delegation to a limited set of services.

tablet pc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A portable computer that allows you to write on or interact with the screen.

tablet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A portable computer that allows you to write on or interact with the screen.

initial snapshot.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Files that include schema and data, constraints, extended properties, indexes, triggers, and system tables that are necessary for replication.

subscriber access number.translation: số truy cập của thuê bao

cascading delete.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: For relationships that enforce referential integrity between tables, the deletion of all related records in the related table or tables when a record in the primary table is deleted.

cascade delete.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: For relationships that enforce referential integrity between tables, the deletion of all related records in the related table or tables when a record in the primary table is deleted.

cd burner speed.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The speed at which the CD drive will record the data.

tts.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to technologies for converting textual (ASCII) information into synthetic speech output. Used in voice-processing applications requiring production of broad, unrelated, and unpredictable vocabularies, such as products in a catalog or names and addresses. recurrence.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The regular pattern according to which a scheduled appointment or task is repeated.

effective.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Capable of producing successful results.

nest.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To embed one construct inside another. severe error.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An error that can cause serious problems and is difficult to repair.

source program.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The program used to create a linked object or embedded object. To edit the object, you must have the source program installed on your computer.

development accelerator core.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An integrated set of Microsoft components, templates, and guidance designed to solve specific customer business problems.

development accelerator extended.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An integrated set of Microsoft components, templates, and guidance designed to solve specific customer business problems.

solution accelerator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An integrated set of Microsoft components, templates, and guidance designed to solve specific customer business problems.

virus scanning api.translation: Hệ Giao tiếp Lập trình Ứng dụng Quét Virút

vsapi.translation: Hệ Giao tiếp Lập trình Ứng dụng Quét Virút
vsapi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A virus-scanning API that is used by third-party antivirus service providers to protect computers that have the Exchange Server 2007 Mailbox server role installed.

create new group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A menu item that creates a new group for the user's Contacts list.

magazine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An electronic publication distributed primarily through the World Wide Web, rather than as an ink-on-paper magazine.

web magazine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An electronic publication distributed primarily through the World Wide Web, rather than as an ink-on-paper magazine.

implicit cursor conversion.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The return of a different type of cursor than the user had declared.

cursor degradation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The return of a different type of cursor than the user had declared.

field data types.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A characteristic of a field that determines what kind of data it can store. For example, a field whose data type is Text can store data consisting of either text or number characters, but a Number field can only store numerical data.

business contact manager toolbar.translation: Thanh công cụ Business Contact Manager
business contact manager toolbar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The toolbar at the top of an item where you can view existing links or create new links to Account, Business Contact, Opportunity, or Business Project records.

input scope.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The type of handwritten or voice-dictated value being entered in an input control on the TabletPC, for example, Number, Date or Currency. This allows for better and faster recognition by the TabletPC recognizer.

non-working time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Time devoted to non-work activities. Out-of-office time.

nonworking time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Time devoted to non-work activities. Out-of-office time.

text attributes.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any characteristic of text, such as font, size, style, color, or effect such as subscript or superscript.

client subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription to a merge publication that uses the priority value of the Publisher for conflict detection and resolution.

local subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription to a merge publication that uses the priority value of the Publisher for conflict detection and resolution.

opportunity record.translation: Hồ sơ Lưu trữ Thông tin Cơ hội
opportunity record.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The location for storing opportunity information, including information that is entered on the Opportunity form, linked records, and history items.

drilldown.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To navigate through levels of data starting from the most summarized (up) to the most detailed (down).

drill down.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To navigate through levels of data starting from the most summarized (up) to the most detailed (down).

union query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query that uses the UNION operator to combine the results of two or more select queries.

pull subscription.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subscription created and administered at the Subscriber. The Distribution Agent or Merge Agent for the subscription runs at the Subscriber.

three-factor authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. security principal.translation: chủ thể an toàn thông tin
security principal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Windows-based computers, an account (such as a user, security group, device, or computer) that can be granted or denied access to resources.

principal.translation: chủ thể an toàn thông tin
principal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In Windows-based computers, an account (such as a user, security group, device, or computer) that can be granted or denied access to resources.

bottleneck.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A condition, usually involving a hardware resource, that causes a computer to perform poorly.

flow dimension member.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any of the different members of the Flow dimension.

exchange rate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The rate at which the currency of one country or region can be traded against that of another country or region.

semiadditive measure.translation: số đo phân nửa bổ sung
semiadditive measure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A measure that can be summed along one or more, but not all, dimensions in a cube.

sample application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: End-to-end, compilable application that uses many technologies and is designed as teaching sample or commercial utility for which the code is made available for learning and re-use.

pre-built application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: End-to-end, compilable application that uses many technologies and is designed as teaching sample or commercial utility for which the code is made available for learning and re-use.

report history.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of previously run copies of a report.

bootstrap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of starting or resetting a computer or a device. When first turned on (cold boot) or reset (warm boot), the computer runs the software that loads and starts the computer's operating system, which prepares it for use.

startup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of starting or resetting a computer or a device. When first turned on (cold boot) or reset (warm boot), the computer runs the software that loads and starts the computer's operating system, which prepares it for use.

supplier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A person or company providing products or services.

routing group connector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An SMTP connector that is required for mail to flow between Exchange routing groups. When Exchange Server 2007 is installed in an existing Exchange Server 2003 and Exchange 2000 Server organization, the required routing group connector is created during setup.

skewed fraction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A fraction that is written on a downward angle: the diagonal fraction bar is placed down and to the right of the numerator, and the denominator is slightly down and to the right of the fraction bar.

data source driver.translation: trình điều khiển nguồn dữ liệu
data source driver.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program file used to connect to a specific database. Each database program or management system requires a different driver.

kerberos.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An authentication protocol that provides a mechanism for mutual authentication between a client and a server, or between one server and another, before a network connection is opened between them.

kerberos authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An authentication protocol that provides a mechanism for mutual authentication between a client and a server, or between one server and another, before a network connection is opened between them.

colleagues.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The privacy relationship setting that allows a medium amount of information to be viewed, typically for people in your company and for people outside your company who work with you.

recordset.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ActiveX Database Objects (ADO) object used to contain a result set. It also exhibits cursor behavior depending on the recordset properties set by an application. ADO recordsets are mapped to OLE DB rowsets.

submit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To send something in for consideration.

slide library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A folder where a collection of PowerPoint slides is shared.

dash.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A short horizontal line used as a punctuation mark.

operand.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item on either side of an operator in a formula.

event table.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A table in the application database that stores event data.

infrastructure master.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A domain controller that holds the infrastructure operations master role in Active Directory. The infrastructure master updates the group-to-user reference whenever group memberships change and replicates these changes across the domain. At any time, the infrastructure master role can be assigned to only one domain controller in each domain.

exchange web services.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of features that provides a programming interface for accessing Microsoft Exchange data through the Client Access server role by using Web services.

generator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The component of Notification Services that matches events to subscriptions and produces notifications.

layout preview.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that uses a minimum amount of data to display the general layout of a report.

partitioning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of replacing a table with multiple smaller tables.

workflow rule.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of action steps in a business process or sales process. A workflow rule specifies the required activities for a workflow and the order in which those activities must be performed.

microsoft sequence clustering algorithm.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The algorithm that is a combination of sequence analysis with clustering and can be used to identify clusters of similarly ordered events in a sequence.

document object model.translation: Mô hình Đối tượng Tài liệu
document object model.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A World Wide Web Consortium specification that describes the structure of dynamic HTML and XML documents in a way that allows them to be manipulated through a Web browser.

dom.translation: Mô hình Đối tượng Tài liệu
dom.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A World Wide Web Consortium specification that describes the structure of dynamic HTML and XML documents in a way that allows them to be manipulated through a Web browser.

column guide.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A vertical layout guide that is used to divide a publication page into two or more columns.

subreport control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that displays a subform in a form or a subform or a subreport in a report.

subform control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control that displays a subform in a form or a subform or a subreport in a report.

anonymous replica.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special type of replica in which you don't keep track of individual users.

certificate issuer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The certification authority which issued the certificate to the subject.

windows management instrumentation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft extension to the Distributed Management Task Force (DMTF) Web-based Enterprise Management (WBEM) initiative.

wmi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft extension to the Distributed Management Task Force (DMTF) Web-based Enterprise Management (WBEM) initiative.

availability indicator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Appears to the left of a meeting or appointment (or all the way around the item when selected), indicating time status as free, tentative, busy, out of office, or no information available. Visible only in Day and Work Week view.

global assembly cache.translation: bộ đệm ẩn hợp ngữ chung
global assembly cache.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer-wide code cache that stores assemblies specifically installed to be shared by many applications on the computer.

natural hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hiearchy in which at every level there is a one-to-many relationship between members in that level and members in the next lower level.

clear.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To remove the data or settings currently present on an entity.

calculation subcube.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of multidimensional cube cells that is used to create a calculated cells definition. The set of cells is defined by a combination of MDX set expressions.

rule firing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of running one of the application rules (event chronicle rules, subscription event rules, and subscription scheduled rules) defined in the application definition file.

data processing extension.translation: mở rộng xử lý dữ liệu
data processing extension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A plug-in that processes data for a specific kind of data source (similar to a database driver).

fine-grained permissions.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A security feature that allows for greater granularity and customization of user permissions.

recovery branch.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A range of LSNs that share the same recovery branch GUID. A new recovery branch originates when a database is created or when RESTORE WITH RECOVERY generates a recovery fork. A multiple-branch recovery path is possible that includes ranges of LSNs that cover two or more recovery fork points.

directory service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A service that provides access to data and objects in a directory or network environment.

memory mapped file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file whose contents are associated with a portion of the virtual address space of a process. It can be used to share a file or memory between two or more processes.

mapped file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file whose contents are associated with a portion of the virtual address space of a process. It can be used to share a file or memory between two or more processes.

recovery path.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The sequence of data and log backups that have brought a database to a particular point in time (known as a recovery point). A recovery path is a specific set of transformations that have evolved the database over time, yet have maintained the consistency of the database. A recovery path describes a range of LSNs from a start point (LSN,GUID) to an end point (LSN,GUID). The range of LSNs in a recovery path can traverse one or more recovery branches from start to end.

portable network graphics.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphic file format that is supported by some World Wide Web browsers. PNG supports variable transparency of images (alpha channels) and control of image brightness on different computers (gamma correction). PNG files are compressed bitmaps.

png.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphic file format that is supported by some World Wide Web browsers. PNG supports variable transparency of images (alpha channels) and control of image brightness on different computers (gamma correction). PNG files are compressed bitmaps.

absolute value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The magnitude of a number, irrespective of its sign (+ or -). An absolute value is always greater than or equal to zero. For example, 10 is the absolute value of 10 and of -10. Programming languages and spreadsheet programs commonly include functions that return the absolute value of a number.

un-sign.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To remove the digital signature added to the document.

custom toolbar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A toolbar that you create for your application.

scheduling and delivery processor.translation: Bộ xử lý Đặt lịch và Phân phối
scheduling and delivery processor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component of the report server engine that handles scheduling and delivery. Works with SQL Agent.

subroutine.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A common term for routine, likely to be used in reference to shorter, general, frequently called routines.

associated pivottable report.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The PivotTable report that supplies the source data to the PivotChart report. It is created automatically when you create a new PivotChart report. When you change the layout of either report, the other also changes.

rack-mounted.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Built for installation in a metal frame or cabinet of standard width (typically 19 inches or 23 inches) and mounting arrangements.

loopback address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The address of the local computer used for routing outgoing packets back to the source computer. This address is used primarily for testing.

global replica.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A replica in which changes are fully tracked and can be exchanged with any global replica in the set. A global replica can also exchange changes with any local or anonymous replicas for which it becomes the hub.

link bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of buttons representing hyperlinks to pages both within a Web site and to external sites.

virtual.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of or pertaining to a device or service that appears to the user as something it actually is not or that does not physically exist.

equijoin.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A join in which the values in the columns being joined are compared for equality, and all columns are included in the results.

add-on device.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A device that is added to the base computer system to increase functionality, such as audio, networking, graphics, or SCSI controller.

customer experience improvement program.translation: Chương trình Cải thiện Trải nghiệm Khách hàng

This information is anonymous and voluntary, and is used strictly for the purposes of software development.

ceip.translation: Chương trình Cải thiện Trải nghiệm Khách hàng
