stand-alone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or being a device that does not require support from another device or system, for example, a computer that is not connected to a network.

standalone.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or being a device that does not require support from another device or system, for example, a computer that is not connected to a network.

building blocks organizer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows users to preview, edit or delete building blocks in a variety of galleries, and insert them into the current document.

dial-up networking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An application that enables remote users to connect to a network.

dun.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An application that enables remote users to connect to a network.

run-time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Occurring after a program has begun to be executed, such as evaluation of variable expressions and dynamic allocation of memory.

column delimiter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A character which separates columns from each other in the CSV file being imported/exported.

directory control block.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An internal NT file system (NTFS) structure in which the file system maintains the state for an open instance of a directory file.

dcb.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An internal NT file system (NTFS) structure in which the file system maintains the state for an open instance of a directory file.

microsoft knowledge base.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft Web site that provides customers with access to a database of articles written by Microsoft Support professionals.

dataset.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of related information made up of separate elements that can be treated as a unit in data handling.

business tool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item that is frequently accessed when using Business Contact Manager for Outlook and that is often listed on the Business Tools menu.

visual basic editor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An environment in which you write new and edit existing Visual Basic for Applications code and procedures. The Visual Basic Editor contains a complete debugging toolset for finding syntax, run-time, and logic problems in your code.

fat32.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A derivative of the file allocation table (FAT) file system. FAT32 supports smaller cluster sizes and larger volumes than FAT, which results in more efficient space allocation on FAT32 volumes.

service set identifier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unique set of letters or numbers that identifies a wireless network. For a computer or device to connect to a wireless network, it must supply that network’s SSID. An SSID can be up to 32 characters.

ssid.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unique set of letters or numbers that identifies a wireless network. For a computer or device to connect to a wireless network, it must supply that network’s SSID. An SSID can be up to 32 characters.

network service set identifier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unique set of letters or numbers that identifies a wireless network. For a computer or device to connect to a wireless network, it must supply that network’s SSID. An SSID can be up to 32 characters.

changed lines.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Vertical lines appearing next to text that has been added, deleted, or changed by using tracked changes. You can specify that changed lines appear to the left or right of text. You can also hide changed lines.

discussion entry.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message that appears in a newsgroup, public folder, or other forum, such as Facebook or Twitter, accessible by a number of individuals.

information.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The meaning of data as it is intended to be interpreted by people.

foreign address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any address type that the MS Mail postoffice does not have a gateway or access component installed for routing.

multicast address resolution service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A service for resolving multicast IP addresses to the asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) addresses of the clients that have joined that multicast group. MARS can work in conjunction with the multicast server (MCS) and clients to distribute multicast data through point-to-multipoint connections.

mars.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A service for resolving multicast IP addresses to the asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) addresses of the clients that have joined that multicast group. MARS can work in conjunction with the multicast server (MCS) and clients to distribute multicast data through point-to-multipoint connections.

secondary server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a log shipping configuration, the server instance where the secondary database resides. At regular intervals, the secondary server copies the latest log backup from the primary database and restores the log to the secondary database. The secondary server is a warm standby server.

base 2.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Having two components, alternatives, or outcomes. The binary number system has 2 as its base, so values are expressed as combinations of two digits, 0 and 1. These two digits can represent the logical values true and false as well as numerals, and they can be represented in an electronic device by the two states on and off, recognized as two voltage levels. Therefore, the binary number system is at the heart of digital computing.

posterize.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A filter effect in Windows Movie Maker.

default device.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The device that Lync and Communicator uses by default when the user places a call (either PBX telephone phone or computer through a VOIP connection).

folder tree.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hierarchy of folders in the Exchange store very similar in structure to the standard file system. A single folder can contain child folders, which, in turn, can contain other child folders.

content index server.translation: máy chủ chỉ mục nội dung
content index server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server that is dedicated to creating and updating context indexes.

mbr disk.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A disk that uses the master boot record (MBR) partition style.

report module.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A module that includes code for all event procedures triggered by events occurring on a specific report or its controls.

insert values query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query (SQL statement) that creates a new row and inserts values into specified columns.

adjusted price value.translation: giá trị của giá điều chỉnh
adjusted price value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Similar to adjusted price, except it is not displayed in the local currency (that is, there is no currency associated with the price).

strikethrough.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to a formatting style in which characters are crossed out by horizontal line.

supplement.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any software update or new intellectual property such as a driver, connector, development kit, guidance, or tool.

message policy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of rules that are applied to email messages. These rules govern how messages are processed and stored, based on a set of requirements. The requirements are typically based on regulatory requirements for an industry or geographic region.

orchestration designer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphical user-interface tool used to design and implement business processes.

history list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of the last 10 files you jumped to in the current program session using hyperlinks.

disk cache.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A portion of a computer's random access memory (RAM) set aside for temporarily holding information read from disk. A disk cache does not hold entire files, as does a RAM disk (a portion of memory that acts as if it were a disk drive). Instead, a disk cache is used to hold information that either has recently been requested from disk or has previously been written to disk. If the required information remains in a disk cache, access time is considerably faster than if the program must wait for the disk drive mechanism to fetch the information from disk.

code stub.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A segment of Visual Basic code that defines the beginning and end of a procedure.

rsconfig utility.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Server connection management tool.

rsconfig.exe.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Server connection management tool.

digital fingerprint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A long, random-looking string of letters and numbers (with punctuation marks for readability) that is used to authenticate the real-world identities of Groove contacts you see in workspaces and contact lists.

business contact.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An individual who is interested in doing business or who currently does business with your organization. A contact may or may not be part of a larger organization (account).

excel on the web.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Office Online application that enables users to view, create, share, and collaborate on Excel documents in a Web browser.

microsoft excel on the web.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Office Online application that enables users to view, create, share, and collaborate on Excel documents in a Web browser.

excel for the web.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The Microsoft Office Online application that enables users to view, create, share, and collaborate on Excel documents in a Web browser.

active directory service interfaces.translation: Giao diện Dịch vụ Active Directory
active directory service interfaces.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A directory service model and a set of Component Object Model (COM) interfaces. ADSI enables Windows applications and Active Directory clients to access several network directory services, including Active Directory.

adsi.translation: Giao diện Dịch vụ Active Directory
adsi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A directory service model and a set of Component Object Model (COM) interfaces. ADSI enables Windows applications and Active Directory clients to access several network directory services, including Active Directory.

ntext.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A variable-length data type that can hold a maximum of 2^30 - 1 (1,073,741,823) characters.

extended stored procedure.translation: thủ tục đã lưu trữ mở rộng
extended stored procedure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A function in a dynamic link library (DLL) that is coded using the SQL Server Extended Stored Procedure API. The function can then be invoked from Transact-SQL using the same statements that are used to execute Transact-SQL stored procedures.

pstn.translation: Mạng điện thoại chuyển mạch công cộng
pstn.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The network of standard analog telephone lines, available worldwide.

public switched telephone network.translation: Mạng điện thoại chuyển mạch công cộng
public switched telephone network.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The network of standard analog telephone lines, available worldwide.

initial synchronization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The first synchronization for a subscription, during which system tables and other objects that are required by replication, and the schema and data for each article, are copied to the Subscriber.

xml path language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A language used to address parts of an XML document. XPath also provides basic facilities for manipulation of strings, numbers, and Boolean values.

xpath.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A language used to address parts of an XML document. XPath also provides basic facilities for manipulation of strings, numbers, and Boolean values.

default value.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A value that is automatically entered in a field or control when you add a new record. You can either accept the default value or override it by typing a value.

synchronization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of reconciling the differences between data stored in one location and a copy of the same data stored in another location.

data synchronization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of reconciling the differences between data stored in one location and a copy of the same data stored in another location.

appointment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An activity represented by a time interval that has a start time, an end time, and a duration.

client cursor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cursor that is implemented on the client. The entire result set is first transferred to the client, and the client API software implements the cursor functionality from this cached result set.

relationship object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An object representing a pair of objects that assume a role in relation to each other.

optional section.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control on a form that contains other controls and that usually does not appear by default. Users can insert and remove optional sections when filling out the form.

crash.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: For a system or program, to fail to function correctly, resulting in the suspension of operation.

live link.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A connection between an element in a hypertext document, such as a word, phrase, symbol, or image, and a different element in the document or in another location, a webpage, file, or script.

static row filter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A filter available for all types of replication that allows you to restrict the data replicated to a Subscriber based on a WHERE clause.

microsoft time series algorithm.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The algorithm that uses a linear regression decision tree approach to analyze time-related data, such as monthly sales data or yearly profits. The patterns it discovers can be used to predict values for future time steps.

global menu bar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A special custom menu bar that replaces the built-in menu bar in all windows in your application, except where you've specified a custom menu bar for a form or report.

forward-only cursor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cursor that cannot be scrolled; rows can be read only in sequence from the first row to the last row.

foreign computer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A computer that uses another message queuing system but, through a connector application, can exchange messages with computers that run Message Queuing.

delivery channel type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The protocol for a delivery channel, such as Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) or File.

report header.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A report section used to place information, such as a title, date, or report introduction, at the beginning of a report.

turbulence force.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A parameter in the Perlin Noise function which is used to scale the amount of force from the vector field that is applied to the images.

variant data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default data type for variables that don't have type-declaration characters when a Deftype statement isn't in effect. A Variant can store numeric, string, date/time, Null, or Empty data.

signed - unverified.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Content has been hashed but could not be verified as valid against the signature.

rolling upgrade.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a cluster, the process of systematically upgrading cluster nodes one node at a time while the other nodes continue to provide service.

cell spacing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The distance between the cells of a table or workbook.

inhibit.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To prevent an occurrence. For example, to inhibit interrupts from an external device means to prevent the external device from sending any interrupts.

stacked column chart.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A column chart subtype that shows the relationship of individual items to the whole, comparing the contribution of each value to a total across categories.

home cell.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the four card locations in the upper-right corner of the screen.

header source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A document that contains the header row (or header record) to be used with the data source specified for a mail-merge main document.

no-bar fraction.translation: phân số không vạch phân cách
no-bar fraction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A fraction that is written vertically with the numerator on top and denominator below, with no fraction bar between them.

graphical user interface.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A display format, like that of Windows, that represents a program's functions with graphic images such as buttons and icons. GUIs enable a user to perform operations and make choices by pointing and clicking with a mouse.

gui.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A display format, like that of Windows, that represents a program's functions with graphic images such as buttons and icons. GUIs enable a user to perform operations and make choices by pointing and clicking with a mouse.

visual interface.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A display format, like that of Windows, that represents a program's functions with graphic images such as buttons and icons. GUIs enable a user to perform operations and make choices by pointing and clicking with a mouse.

mail nickname.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The portion of the email address that appears to the left of the @ symbol.

animated gif.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A series of graphic images in GIF format, displayed sequentially in a single location to give the appearance of a moving picture.

attached document.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An ASCII text file or a binary file, such as a document created in a word processing system, that is included with an email message as an attachment.

help viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The tool or window that contains the Help content.

print area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One or more ranges of cells that you designate to print when you don't want to print the entire worksheet. If a worksheet includes a print area, only the print area is printed.

by default.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: How a program's action is determined if the user does not make a choice or supply a required value.

call forwarding on.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The menu item that displays a menu of options that the user can select to turn on the automatic forwarding of incoming calls.

error detection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technique for detecting when data is lost during transmission. This allows the software to recover lost data by notifying the transmitting computer that it needs to retransmit the data.

billfold.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A paper size of 95.25mm x 171.45 mm.

decision support system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of programs and related data designed to help with analysis and decision making. network monitor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A packet capture and analysis tool used to view network traffic.

microsoft network monitor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A packet capture and analysis tool used to view network traffic.

bound column.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The column in a list box, combo box, or drop-down list box that's bound to the field specified by the control's ControlSource property.

alef lam.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Analogous to the English word "the." Can be ignored when sorting text in tables in several Microsoft Office programs when enabled for right-to-left features.

enhanced screentip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A new type of ScreenTip that is larger and can contain more detailed information, including graphics.

semantic model definition language.translation: Ngôn ngữ Định nghĩa Mô hình Ngữ nghĩa
semantic model definition language.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of instructions that describe layout and query information for reports created in Report Builder.

poison-message queue.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subqueue of the application queue where poison messages get moved to be later processed by a poison-message handling application.

lowercase.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or characterized by non-capital letters.

processing instructions.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Information stored in the prologue of an XML document. This information is passed through the XML parser to any application that uses the XML document.

web part description file.translation: Tệp tin mô tả Phần Web

availability.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A condition of a user that can be displayed to the user's contacts to communicate whether the user is currently online and available, offline and unavailable, and so on.

contact information.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Information, such as name, phone number, email address, or address, that is used to contact someone.

microsoft® office forms server 2007 cal.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft client access license (CAL) for Microsoft Office Forms Server 2007.

microsoft® office outlook® web access.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Web application that provides secure access to email, personal calendar, group scheduling, and collaboration applications on Microsoft Exchange Server with only a Web browser.

remote desktop protocol.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The proprietary protocol to provide remote display and input capabilities over network connections for Windows-based applications between two computers.

rdp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The proprietary protocol to provide remote display and input capabilities over network connections for Windows-based applications between two computers.

simple object access protocol.translation: Giao thức Truy nhập Đối tượng Đơn giản
simple object access protocol.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A simple, XML-based protocol for exchanging structured data and type information on the World Wide Web. The protocol is currently the de facto standard for XML messaging.

soap.translation: Giao thức Truy nhập Đối tượng Đơn giản
soap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A simple, XML-based protocol for exchanging structured data and type information on the World Wide Web. The protocol is currently the de facto standard for XML messaging.

conditional.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of an action or operation that takes place based on whether or not a certain condition is true.

form template library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The location, in the top-level site of a site collection, where the form templates that have been activated by an administrator are stored.

agile methodology.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any of a family of processes that software developers use to minimize risk by developing applications incrementally, over a series of short iterations. In this model, real-time communications, such as in person conversations and telephone calls, are preferred over written documentation; the primary measure of progress is working software, instead of hours spent, tasks completed, documents reviewed, or phases signed-off; stakeholders are expected to collaborate, instead of negotiating; and planning happens continuously in order to respond to change.

client application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Application software that gathers data from the user, prepares it for the server, and issues a request to the server. The client presents data received from the server to the user through its own user interface.

calendar item.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item in the Exchange store that represents an appointment, a meeting, a meeting request, or an event. It can identify the place, resources, recurrence, and attendees involved at a discrete time.

linking table.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A table that has associations with two other tables, and is used indirectly as an association between those two tables.

alef hamza.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A single Arabic character that represents the two-character combination Alef plus Hamza.

web-based application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software program that uses Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) for its core communication protocol and that delivers Web-based information to the user in the Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) language.

web-enabled application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software program that uses Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) for its core communication protocol and that delivers Web-based information to the user in the Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) language.

named entity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A code that's used in HTML to describe symbols, international letters, and other special characters. Character entities are maintained by the International Standards Organization (ISO).

character entity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A code that's used in HTML to describe symbols, international letters, and other special characters. Character entities are maintained by the International Standards Organization (ISO).

best bet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Content or links that an administrator associates with specific keywords, and that are displayed prominently in search results when a query contains one of those keywords.

allow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The permission setting that permits a person or domain to add the user to contact lists, see the user's status, or send instant messages to the user.

resample.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Changing the pixel dimensions (and therefore the physical file size) of a picture or a graphic. Graphics can be resampled down (the number of pixels decreased) or resampled up (the number of pixels increased).

page template.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A predesigned, generic web page you can use to create new custom pages. Some of the page templates in FrontPage provide typical page content, while others provide common page layouts.

null key.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A null value that is encountered in a key column.

computer administrator.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The person in charge of managing a computer. The administrator is responsible for installing software, assigning passwords, and managing files.

speaker fill.rule: Microsoft Terminology. orphan file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file that remains on a system after it has ceased to be of use.

font style.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The stylistic attributes of a font — such as bold, italic, and underline.

rubber-banding.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In computer graphics, changing the shape of an object made up of connected lines by "grabbing" a point on an anchored line and "pulling" it to the new location.

video conversation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An instant message conversation in which one or both participants is broadcasting a video feed by using a camera.

nvarchar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The variable-length data type with a maximum of 4,000 Unicode characters.

redirect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To take action to deflect a phone call after the phone rings but before the call is answered.

cd sleeve.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A case for holding CDs.

line editor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A text-editing program that numbers each line of text, working with the document on a line-by-line rather than on a word-by-word basis.

allow list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A list of users, accounts, Web sites, etc. that are permitted to perform certain actions on a network.

key management service.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An optional Microsoft Exchange 2000 Server component that is installed on a designated server in an administrative group. metadata cache.translation: bộ đệm ẩn siêu dữ liệu

content master.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A slide template that defines default formatting or the position of placeholders for one or more slides in a presentation.

cost center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An operating unit whose managers are accountable for budgeted and actual expenditures.

attendee.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A meeting participant who cannot initiate desktop or application sharing or presenting and whose permissions are controlled by the organizer and presenters.

partnership.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of rules on a computer and a portable device that allow digital media files and other information to be synchronized.

stolen page.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A page in Buffer Cache taken for other server requests

image file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file containing graphics (illustrations, photographs, etc.) or other visual information.

powerpoint previewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A context menu that enables the user to preview the contents of a file with the Office Preview Handler (OPH) in Outlook (either documents attached to email or SharePoint documents in Outlook).

purge.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To eliminate old or unneeded information systematically.

paper source.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The location (such as Upper Paper Tray or Envelope Feeder) of the paper at the printer.

focusable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to anything (e.g. elements) that can receive focus.

push button.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standard system control that initiates a command.

spotlight site.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A listing or document selected as the best recommendation in the Site Directory.

assumption.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Baseline data that apply throughout a business or to a financial model.

internet protocol version 6.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A revised version of the Internet Protocol (IP) designed primarily to address growth on the Internet. IPng is compatible with, but an evolutionary successor to, the current version of IP, IPv4 (IP version 4), and was approved as a draft standard in 1998 by the IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force). It offers several improvements over IPv4 including a quadrupled IP address size (from 32 bits to 128 bits), expanded routing capabilities, simplified header formats, improved support for options, and support for quality of service, authentication, and privacy.

ipv6.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A revised version of the Internet Protocol (IP) designed primarily to address growth on the Internet. IPng is compatible with, but an evolutionary successor to, the current version of IP, IPv4 (IP version 4), and was approved as a draft standard in 1998 by the IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force). It offers several improvements over IPv4 including a quadrupled IP address size (from 32 bits to 128 bits), expanded routing capabilities, simplified header formats, improved support for options, and support for quality of service, authentication, and privacy.

smtp connector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software component that represents a logical path between a source and a destination for the purpose of transmitting Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) messages. A SMTP connector can be configured as a Send connector or as a Receive connector.

sign-in name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ID that the user enters to sign in to Lync or Communicator.

voice command.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A spoken command that controls a program or computer operation through speech recognition technology.

binary large object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A discrete packet of binary data that has an exceptionally large size, such as pictures or audio tracks stored as digital data, or any variable or table column large enough to hold such values. The designation "binary large object" typically refers to a packet of data that is stored in a database and is treated as a sequence of uninterpreted bytes.

blob.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A discrete packet of binary data that has an exceptionally large size, such as pictures or audio tracks stored as digital data, or any variable or table column large enough to hold such values. The designation "binary large object" typically refers to a packet of data that is stored in a database and is treated as a sequence of uninterpreted bytes.

to-do item.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A personal or work-related project, assignment, or errand to be tracked through to completion.

dialog box.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A secondary window that allows users to perform a command, asks users a question, or provides users with information or progress feedback.

cell range.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A block of two or more cells in a spreadsheet.

trace logging.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A means of capturing highly detailed information about the PerformancePoint Server system when problems occur.

report item.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Entity on a report.

unbalanced hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hierarchy in which one or more levels do not contain members in one or more branches of the hierarchy.

ragged hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hierarchy in which one or more levels do not contain members in one or more branches of the hierarchy.

multidimensional structure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database paradigm that treats data as cubes that contain dimensions and measures in cells.

hanging quotation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Giant quotation marks used to frame a pull quote.

folder hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A bounded namespace that uniquely identifies all reports, folders, shared data source items, and resources that are stored in and managed by a report server.

dynamic cursor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cursor that can reflect data modifications made to the underlying data while the cursor is open.

fps.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of video frames displayed per second. Higher frame rates generally produce smoother movement in the picture.

frame rate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of video frames displayed per second. Higher frame rates generally produce smoother movement in the picture.

frames per second.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The number of video frames displayed per second. Higher frame rates generally produce smoother movement in the picture.

accumulated depreciation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The sum of posted depreciations for all the periods in which a fixed asset has been in service.

security configuration wizard.translation: SCW (viết tắt của Bảng cài đặt cấu hình bảo mật)
security configuration wizard.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool that automates security best practices to reduce the attack surface for a server. The SCW was introduced with Windows Server 2003 Service Pack 1.

scw.translation: SCW (viết tắt của Bảng cài đặt cấu hình bảo mật)
scw.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool that automates security best practices to reduce the attack surface for a server. The SCW was introduced with Windows Server 2003 Service Pack 1.

file mapping.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The association of a file's contents with a portion of the virtual address space of a process.

multi-hosting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ability of a Web server to support more than one Internet address and more than one home page.

multihosting.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ability of a Web server to support more than one Internet address and more than one home page.

multihoming.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The ability of a Web server to support more than one Internet address and more than one home page.

shape client.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The recognizer specific part of the shape trainer. Typically every recognizer claiming to support shape personalization must supply a Shape Client DLL. All the Microsoft Latin recognizers will all use the same Shape Client.

autoflow.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The automatic flowing of text from one frame to another.

check mark.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small x or other sign that appears in the check box if the option represented by the box is selected.

ods library.translation: thư viện Dịch vụ Dữ liệu Mở
ods library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of C functions that makes an application a server. ODS library calls respond to requests from a client in a client/server network. Also manages the communication and data between the client and the server. ODS library follows the tabular data stream (TDS) protocol.

open data services library.translation: thư viện Dịch vụ Dữ liệu Mở
open data services library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of C functions that makes an application a server. ODS library calls respond to requests from a client in a client/server network. Also manages the communication and data between the client and the server. ODS library follows the tabular data stream (TDS) protocol.

yes/no data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A field data type you use for fields that will contain only one of two values, such as Yes or No and True or False. Null values are not allowed.

style inspector.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A floating task pane that allows users to view and customize specific paragraph and text style properties.

html file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file format that can be viewed using a Web browser. With this file format, you can publish your reports directly to your Intranet or web site.

remote service binding.translation: liên kết dịch vụ từ xa
remote service binding.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Service Broker object that specifies the local security credentials for a remote service.

language interface pack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Add-in software that provides partially localized user interfaces for particular computer programs in languages not supported by localized versions of those programs.

lip.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Add-in software that provides partially localized user interfaces for particular computer programs in languages not supported by localized versions of those programs.

independent software vendor.translation: nhà cung cấp phần mềm độc lập
independent software vendor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A third-party software developer which may include an individual or an organization that independently creates computer software.

isv.translation: nhà cung cấp phần mềm độc lập
isv.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A third-party software developer which may include an individual or an organization that independently creates computer software.

recursive partitioning.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The iterative process, used by data mining algorithm providers, of dividing data into groups until no more useful groups can be found.

cluster adapter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The adapter that, when using multiple network adapters in each host of a Network Load Balancing cluster, handles the network traffic for cluster operations (the traffic for all hosts in the cluster). This adapter is programmed with the host's cluster IP address.

session cookie.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cookie that is deleted at the end of the browser session.

public folder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A folder on a public server that people can use to share information, such as work information, discussions, contacts, tasks, and classified ads. Access permissions determine who can view and alter the folder and to what extent.

distribution server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server running Windows Media Services that publishes content received from another streaming source, such as an encoder or another Windows Media server.

system requirements.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A minimum hardware configuration of a computer (typically relates to CPU speed and type, size of RAM, free space on hard disk, and presence of other devices such as sound card, CD-ROM, etc.) needed to run a software program on it.

minimum system requirements.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A minimum hardware configuration of a computer (typically relates to CPU speed and type, size of RAM, free space on hard disk, and presence of other devices such as sound card, CD-ROM, etc.) needed to run a software program on it.

home plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A drawing that shows the layout of a house. It can be used to draw new house plans or remodeling plans, kitchen and furniture arrangements, or plans to add a new room to your home. A type of building plan.

ip address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A binary number that uniquely identifies a host (computer) connected to the Internet to other Internet hosts, for the purposes of communication through the transfer of packets.

internet protocol address.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A binary number that uniquely identifies a host (computer) connected to the Internet to other Internet hosts, for the purposes of communication through the transfer of packets.

cold boot.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A startup process that begins with turning on the computer's power. Typically, a cold boot involves some basic hardware checking by the system, after which the operating system is loaded from disk into memory.

cold start.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A startup process that begins with turning on the computer's power. Typically, a cold boot involves some basic hardware checking by the system, after which the operating system is loaded from disk into memory.

shell.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The command interpreter that is used to pass commands to the operating system.

client-side image map.translation: ánh xạ ảnh phía máy khách
client-side image map.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An image map that directly encodes in a Web page the destination URL of each hot spot in that image map. Client-side image maps do not require processing from a server when a site visitor follows the hyperlinks in the image map.

apartment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group of one or more COM objects in a process. A COM object lives in exactly one apartment, in the sense that its methods can legally be directly called only by a thread that belongs to that apartment. Any other thread that wants to call the object must go through a proxy.

top-fold card.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One of the page size options available in Publisher for printing a folded card. This option prints four pages per sheet of paper, with fold on top.

server error.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A failure to complete a request for information through HTTP that results from an error at the server rather than an error by the client or the user. Server errors are indicated by HTTP status codes beginning with 5.

subentry.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An index entry that falls under a more general heading. For example, the index entry "planets" could have the subentries "Mars" and "Venus."

sample.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subset of a population to represent the characteristics of the entire population being studied.

data series.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Related data points that are plotted in a chart. Each data series in a chart has a unique color or pattern and is represented in the chart legend. You can plot one or more data series in a chart. Pie charts have only one data series.

series.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Related data points that are plotted in a chart. Each data series in a chart has a unique color or pattern and is represented in the chart legend. You can plot one or more data series in a chart. Pie charts have only one data series.

page layout view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view of a document as it will appear on the printed page.

print layout view.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A view of a document as it will appear on the printed page.

analogous colors.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Colors that are directly next to each other on the color wheel. Each color has two analogous colors (one on each side of it).

application pool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A grouping of one or more URLs served by a worker process.

web pool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A grouping of one or more URLs served by a worker process.

balanced hierarchy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A dimension hierarchy in which all leaf nodes are the same distance from the root node.

leaf level.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The bottom level of a clustered or nonclustered index, or the bottom level of a hierarchy.

model dependency.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A relationship between two or more models in which one model is dependent on the information of another model.

screen font.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A typeface designed for display on a computer monitor screen. A screen font often has an accompanying PostScript font for printing to PostScript-compatible printers.

incoming conversation alert.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A notification that the user receives when someone is sending an invitation to the user to begin a conversation in Lync or Communicator.

space explorer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window that displays a list of all the spaces in the drawing and all the resources associated with each space.

high performance file system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A fixed-disk file system that organizes the disk into volumes, rather than partitions and logical drives. HPFS supports long, mixed-case filenames and extended attributes, and implements several levels of caching, for improved operating-system performance. The IBM OS/2 operating system supports HPFS.

high-performance file system.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A fixed-disk file system that organizes the disk into volumes, rather than partitions and logical drives. HPFS supports long, mixed-case filenames and extended attributes, and implements several levels of caching, for improved operating-system performance. The IBM OS/2 operating system supports HPFS.

hpfs.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A fixed-disk file system that organizes the disk into volumes, rather than partitions and logical drives. HPFS supports long, mixed-case filenames and extended attributes, and implements several levels of caching, for improved operating-system performance. The IBM OS/2 operating system supports HPFS.

adornment.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control or status area that is attached to the edge of a pane or window, such as a toolbar or ruler.

e-mail drop folder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A disk directory in which an SMTP service can deposit incoming mail messages.

drop directory.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A disk directory in which an SMTP service can deposit incoming mail messages.

asset library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A library that provides content types with common properties and enhanced views to find and preview digital assets.

repeating group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A group in the data source that can occur more than once. Controls such as repeating sections and repeating tables are bound to repeating groups.

qualifier.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A modifier containing information that describes a class, instance, property, method, or parameter. Qualifiers are defined by the Common Information Model (CIM), by the CIM Object Manager, and by developers.

deadly embrace.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In operating systems and database applications, a situation in which two or more processes cannot continue because each process is waiting for resources to be freed by the continuation of the other process.

defragmentation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of rewriting parts of a file to contiguous sectors on a hard disk to increase the speed of access and retrieval.

gutter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The blank area between two or more columns of text or between two facing pages in a publication.

plot area.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a 2-D chart, the area bounded by the axes, including all data series. In a 3-D chart, the area bounded by the axes, including the data series, category names, tick-mark labels, and axis titles.

applet.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A small piece of code that can be transported over the Internet and executed on the recipient's machine. The term is especially used to refer to such programs as they are embedded in line as objects in HTML documents on the World Wide Web.

outlook integration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Connectivity between Lync or Office Communicator, and Outlook where Lync or Office Communicator receives data from Outlook to make the functions of Lync or Office Communicator work.

windows xps viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The app that allows users to visualize, navigate, and customize the view of files with an XPS document format.

xml paper specification viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The app that allows users to visualize, navigate, and customize the view of files with an XPS document format.

xps viewer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The app that allows users to visualize, navigate, and customize the view of files with an XPS document format.

parent account.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An account that is above other accounts in the hierarchy to which any action taken on the main account entity can propagate to.

selection net tool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A tool that defines a rectangular area that encloses all the shapes to be selected.

liability.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A monetary debt or obligation of future services.

command syntax.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The order in which the user must type a command-line command or utility name and any arguments and options that follow it.

command-line syntax.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The order in which the user must type a command-line command or utility name and any arguments and options that follow it.

microsoft® office sharepoint® server 200.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft server product that creates a portal Web site that allows users to share documents and search for information across the organization and enterprise within one extensible portal interface.

windows integrated security.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A security mode that leverages the Windows authentication process.

integrated security.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A security mode that leverages the Windows authentication process.

address list.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of recipient and other Active Directory objects. Each address list can contain one or more types of objects (for example, users, contacts, groups, public folders, conferencing, and other resources).

remote installation server.translation: Máy chủ Cài đặt Từ xa
remote installation server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An optional component that remotely installs Windows XP Professional. RIS installs the operating system on remote boot-enabled client computers by connecting the computer to the network, starting the client computer, logging on with a valid user account, and copying an operating system image to the client computer.

downsample.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To decrease the number of audio samples or pixels, by applying an operation such as averaging. Popular internet music formats, such as MP3, use down-sampling to reduce file size.

territory.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The area in the country/region where an account is located.

secondary calendar.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The alternate calendar that is selected from within Outlook. The secondary calendar appears when dual calendar support is enabled.

software upgrade.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A software package that replaces an existing version of a product or a feature with a newer and/or more powerful or sophisticated version of the same product or feature. The upgrade process typically leaves existing customer data and preferences intact while replacing the existing software with the newer version.

locked.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The condition of a field, record, recordset, or database that makes it read-only to all users except the user currently modifying it.

syntax.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The rules governing the formation of a command-line statement, including the order in which a command must be typed, and the elements that follow the command.

make-table query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query (SQL statement) that creates a new table and then creates records (rows) in it by copying records from an existing table.

make table query.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A query (SQL statement) that creates a new table and then creates records (rows) in it by copying records from an existing table.

submission queue.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A persistent queue that is used to hold messages that are submitted to the Exchange Server organization through SMTP-receive, the Pickup directory, or the store driver.

buffer storage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An area of storage that is used to hold data to be passed between devices that are not synchronized or have different bit transfer rates.

domain integrity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The validity of entries for a specific column of data.

client access server role.translation: quyền máy chủ cho phép Máy khách Truy cập
client access server role.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of components and services that enable users to access their Exchange mailboxes through the application Outlook Web Access and the protocols Exchange ActiveSync, Post Office Protocol version 3 (POP3), and Internet Message Access Protocol 4rev1 (IMAP4). The Client Access server role also includes Web services that are used by other Exchange 2007 server roles.

sic.translation: Hệ thống Phân ngành Kinh doanh Tiêu chuẩn
sic.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Classification system developed by U.S. government to classify businesses based on their industry.

standard industrial classification.translation: Hệ thống Phân ngành Kinh doanh Tiêu chuẩn
standard industrial classification.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Classification system developed by U.S. government to classify businesses based on their industry.

north american industry classification s.translation: Hệ thống Phân ngành Kinh doanh Tiêu chuẩn
north american industry classification s.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Classification system developed by U.S. government to classify businesses based on their industry.

naics.translation: Hệ thống Phân ngành Kinh doanh Tiêu chuẩn
naics.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Classification system developed by U.S. government to classify businesses based on their industry.

microsoft® office publisher 2007.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft business desktop publishing program that enables users to create marketing materials by providing built-in professional design expertise and enhanced automation tools.

advertisement.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A message placed in a mass medium (and usually paid for by the advertiser) to persuade targeted customers or prospects.

data outline.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A window that you can display when a data access page is open in Design view.

sa.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A combination of identifiers, which together define Internet Protocol security (IPsec), that protects communication between sender and receiver.

security association.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A combination of identifiers, which together define Internet Protocol security (IPsec), that protects communication between sender and receiver.

source database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database on the Publisher from which data and database objects are marked for replication as part of a publication that is propagated to Subscribers. For a database view, the database on which the view is created.

shipping label.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A label that is printed with a recipient's address and is used to mail or ship an item.

mailing label.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A label that is printed with a recipient's address and is used to mail or ship an item.

license management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of the Windows Media Rights Manager software development kit (SDK) that enables consumers to back up the licenses for their Windows Media files and restore them to the same computer or to different computers. The restoration process is managed by Microsoft License Management Service, which limits the number of times a license can be restored to prevent fraud.

record locking.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A technique employed in distributed processing and other multiuser situations to prevent more than one user at a time from writing data to a record.

outlook item.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The basic element that holds information in Outlook (similar to a file in other programs). Items include email messages, appointments, contacts, tasks, journal entries, notes, posted items, and documents.

storefront.translation: mặt tiền cửa hàng trên web
storefront.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A business that displays its merchandise on the Internet and has provisions for contact or online sales.

web storefront.translation: mặt tiền cửa hàng trên web
web storefront.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A business that displays its merchandise on the Internet and has provisions for contact or online sales.

electronic storefront.translation: mặt tiền cửa hàng trên web
electronic storefront.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A business that displays its merchandise on the Internet and has provisions for contact or online sales.

online storefront.translation: mặt tiền cửa hàng trên web
online storefront.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A business that displays its merchandise on the Internet and has provisions for contact or online sales.

performance counter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of components that allow you to track the performance of an application.

up and running.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In operation; operating, working.

sql_variant.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A data type that stores values of several data types, except for text, ntext, image, timestamp, and sql_variant types. It is used in a column, parameter, variable, or return value of a user-defined function.

drop cap.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A large capital letter at the beginning of a text block that occupies the vertical depth of two or more lines of regular text.

main document.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a mail-merge operation, the document that contains the text and graphics that are the same for each version of the merged document, for example, the return address or salutation in a form letter.

roll forward.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: To apply logged changes to the data in a roll forward set to bring the data forward in time.

file format.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The structure or organization of data in a file.

windows installer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of Windows that defines and manages a standard format for application setup and installation, and tracks components such as groups of files, registry entries, and shortcuts.

msi.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature of Windows that defines and manages a standard format for application setup and installation, and tracks components such as groups of files, registry entries, and shortcuts.

enum.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of named integral constants.

enumeration.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of named integral constants.

list builder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An online service for your marketing campaign that allows you to acquire and manage email lists, and to track the results.

microsoft list builder.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An online service for your marketing campaign that allows you to acquire and manage email lists, and to track the results.

grace period.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The time period during which a product or service will remain functional before the user or customer must license, register, renew, or otherwise (re)activate their product or subscription.

grace time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The time period during which a product or service will remain functional before the user or customer must license, register, renew, or otherwise (re)activate their product or subscription.

lorg.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An organization with more than 1000 employees and more than 500 personal computers.

large organization.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An organization with more than 1000 employees and more than 500 personal computers.

hidden text.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Text that does not display in the normal view of a document's content.

new group.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The default name for a group of contacts created by the user.

attachment previewing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that allows users to see and interact with E-mail messages and their attachments side by side in the reading pane.

securable.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An entity that can be secured with permissions. The most prominent securables are servers and databases, but discrete permissions can be set at a much finer level.

cleartype.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A font display technology that dramatically improves font display resolution so that letters on the computer screen appear smooth, not jagged. ClearType dramatically improves the readability of text on color LCD monitors with a digital interface, such as those found in laptops and high-quality flat-panel desktop displays.

microsoft office interconnect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The program that enables users to send and receive business card information digitally and shares data storage with Outlook.

continuous form.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A form that displays more than one record on the screen in Form view.

cost increase.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A calculated field that subtracts the total budgeted cost from the total actual cost and then divides that value by the total budgeted cost. This value is then multiplied by 100.

bootstrapper.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that is run automatically when a computer is turned on or booted.

boot loader.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that is run automatically when a computer is turned on or booted.

bootstrap loader.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that is run automatically when a computer is turned on or booted.

user-defined aggregate function.translation: hàm tập hợp do người dùng xác định
user-defined aggregate function.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An aggregate function created against a SQL Server assembly whose implementation is defined in an assembly created in the .NET Frameworks common language runtime.

microsoft® office project server 2007 ca.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Microsoft client access license (CAL) for Microsoft Office Project Server 2007.

basic authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An HTTP authentication protocol that encodes but does not encrypt username and password.

plaintext authentication.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An HTTP authentication protocol that encodes but does not encrypt username and password.

transaction log backup.translation: sao lưu nhật ký giao dịch
transaction log backup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A backup of transaction logs that includes all log records not backed up in previous log backups. Log backups are required under the full and bulk-logged recovery models and are unavailable under the simple recovery model.

log backup.translation: sao lưu nhật ký giao dịch
log backup.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A backup of transaction logs that includes all log records not backed up in previous log backups. Log backups are required under the full and bulk-logged recovery models and are unavailable under the simple recovery model.

sparse file.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A file that is handled in a way that requires much less disk space than would otherwise be needed. Sparse support allows an application to create very large files without committing disk space for those regions of the file that contain only zeros. For example, you can use sparse support to work with a 42-GB file in which you need to write data only to the first 64 KB (the rest of the file is zeroed).

xml tree.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A hierarchical structure of XML elements.

nonbreaking space.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A space that is used to prevent multiple words from breaking if they fall at the end of a line.

operations master.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A domain controller that has been assigned one or more special roles in an Active Directory domain.

data compaction.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A process for removing redundant data from a digital media file or stream to reduce its size or the bandwidth used.
