input set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of data provided to a Multidimensional Expressions (MDX) value expression upon which the expression operates.

static cursor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A cursor that shows the result set exactly as it was at the time the cursor was opened.

typewriter.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A title animation in Windows Movie Maker.

service program.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program that uses Service Broker functionality. A service program may be a Transact-SQL stored procedure, a SQLCLR stored procedure, or an external program.

automatic update.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A method that allows a computer to be scanned and recommends software updates that fix problems, add functionality, or provide the latest drivers.

security breach.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An event that compromises the security of a computer, application, network or other resource.

breach.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An event that compromises the security of a computer, application, network or other resource.

depth of field.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The measurement of the area in front of and behind the subject that is in focus.

stencil.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of masters associated with a particular Visio drawing type, or template. By default, stencils that open with a template are docked on the left side of the drawing window.

long data type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A fundamental data type that holds large integers. A Long variable is stored as a 32-bit number ranging in value from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647.

odbc resource dispenser.translation: Bộ phân phối tài nguyên ODBC
odbc resource dispenser.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A DLL that manages pools of database connections for COM+ components that use the standard open database connectivity (ODBC) programming interfaces.

autocomplete.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The feature in Internet Explorer that remembers the information you have typed into the Address bar, web forms, or password fields, and which automatically fills in that information if you start to type the same thing again later.

technical preview.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pre-released version of a product that is sent to customers and partners for evaluation and feedback.

beta product.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A pre-released version of a product that is sent to customers and partners for evaluation and feedback.

data processing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The manipulation of data to transform it into some desired result.

application name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The unique and friendly name that refers to an application.

dsn-less connection.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A type of data connection that is created based on information in a data source name (DSN), but is stored as part of a project or application.

form properties.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Attributes of a form that affect its appearance or behavior. For example, the DefaultView property is a form property that determines whether a form will automatically open in Form view or Datasheet view.

field results.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Text or graphics inserted in a document when Microsoft Word carries out a field's instructions. When you print the document or hide field codes, the field results replace the field codes.

award certificate.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A document presented to an individual or team in formal recognition of their effort or achievement.

precedence constraint.translation: ràng buộc thứ tự ưu tiên
precedence constraint.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A control flow element that connects tasks and containers into a sequenced workflow.

left-aligned.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to text that is aligned along the left margin.

windows user name.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A unique name that identifies a user account to operating system. An account's user name must be unique among the other group names and user names within its own domain or workgroup.

group filter control.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A drop-down list box control on a data access page that retrieves records from an underlying recordset based on the value you select from the list. On a grouped page, the control retrieves a specific group of records.

photo cd.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphics file format developed by Eastman Kodak Company.

pcd.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A graphics file format developed by Eastman Kodak Company.

delivery extension.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A plug-in that delivers reports to a specific target (for example, email delivery).

user-defined object.translation: đối tượng do người dùng xác định
user-defined object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A custom object defined by the user.

alias type.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user-defined data type based on one of the SQL Server system data types that can specify a certain data type, length, and nullability.

office genuine advantage.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program for licensed Office software that provides access to updates, value-added downloads, free software trials, and special promotions.

oga.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A program for licensed Office software that provides access to updates, value-added downloads, free software trials, and special promotions.

function library.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of routines compiled together.

overdue.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An account status indicating that payments are late or not yet received.

server collation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The collation for an instance of SQL Server.

file share.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A directory or folder made available to users over the network.

smart quotes.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In word processors, a function that automatically converts the ditto marks ( " ) produced by most computer keyboards to the inverted commas used in typeset text.

microsoft® office project standard 2007.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An edition of Microsoft project management software used to plan, manage, and communicate a project schedule and other information among workgroup members, project managers, and other stakeholders.

ragged left.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Of, relating to, or being lines of text whose left ends are not vertically aligned but form an irregular edge. Text may be right-justified and have a ragged left margin. Ragged-left text is used infrequently-typically, for visual effect in advertisements.

boot partition.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The partition that contains the Windows operating system and its support files. The boot partition can be, but does not have to be, the same as the system partition.

data plan.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A standardized service agreement between a user and a mobile operator that establishes data service details such as pricing, types of services, and bandwidth.

file sharing.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The use of computer files on networks, wherein files are stored on a central computer or a server and are requested, reviewed, and modified by more than one individual. When a file is used with different programs or different computers, file sharing can require conversion to a mutually acceptable format. When a single file is shared by many people, access can be regulated through such means as password protection, security clearances, or file locking to prohibit changes to a file by more than one person at a time.

break mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A temporary suspension of program execution while in the development environment. In break mode, you can examine, debug, reset, step through, or continue program execution.

base line.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In the printing and display of characters on the screen, an imaginary horizontal line with which the base of each character, excluding descenders, is aligned.

content management.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The collection, storing, and sharing of information in a single system where many users can access it.

heartbeat interval.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time that can elapse before the Exchange server asks a mobile device running Exchange ActiveSync to connect again.

marketing automation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A subset of customer relationship management (CRM) that focuses on the definition, scheduling, segmentation and tracking of marketing campaigns.

ole db.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component database architecture that provides efficient network and Internet access to many types of data sources, including relational data, mail files, flat files, and spreadsheets. OLE DB comprises a specialized set of COM interfaces that expose data from a variety of data stores, both relational and nonrelational.

object linking and embedding database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component database architecture that provides efficient network and Internet access to many types of data sources, including relational data, mail files, flat files, and spreadsheets. OLE DB comprises a specialized set of COM interfaces that expose data from a variety of data stores, both relational and nonrelational.

oledb.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A component database architecture that provides efficient network and Internet access to many types of data sources, including relational data, mail files, flat files, and spreadsheets. OLE DB comprises a specialized set of COM interfaces that expose data from a variety of data stores, both relational and nonrelational.

local distributor.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A server that is configured as both a Publisher and a Distributor for SQL Server Replication.

add time stamp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A button in the Comments section that the user can click to add a date or time stamp.

business process.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A specified sequence of steps required to complete a complex task, such as creating a contract. A business process can be performed manually or through the use of a workflow rule.

font substitution.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A substitution that occurs when Windows or your printer uses a font similar to the one you used in your publication to display or print your publication.

headphone virtualization mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An audio effect setting that allows users with stereo headphones to experience stereo and multi-channel content without the need to set up an extensive multi-channel speaker system.

virtualization mode.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An audio effect setting that allows users with stereo headphones to experience stereo and multi-channel content without the need to set up an extensive multi-channel speaker system.

file as printout.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A command that will use a print driver installed by OneNote to create an image of a wide variety of filetypes. Files are printed to the print driver and inserted as images into OneNote.

cluster-aware application.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An application that can run on a cluster node and that can be managed as a cluster resource. Cluster-aware applications use the Cluster API to receive status and notification information from the server cluster.

system event.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An event triggered by Windows system components that is recorded in the system log, such as the failure of a driver or other system component to load during startup.

ordered set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of members returned in a specific order.

nonleaf member.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A member with one or more descendants.

computer-aided design.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A system of programs and workstations used in designing engineering, architectural, and scientific models ranging from simple tools to buildings, aircraft, integrated circuits, and molecules.

brand image.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A company's or partner's logo, fonts, and color themes or schemes intended to visually signify who and what the company is.

brand identity.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A company's or partner's logo, fonts, and color themes or schemes intended to visually signify who and what the company is.

free media pool.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A logical collection of unused data-storage media that can be used by applications or other media pools. When media are no longer needed by an application, they are returned to a free media pool so that they can be used again.

solutions to problems.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An item on the Control Panel.

audit history.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Information maintained about the history of an item, including all reading and editing sessions.

hosted.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Pertaining to an application on Microsoft Dynamics Live CRM and partner-hosted versions of Microsoft Dynamics CRM. Deployments where the Microsoft Dynamics CRM server is maintained for an organization by a third-party, such as Microsoft or a partner.

keyboard layout.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The key arrangement used for a particular keyboard, including such factors as the number of keys (101 is the current standard) and the configuration of the keys (QWERTY is the United States standard). Some proprietary systems use different layouts, and many allow you to map the keys to characters according to your preferences.

color profile.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A profile that contains the data needed for translating the values of a color gamut. This data includes information about color, hue, saturation, and brightness.

markup overlay.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Translucent shapes, ink shapes, or comments that are superimposed over a drawing without changing the underlying drawing.

transition effect.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An animation effect that specifies how the display changes as a user moves from one item (such as a slide or Web page) to another.

compile time.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The amount of time required to perform a compilation of a program. Compile time can range from a fraction of a second to many hours, depending on the size and complexity of the program, the speed of the compiler, and the performance of the hardware.

single language pack.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of language resources that supports the deployment of a software program in a particular language.

slp.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of language resources that supports the deployment of a software program in a particular language.

dimension level.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A set of members in a dimension hierarchy such that all members of the set are at the same distance from the root of the hierarchy. For example, a time hierarchy may contain the levels Year, Month, and Day.

report server database.translation: cơ sở dữ liệu máy chủ báo cáo
report server database.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A database that provides internal storage for a report server.

welcome center.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature that serves as a launching point for several optional Windows tasks and OEM-defined tasks.

running head.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One or more identifying lines printed at the top of a page. A header may contain a page number, a date, the author's name, and the document title, the name of chapter.

page header.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: One or more identifying lines printed at the top of a page. A header may contain a page number, a date, the author's name, and the document title, the name of chapter.

sql server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A complete platform for data management, business analytics and intelligent apps that can be used in a consistent way across both on-premises and the cloud, and runs on Windows, Windows server and Linux.

microsoft sql server.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A complete platform for data management, business analytics and intelligent apps that can be used in a consistent way across both on-premises and the cloud, and runs on Windows, Windows server and Linux.

boot drive.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: In a PC-compatible computer, the disk drive that the BIOS uses to automatically load the operating system when the computer is turned on.

look up.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The UI element that initiates the process of seeking a particular file or specific data. A search is carried out by a program through comparison or calculation to determine whether a match to some pattern exists or whether some other criteria have been met.

recurrence pattern.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The regular pattern according to which a scheduled appointment or task is repeated.

application pane.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A discrete area of a split or single window in which an application user interface is rendered.

tree structure.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Any structure that has the essential organizational properties of a tree.

account domain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows NT domain that holds user account data.

master user domain.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A Windows NT domain that holds user account data.

always on top.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A user interface element that causes the application window to always be displayed over other open windows on the computer, even when it does not have focus.

roll forward set.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The set of all data restored by a restore sequence. A roll forward set is defined by restoring a series of one or more data backups.

indentation.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: Displacement of the left or right edge of a block of text in relation to the margin or to other blocks of text.

inline object.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A picture or other object placed within a line of text that retains its place next to adjacent text when text is added or deleted.

command buffer.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: An area in memory in which commands entered by the user are kept. A command buffer can enable the user to repeat commands without retyping them completely, edit past commands to change some argument or correct a mistake, undo commands, or obtain a list of past commands.

coarse-grained lock.translation: khóa toàn bộ cấu trúc dữ liệu
coarse-grained lock.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A lock that applies to a large amount of code or data.

proofing tools.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A collection of tools such as a spelling checker, grammar checker, and thesaurus.

authoring.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: The process of creating and designing content or software program by using specialized authoring tools.

bcc.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature in email programs that allows a user to send a copy of an email message to a recipient without notifying other recipients that this was done.

blind carbon copy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature in email programs that allows a user to send a copy of an email message to a recipient without notifying other recipients that this was done.

blind courtesy copy.rule: Microsoft Terminology. Definition: A feature in email programs that allows a user to send a copy of an email message to a recipient without notifying other recipients that this was done.

spring boot.rule: Là tên framework, tuyệt đối giữ nguyên không dịch.

dependency injection.rule: Chủ yếu dịch là 'Tiêm phụ thuộc', nhưng có thể kèm thuật ngữ gốc trong ngoặc.
